title: fix(check): flush the explainer receipt before exiting so a piped stdout is not truncated
body:
Fixes #1130.

## Problem

On macOS `process.stdout` is asynchronous when it is a pipe. The explainer branch of `archify/scripts/check-render-output.mjs` printed its receipt with `console.log` and called `process.exit()` on the next line, so any receipt larger than one pipe chunk (about 8 KiB) was cut mid-JSON. `deliver` and `finalize` spawn the checker with a piped stdout and then fail with `delivery/receipt-invalid` ("Could not parse the successful artifact-check receipt: Unterminated fractional number in JSON") even though the artifact passed every check.

The diagram path at the bottom of the same script already avoids this by setting `process.exitCode` and letting the process drain; only the explainer branch still exited eagerly.

## Change

One file, `archify/scripts/check-render-output.mjs`, explainer branch only:

- write the receipt with `process.stdout.write` and call `process.exit(code)` from the write callback, after the data has flushed;
- hold the module with a never-resolving top-level `await` so execution does not fall through into the diagram path and print a second receipt.

No change to the receipt shape, exit codes, or the diagram path.

## Evidence

Reproduced with a 7-panel explainer (architecture + workflow + 2 erd; receipt 21,289 bytes) on macOS 26.3 / Node 22:

| | `check <html> --json \| wc -c` | `finalize explainer` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 8192 (ends at `"minimumProjectedTextPx": 6.7510971786`) | `deliver = fail` · `delivery/receipt-invalid` |
| after | 21289 · `JSON.parse` ok · `ok: true` | `validate · deliver · check = pass` |

`node --test test/output-path.test.mjs`: 40 pass, 0 fail.

Opened as a draft per CONTRIBUTING (defect fix awaiting maintainer agreement on #1130). A regression test would need an explainer fixture whose receipt exceeds one pipe chunk; happy to add one in the shape maintainers prefer.

title: fix(qa): finish bounded keyboard traversal across native scroll stops
body:
## Problem and behavior

A page with native scroll regions or dynamic SourceCard links can require more key presses than its initial control count. The current QA cutoff stops early and reports reachable footer controls as missing. This change freezes the initial target identities and continues real Tab/radio-arrow traversal until all initial targets are reached, a supported no-progress cycle is detected, or bounded work is exhausted.

The existing research branch is refreshed onto dev `500d4a65211ffe607fde6b3ce7505027b45bb59e`, retaining its SVG-block extraction fixes. Only the keyboard checker, its focused regressions, the canonical ZIP and experiment evidence differ from dev. Reader HTML, layout and focus order are unchanged. Scope comes from the maintainer's [ongoing research task and actual-artifact validation](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/4671df2c578925f4c70a7ec7abd68ada93a0d472/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/keyboard-current-artifacts.md).

## Boundaries and cost

Success still requires real keyboard arrival at every initial target. Hiding/removing a target or cloning its QA key cannot make it pass. Real traps and exhausted budgets remain failures. Work is bounded by initial target count + min(initial DOM elements, 1024) + 3 actions; this cost belongs to browser QA, with no new Reader dependency. The cycle check is a conservative heuristic, not a universal accessibility proof.

Scoped test-value review retained decisive scroller/SourceCard positives and identity/trap/budget negatives. No new generic focus model or frame/shadow recursion was added. Generation benchmarks do not apply: this change checks fixed HTML and does not change diagram generation.

## Verification

[Current-base reproduction and selected evidence](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/f9fc38cbc19f5bb2725fd54d957e182831eb1eb9/experiments/keyboard-traversal/refresh-dev-500d) use official Node 22.23.2 and its canonical bundled zlib:

- At tested merge `48eaf689`, render-output checks plus the Explainer caller tests: 96 passed, zero failed/skipped. Core smoke: 19 passed, zero failed/skipped. Final `f9fc38cb` adds evidence only.
- Two canonical ZIP builds and the committed ZIP are byte-identical (`712de2a5db70e88ba6cbab82b2810978da6ac4afc74ac61eecf2471499de4cf9`). All 235 entry names match current dev; only the keyboard checker entry differs. Both packed checkers equal combined source.
- Independent review verified ancestry, unchanged candidate behavior, actual logs, all recorded raw-file hashes and ZIP entries. The only base-sync conflict was the generated ZIP, rebuilt from combined source.

[Earlier browser and CLI evidence](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/9601c9b6e4b6addc2f348677d1c198bc6bc74192/experiments/keyboard-traversal/refresh-dev-e837) retains tested merge `49413625`: the full real-Chrome Explainer browser file passed 19/19; public CLI browser-check on the authentic-provenance Trace HTML reached 27/27 in 33 actions across four arms, with unchanged HTML; extracted-package native scroller passed and true trap failed. These paths, the browser orchestrator, wrapper, renderer, dependencies and build script are unchanged by the latest base update. The changed static checker and its Explainer caller have the new local coverage above. This is reused evidence, not a fresh browser run.

Earlier direct-API checks on Task/Trace/OCI retain their original revision: 40/40, 27/27, 29/29 across four arms. Historical baseline 16/12/16 diagnostics remain recorded. Raw logs remain local; committed summaries include hashes and disclosed gaps, including no pre-run hash of the original delivery receipt.

Hosted CI for final head `f9fc38cbc19f5bb2725fd54d957e182831eb1eb9` is complete: 19 checks succeeded and two deployment jobs were skipped ([run 40431526745](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40431526745), attempt 2). Attempt 1 failed on the shared 1396×480 compact Sequence case; the WebM aggregate reflected browser failure while decoding succeeded. After the workflow completed, only the failed browser job was requested for rerun and its dependent aggregate followed; other successes retain attempt-1 execution. The [original failure and source-level diagnosis](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/255828331107d1c794f03a74e0695c425182c477/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/keyboard-current-ci-diagnosis.md) remain recorded. Matching earlier #1121 geometry and a passing rerun do not establish root cause or a repaired layout defect. The previous head `9601c9b6` completed 19 checks with two deployment skips ([historical run](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40427641788)); those results are not relabeled as this head's CI. No human acceptance, AT support, all dynamic-control coverage or reading-speed claim.

## Actual image

This existing Trace observation shows real Tab reaching the footer on the same frozen HTML. It is reused at its original identity, not a visual redesign or a new screenshot from the refreshed checker. [Capture binding and original observation](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/9f9f9dacf58832f1c8784a1a24f6e04c456a4881/experiments/trace-flow-evidence/root-review/README.json).

![Actual Tab reaches the footer on unchanged HTML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/9f9f9dacf58832f1c8784a1a24f6e04c456a4881/experiments/trace-flow-evidence/root-review/footer-tab.png)

## AI assistance and accountability

Codex/GPT-6.1-Sol reviewed the algorithm, scope and evidence; GPT-6.1-Terra refreshed the isolated tree and ran scoped checks. Accountable maintainer: @tt-a1i. Existing attribution and license notices are preserved.

- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them.

Draft for review only; no merge, release, deployment or live installation.

title: experiment: explain OCI whiteouts and same-layer visibility
body:
## 问题与结果

上层 tar 的新增文件先于 opaque marker 出现，是否会被随后出现的标记删掉？这个固定内容实验用两份原创小 tar、完整成员清单和同一张原生图说明：普通 whiteout 隐藏下层指定目标，opaque 隐藏下层子项，同层新增文件保留。

实际测量只包含 tar bytes、成员顺序、类型与 payload 摘要；可见文件是固定 OCI 规范推导，页面首屏即说明这一区别。没有运行容器、mount、解压程序或上游工具，没有声称 OCI 兼容或磁盘回收收益。dive/container-diff 提供阅读问题，行为依据使用固定 OCI layer 规范，来源与完整许可均保留。

仅新增 `experiments/oci-whiteouts/**`，复用现有图与 Explainer；不改共享 Viewer、schema、依赖或旧实验。Nix 共享闭包方向因与 retained-size 重叠而排除，此处只讨论 changeset 的可见性。

## 证据与限制

- 7 项 Python stdlib 检查通过，独立 Agent 在 `2db99eb8` 重跑：完整 inventory、标记语义、同层保留、全部 6 种成员顺序、错误输入和已有输出保护。排列检查是规范模型，不是 6 次容器运行。
- 原生图 finalize 四阶段通过；Explainer validate/deliver/check 通过。额外严格浏览器门禁 **失败，16 条 keyboard-traversal 诊断**；首稿 authored schema/Markdown 错误与修正记录保留。
- Root 实际查看 1440×900 明暗和390×844明暗、打开交互图、Escape 返回焦点。真实 Tab 到达 inventory/order copy 32–33、两条来源34–35和页脚36；保留原观察，不用它覆盖自动失败或替代真人无障碍验收。
- test-value / focused simplification：固定两层小模型，不写通用 tar importer/unpacker；图与说明共用一个原生 JSON。原始生成空白与源文件检查分别记录。

[固定 README、复现命令与来源](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/5f37aaa707567a4004317cad12fc4c02cb2f27b6/experiments/oci-whiteouts/README.md)。基线 `e837dc4c`；最后提交只补 root 浏览器观察、图片及文档，产物字节未变。远程 CI 在创建本 Draft 时尚无结论。Draft 供审查内容方向的价值与限制，尚无用户阅读收益或人工验收结论。

![实际解释页首屏](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/5f37aaa707567a4004317cad12fc4c02cb2f27b6/experiments/oci-whiteouts/root-review/final-light.png)

title: experiment: read authored behavior paths with explicit test associations
body:
## Problem and value

The existing task-review-map explains changed nodes and accounts for Git hunks, but its generic node list does not say which authored behavior step is associated with which test source. This experiment adds a small sidecar projection over the unchanged, hash-pinned mapping: a missing-artifact path with a test association, a delivered path without declared associations, and a clearly labelled synthetic omission contrast.

Scope was authorized by the maintainer's resumed research task and [deduplicated against the existing 49 experiments and open work](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/codex/research-lab-20261026/docs/research/2026-10-26). Inspired by task-view's Flow view; no Git adapter, upstream renderer or new product schema is copied. [Reproduce and inspect](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/843c877b251baf89925f99e11594fc5630c1c165/experiments/task-flow-tests/README.md).

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI: Codex / GPT-6.1-Sol agents for source research, implementation, tests, independent review and actual browser inspection.
- Accountable maintainer: @tt-a1i. Proposed reading improvement over fixed historical public code; flow and test associations are authored statements.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them.

## Stability impact

Only `experiments/task-flow-tests/` changes. The fixed mapping is reused byte-for-byte from `dcedd53856b82d3e403a9651dca0e15840496942`. No historical tests or task-view code were executed. The page keeps reference agreement, declared test association and test execution separate. Unknown/duplicate references are rejected. No shared Viewer, CLI, schema, package or installation change.

Scoped test-value/maintenance review retained a small projector and decisive identity, association, allowed-input and output-protection tests. The real-generation benchmark pilot is not applicable: this is a bounded projection/content experiment, not a generation-pipeline change. No comprehension-speed improvement is claimed.

## Tests run

Base `e837dc4cb83042d2b6c596e039692e25ec62c2da`; implementation `0d5f46834bbe8e631b6c20d2acc81c206583812d`; head `843c877b251baf89925f99e11594fc5630c1c165` adds browser evidence only.

- 9 focused tests pass, including a single-path/zero-association case that exposed and now prevents an incorrect fixed summary.
- Finalize: validate/deliver/check pass with 0 diagnostics; default Explainer browser-check not requested.
- Separate strict-provenance visual-check: containment/readability/chrome/theme/captures pass, but overall **fails with 16 keyboard-traversal diagnostics** across four states. Exact failure, initial and revised drafts, and an intermediate test failure remain recorded.
- Root actual browser: step navigation, regression source link, light/dark desktop and 390px viewport inspected. Actual Tab traversal reached all three footer source links and the Archify link at steps 44–47. This is separate evidence; the automated failure is not relabelled as passed. No assistive-technology claim.
- Independent review passed the final semantic/identity/maintenance scope. Remote CI is recorded separately in the dated follow-up below.

## Visual evidence

Final artifact SHA256 `f8c908b1d9e4e2eccf127387d886eba425aa06106448fbd212eac931f6f4b17b`. Actual screenshots at 1440×900; the 390px image and full keyboard sequence are in [root-review](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/843c877b251baf89925f99e11594fc5630c1c165/experiments/task-flow-tests/root-review). Agent visual inspection confirms the linked-test state is visible; the mobile diagram is a small preview with an explicit open-diagram affordance and long code scrolls locally. Human acceptance remains pending.

![Path and test association](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/843c877b251baf89925f99e11594fc5630c1c165/experiments/task-flow-tests/root-review/overview-light.png)

![Associated test source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/843c877b251baf89925f99e11594fc5630c1c165/experiments/task-flow-tests/root-review/test-source.png)

## Generated artifacts

Only isolated experiment HTML, JSON, screenshots and portable evidence summaries. Shared Viewer/ZIP inputs are unchanged. Original and second-draft outputs preserve their own evidence identities. Source and license attribution distinguish task-view's MIT root from vendored EPL-2.0 materials; no vendor code is reused.


## CI follow-up · 2026-10-27

精确 head 的初次 browser-regression (2) 失败于共享 Sequence 的 1396×480 短视口 containment。第一次单 job 重跑请求因 workflow 尚未结束而返回 `job cannot be rerun`。随后 webm-decode 成功结束；webm-artifact 当次失败来自 browser 依赖汇总，没有第二个解码错误。

workflow 完成后，单独请求重跑该 browser job。相同 head 的 attempt 2 于 00:31:02 UTC 成功结束；当前检查为 19 success、2 deployment skipped。仅失败 browser job 及其依赖汇总重新执行，其他成功 job 保留原执行时间。

原始失败和本地 Reader Layout 18/18 通过仍保留；重跑通过没有确定首次失败根因。未修改共享代码或启动全套新 run。[首次只读诊断](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/c0903e6efd3daf40dba3b5703839b358c6138fc1/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/task-flow-ci-diagnosis.md) · [重跑记录](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/c0903e6efd3daf40dba3b5703839b358c6138fc1/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/task-flow-ci-rerun.md) · [最终检查快照](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/c0903e6efd3daf40dba3b5703839b358c6138fc1/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/task-flow-ci-attempt2.json)。

title: 在语义护照中只读展示节点的任务清单（Task checklist）
body: ## 问题与价值 - 相关 issue：实现 #1114，维护者已同意直接提 PR。 - 当前基线上的实际问题、预期结果，以及为什么值得长期维护： - 实际问题：在当前基线 `dev`（`e837dc4c`）上，节点虽支持已验证的 `sources` 和说明文字 `explanation`（#398），但无法表达逐条任务的状态和验收标准；开发进度只能散落在图外，编码智能体汇报的进度也无法对照代码核实。 - 预期结果：本 PR 支持在 `architecture`、`workflow`、`sequence`、`dataflow` 和 `lifecycle` 五种图的节点上，可选配置只读的 `task_checklist` 并在语义护照中展示，任务证据按固定提交校验。任务状态是作者（或智能体）的声明：固定提交的源码引用只证明引用的文件和行存在，不证明任务已经实现，Archify 也不判断代码是否满足验收标准。 - 为什么值得长期维护：实现方式与 `explanation` 一致，直接复用现有的仓库证据校验器，不引入任何新的运行时、状态存储或外部依赖。 - 体积代价：每张单图 HTML 增加 6,717 字节，`archify.zip` 增加 36,807 字节（0.53%）。 - 改动前后的证据入口：见下文“测试”与“视觉证据”。 ## AI 辅助与贡献者责任 - AI 使用：实现、调查、测试与审查辅助。 - 工具与模型及辅助范围：使用 Claude Code（Claude Opus 5.5）辅助代码库调查、方案比较、实现、测试、审查、生成物重建和本说明的起草；前身的个人原型（Archify-List）使用了 Codex 和 Cursor。 - 负责的贡献者：@Silencentury - 问题来源：改进提议（来自个人原型：和编码智能体一起开发时，用 Archify 图跟踪实现进度）。 - [x] 本人已审阅提交的代码与说明，理解其影响，并能回答相关问题；验证结果与缺口已记录在下文。 ## 稳定性影响 - 影响等级、行为变化和共享调用方：契约变更（五种图的节点新增一个可选 Schema 字段，另有 Skill 说明），同时涉及共享行为： - Schema：`common.schema.json` 新增 `$defs/taskChecklist`，支持 1–12 条任务；`title` 为 1–120 个字符，`status` 取值为 `implemented`、`needs-review` 或 `pending`，可选字段为 `criteria`（1–280 个字符）和 `sources`；已实现的任务必须带证据，待实现的任务不能带。 - 仓库证据：`verifyRepositoryEvidence` 采用与节点证据相同的检查和诊断逻辑来校验任务证据，校验结果新增可选的 `taskChecklists` 映射，交付回执的 `evidence.references` 也同步计入任务证据。Story 工具和 `archify/explainer/sources.mjs` 不读任务清单，不受影响。 - 页面渲染：只有写了任务清单的文档才在 SVG 之外输出 `archify-task-checklists-data` JSON 块，新的模板占位符也仅在此时才必需，现有自定义模板不受影响。`focus.js` 将源码链接的渲染提取为辅助函数 `sourceLink()`，供节点证据和任务共用，节点证据的 DOM 结构不变；#1055 的浅色主题覆盖规则加入了“已实现”标记。 - 多语言与文档：六种语言目录各新增五条文案；`SKILL.md` 说明何时编写 `task_checklist`、它与 Explainer 读者待办清单的区别，并写明状态是作者声明、源码引用只证明文件和行存在。 - simplify-codebase（聚焦）：任务证据通过 `citationGroups()` 复用节点证据的校验循环，源码链接直接复用上述 `sourceLink()`，未另写一套；未发现其他值得删减的地方。 - 保持不变的行为、有意的兼容性变化和失败时的表现： - 保持不变的行为：规范的 SVG、PNG 和 WebM 导出不含清单内容；所有重新生成的页面里，图表 SVG 与基线逐字节相同；节点证据的校验逻辑不变。 - 有意的兼容性变化：见上文 Schema 与页面渲染两条；另外 `source-required` 的修复建议补充了任务证据说明。 - 失败时的表现：不符合上述规则的清单由 Schema 直接拒绝；无法校验的任务证据（包括缺少 `meta.repository`）会让 `validate`、`render` 和 `deliver` 失败并给出仓库证据诊断；自定义模板缺少占位符时会明确报错。 ## 测试 对比基线 `500d4a65`（`dev`），候选提交 `6979ce89`。由智能体在本地运行（环境：macOS arm64，官方 Node 22.23.2 / zlib 1.3.1-e00f703，Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.47）： - 新增测试： - `test/passport-task-checklist.test.mjs`：覆盖五种图上的 Schema 规则、SVG 之外的 JSON 块与 `zh-CN` 界面文案，以及任务证据的校验与失败路径（缺文件、缺 `meta.repository`）。 - `test/passport-task-checklist-browser.test.mjs`（真实浏览器）：验证折叠的计数行、点击展开和 Enter 收起、状态标记的无障碍名称、已验证的源码链接，以及规范 SVG 不含任务内容；同时验证底部节点的长清单在图区内滚动，且聚焦下一个节点时自动恢复折叠。另有一个按审查意见补充的 320×300 测试：同一节点同时带返回上层链接、接近上限的 explanation 和 12 条带链接的任务，验证键盘能逐个到达任务链接且自动滚入视野、展开收起、说明面板的返回、护照的关闭、关闭后返回上层按钮可点，以及重新聚焦或切换节点后从折叠开始。 - `test/reader-text-contrast.test.mjs`：增加一条接线断言。 - test-value（测试有效性）：Schema 规则在进程内直接校验，命令行的失败退出已有 `repository-evidence` 的用例覆盖。“只有任务证据、没写 `meta.repository`”这条边界和浅色覆盖的接线断言均做过故障注入：撤掉对应改动后，测试如期失败。 - 测试结果： - `npm run test:full`（在 `6979ce89` 上，未设置 `ARCHIFY_CHROME`）：通过。68 项生成物检查通过；3,661 个测试中 3,526 个通过、0 个失败、135 个跳过（其中 122 个需要真实浏览器）。 - 真实浏览器（在 `678d21d6` 上，之后只合并了上游的检查器修复和重建的 `archify.zip`）：单独运行 `test/passport-task-checklist-browser.test.mjs`，2 个测试均通过。完整的浏览器门禁和 `npm run test:webm` 交给 CI。 - MCO（沿用 `9786a5b7` 上的结果，之后没有改动渲染代码和生成页面）：设置 `ARCHIFY_MCO_REPO_ROOT`（`mco-org/mco@9f1a1cf1`）运行 `test/real-repository-proof.test.mjs`，3/3 通过。 - `archify finalize`（在 `6979ce89` 上；使用一张带三条任务、证据已验证的图）：`validate`、`deliver`、`check` 和 `browser-check` 全部通过，回执中的 `evidence.references` 为 2。 - 合并后用新的检查器对本 PR 改动的 62 个 HTML 文件运行 `archify check`：61 个通过；`experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html` 的 showcase 版式检查未通过，上游 `dev` 上的同一页面结果相同。 - 观察到的不稳定（与本改动无关）：第一次全量运行中，`output-path.test.mjs` 复制 `archify/` 时与并行的 `release-package-gates.test.mjs` 争用临时文件，报 `ENOENT`；单独重跑和第二次全量运行均通过。 - 真实仓库生成对比：未运行，建议豁免。原因：`task_checklist` 需要显式添加，新增的 Skill 段落只在用户要求展示实现进度时才适用，默认生成行为不变。 ## 视觉证据 - 提供的证据：深色、浅色主题截图各一张（附在本节末尾）。 - 对比条件：1440×900，设备像素比 1，减少动效，经典预设；在 `archify/examples/web-app.architecture.json` 的 `users` 节点上加三条任务（已实现和待复核任务带已验证证据，另有一条待实现），聚焦并展开。 - 自动或浏览器检查：见上文。对比度在 Chrome 中按合成后的护照背景测量：四个浅色预设下新增文字不低于 `4.54:1`，四个深色预设下不低于 `5.27:1`。复用的源码链接行号样式在经典浅色下为 `3.77:1`，属原有问题，本 PR 未改。 - 人工视觉审查：通过。 ## 生成物 - 随源码提交（`4f2a9bcd`）：`archify/assets/template.html` 和 `archify/renderers/shared/generated-validators.mjs`。 - 随生成物提交（`9786a5b7`，从最终源码重建了 66 个文件）： - 根目录和打包的示例各 15 个； - 5 个 drilldown 示例及其根目录副本； - `examples/ai-agent-n8n.html` 及两个 MCO 页面； - 画廊（`docs/gallery.html`、清单和 16 个页面）； - `examples/web-app.html`（没有生成脚本，按模板派生，`test/golden.mjs` 会检查）； - Checkout 对比示例及回执，以及 `archify.zip`。 - 说明：drilldown、n8n 和 MCO 这 13 个页面没有生成脚本，所用命令在基线上能逐字节重建仓库中的文件，因此 diff 里只有本 PR 的模板变化。 - 合并上游 `dev`（`500d4a65`，#1031 的检查器修复）时，`archify.zip` 是唯一冲突，已按规定工具链从合并后的源码重建（逐字节可复现），其中也包含本轮 `SKILL.md` 的措辞。 - README 动图回执：只更新了三个画廊页面的 `artifactSha256`，GIF 没有重录，做法同 `3b5b16c0`。 - 已重建且无变化的页面与历史快照：`docs/guide.html`、`docs/start.html` 重建后无变化。其余内嵌 Viewer 的历史快照（`docs/cases/` 下 6 个、`examples/` 下 4 个）保留在原来的版本，同 #398 和 #1055 的做法。

title: fix: hide classic grid in SVG exports
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

- Related issue / agreed discussion, or why this is a purely mechanical documentation correction:
  Fixes #1111. Note: This cleanly provides the scoped fix on top of `upstream/dev` (replacing the branch state in PR #1115), removing accidental inclusion of `main` commits and resolving all merge conflicts.
- Actual problem on the current base, intended outcome, and why it is worth maintaining:
  In standalone SVG exports, the classic preset grid rule was discarded by `serializeSvg` because its selector began with `html`:
  `html[data-preset="classic"] .diagram-container > svg .c-grid { stroke: transparent; }`
  As a result, standalone exported SVGs rendered a visible 40px background grid, whereas the live viewer and PNG exports hid it. Changing the selector to `svg[data-preset="classic"] .c-grid { stroke: transparent; }` allows it to pass the SVG serializer's selector filter (which permits `svg[...]`) and correctly hides the grid across all standalone SVG export variants (`svg`, `svg-light`, `svg-dark`).
- Before/after evidence entry point:
  Verified via automated CDP browser suite in `test/export-browser.test.mjs`.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, or review assistance
- Tools and model (if known), and assisted areas: Antigravity coding assistant; root-cause investigation, CSS selector fix, viewer template regeneration, and browser regression test authoring.
- Accountable contributor: @vedantb7
- Problem origin: observed usage reported in issue #1111
- [x] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: Local behavior / viewer CSS styling. Only affects `.c-grid` stroke for diagrams configured with `data-preset="classic"`.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: Live viewer appearance is identical. PNG exports remain unaffected. Non-classic presets (e.g., `blueprint`, `editorial`, `signal-flow`) are untouched and continue rendering their grids as designed.

## Tests run

- Comparison base: `upstream/dev` at `e837dc4cb83042d2b6c596e039692e25ec62c2da`
- Candidate head: `vedantb7/archify:fix/1111-classic-svg-grid-clean` at `04f5725515228189859f518e388d7ae19f56e9c9`

### Passing test commands and results:
1. `node scripts/generate-viewer.mjs --check`
   - Result: PASSED (exit code 0; generated viewer template matches source)
2. `node test/golden.mjs`
   - Result: PASSED (exit code 0; all 15 golden renders match; all schema and version sync checks pass)
3. `node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/animation.test.mjs test/preset-tryon.test.mjs test/generate-viewer.test.mjs`
   - Result: PASSED (333 tests passed, 0 failed)
4. `node scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs test/export-browser.test.mjs`
   - Result: PASSED (24 tests passed, 0 failed; specifically verified: `✔ classic preset hides background grid in viewer and exported standalone SVGs without affecting PNG (5124ms)`)
5. `git diff --check upstream/dev`

### Disclosed environmental gaps:
- `npm run test:core` and `check:brand-marks` were skipped due to uninstalled optional devDependencies (`parse5`, `simple-icons`) in the local environment, preserved without altering package manifests.

## Visual evidence

- Comparison conditions: Verified across light and dark themes using bundled lifecycle/architecture inputs.
- Automated or browser checks: Headless Chrome CDP suite verifies computed stroke of `.c-grid` is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` for classic SVGs and non-transparent (`rgba(...)`, opacity `0.78`) for blueprint SVGs.
- Perceptual visual review: passed

## Generated artifacts

## Problem and value

Fixes #1072. Public Workflow validation can fail to terminate for valid finite widths such as 1e30: adding the 12px port-probe spacing no longer changes representable coordinates.

## Scope

Based on inspected dev `10b4dd5c5f2264baa315ee65a9b4cc23c13ea5f0`. This isolates the progress guard and public-CLI regression from the unrelated #1070/#1071 fixes in the earlier fork commit. The canonical ZIP is rebuilt from this narrow source.

- Green: widths1e18,1e25,1e26,1e30 and ordinary320 complete through the public CLI, return structured receipts, preserve input bytes and write no HTML. Timeout cleanup owns the entire spawned process group.

title: perf(explainer): index outgoing shorthand edges
body:
## Problem and value

- Related issue / agreed discussion: Proposal issue #1107. This draft is for maintainer scope discussion; it is not requesting final review.
- Actual problem on the current base, intended outcome, and why it is worth maintaining: `rankedPlacement` rescanned all edges for each queued node, so sparse graph placement did work proportional to nodes × edges. A precomputed outgoing adjacency index reduces traversal to the graph's vertices and edges without changing output.
- Before/after evidence entry point: A warmed synthetic public-compiler comparison on Node v24.22.1 (2,000 nodes, 1,999 edges, 15 samples) measured 17.90 ms baseline median and 5.61 ms candidate median. Generated specs were deeply equal. This is a local synthetic compile measurement, not end-to-end authoring telemetry.

title: Improve workflow compilation performance
body:
## Problem and value

- Related issue / discussion: none; selected from a focused performance inspection.
- `laneTop()` recomputed preceding lane heights with `slice().reduce()` on every lookup, and `nodeStep()` used `findIndex()` for each node outside `mainPath`. Both repeat work as workflow size grows. This PR precomputes lane tops and first-occurrence node indexes once per compile.
- Before/after evidence: paired, alternating base `10b4dd5c` and candidate `3233ebcd` runs on Node v24.22.1 with a synthetic 2,000-lane/2,000-node workflow (10 samples per revision). Median compile time was 30.14 ms → 11.90 ms; p90 was 47.72 ms → 14.51 ms. Both produced a 2,323,000-byte SVG with the same SHA-256 (`6a93f25dbc5c4cb5ffc9641362329333eec26fb96817b2dcf79bfb9e28c03631`). This is a stress-case measurement, not a claim about typical workflows.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: investigation, implementation, benchmark, and tests.
- Tools and model (if known): Copilot App (Auto mode; concrete model not identified), git, Node.js.
- Accountable contributor: @cookingwithvlad-del
- Problem origin: code inspection and a synthetic compiler benchmark.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared workflow compiler geometry/indexing; applies to workflow compilation.
- Existing behavior preserved: lane-top prefix arithmetic and first matching node index are retained; the stress fixture's emitted SVG is byte-identical. No schema, layout, or authored behavior is intentionally changed.
- Real-repository generation matrix: not run. This is an output-preserving compiler optimization with no intended change to agent authoring, repair, or diagram quality; the direct compiler benchmark and existing workflow behavior tests are the relevant evidence.

## Tests run

- Base: `origin/dev` at `10b4dd5c`; candidate: `3233ebcd`.
- `npm run test:focus -- test/workflow-compiler.test.mjs test/workflow-compiler-call-contract.test.mjs test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs test/workflow-automatic-width.test.mjs test/workflow-counterflow-spacing.test.mjs` — passed, 165 tests.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Synthetic paired benchmark and output digest comparison — details above; no browser or perceptual review was needed because rendered bytes are unchanged.

## Ten performance improvement candidates identified

1. **Selected in this PR:** cache workflow lane tops and node indexes instead of repeatedly reducing lane prefixes and searching all nodes.
2. Build workflow group/phase lookup structures for `nodeContext()` instead of scanning both collections for every node (`workflow-compiler.mjs`, `createWorkflowLaneGeometry`).
3. Reuse workflow edge-index maps where code repeatedly calls `workflow.edges.indexOf()` while assembling route/label diagnostics (`workflow-compiler.mjs`).
4. Build a reverse workflow source-index-to-edge lookup for the `routeFirst` pass instead of calling `workflow.edges.find()` (`workflow-compiler.mjs`, `validateReadablePinnedGeometry`).
5. Index authored workflow nodes for the repeated `document.nodes.find()` calls used while probing capacity repairs (`workflow-compiler.mjs`, `createLegacyCapacityRepair`).
6. Replace the shared legend's nested legend-rectangle/obstacle scans with a spatial candidate lookup (`shared/legend.mjs`, collision placement).
7. Build dataflow node-to-incident-flow adjacency once rather than filtering all flows for every node (`dataflow-compiler.mjs`, Showcase automatic layout).
8. Precompute dataflow flow indexes instead of repeatedly calling `indexOf()` while building route candidates (`dataflow-compiler.mjs`, label routing).
9. Index dataflow label rectangles by relation/index instead of repeated `find()`/`findIndex()` scans during label repair (`dataflow-compiler.mjs`).
10. Index previously placed waterfall rows by node ID instead of searching `placed` for every parent (`waterfall/render-waterfall.mjs`).

Items 2–10 are inspection candidates, not individually benchmarked or included in this change.

title: Add an Atlas view to Code Analysis
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

- Related issue / agreed discussion: none yet. Opened as a **draft** to discuss scope with a working implementation; per CONTRIBUTING.md this needs maintainer agreement before final review.
- Actual problem on the current base (`25b767c`): the Classic view reads a run against the authored architecture diagram, so its unit is the component. On a repository the author has not drawn yet, or one with many modules, the overall shape is hard to see: which modules are tangled, where complexity concentrates, where a cycle actually runs. On MyBatis 3 the overview lists 41 findings, but nothing shows that 18 of 21 modules sit in one cycle or that `executor` and `session` take part in more cross-module dependencies than any other module (270 and 212 of 749).
- Intended outcome: a second view, **Atlas**, that draws the analyzed tree itself at file and function level so problems are visible at a glance, while the Classic view stays the place to read source evidence. The Atlas links every finding back to it.
- Before/after evidence entry point: [Visual evidence](#visual-evidence) (MyBatis 3 and Apache Dubbo screenshots, how to read the Atlas, motion recording) and Tests run below. The base has no Atlas, so there is no before image; the Classic view is unchanged.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, documentation and this description.
- Tools and model: Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 — payload builder, canvas view, Classic hand-off, served-page loading, tests, docs.
- Accountable contributor: @yijiez666-alt
- Problem origin: proposed improvement.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared behavior (overlay page) plus a new view; no schema or rule change.
  - New `overlay/atlas.mjs`: `buildAtlas({ graph, facts, findings, review })` projects the run's raw facts, module graph and findings into compact arrays (files grouped by module, one entry per resolved file-to-file dependency, every measured function with its finding, each finding with the indices it selects). `ATLAS_CSS` / `ATLAS_JS` draw it on a `<canvas>`: module arcs, file ticks, bundled dependency curves, function spikes scaled to complexity, selected findings drawn on top, polar hit testing, theme-aware colours. Motion shows change only: a reveal from the centre on opening, a cross-fade on a new focus or finding, and a light travelling around a selected import cycle in import direction; off with `prefers-reduced-motion`. The graph is painted once into an off-screen frame and composited with the motion layer and the hover mark.
  - `overlay/inject.mjs`: embeds `#bauify-atlas-data` before the Classic script (which then offers an **Atlas** button in the reader) and the Atlas style/script after it; exposes `window.__archifyShowFinding(id)` so the Atlas opens a finding with its evidence in the Classic view.
  - `bin/serve.mjs`: the served page copies the Atlas parts when present, in document order; the three Classic parts remain required.
- Preserved: Classic view behavior, payload and wording are unchanged apart from the Atlas button; without raw facts no Atlas is embedded or offered. The Atlas adds no analysis and makes no claim the findings do not: unresolved dependency records draw no curve and the side panel states their count.
- Cost: the page embeds about 1.8 MB more for Apache Dubbo (2,427 files, 13,447 dependencies, 19,439 functions) next to the existing 15.9 MB payload; a full draw takes ~40 ms on MyBatis 3 and ~110 ms on Dubbo in headless Chrome.
- PR improvement check: test-value applied below. simplify-codebase: the Atlas reuses the Classic finding page for evidence instead of a second source viewer; finding titles are computed once in the payload.
- Open questions for scope: whether the Atlas belongs in this module branch now; whether a function call graph (not extracted today, so no function-to-function curves) should follow.

## Tests run

Base `25b767c` (`labs/code-analysis`), head `f0be206`. Agent-run, Linux, Node 22.23.4, Chrome.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| `node --test archify/modules/code-analysis/test/*.test.mjs` | 220/220 passed |
| `node --test test/core-smoke.test.mjs` | 19/19 passed |
| `ARCHIFY_CHROME=… node --test test/code-analysis*.test.mjs` | 11/11 passed |
| `node scripts/package-smoke.mjs <extracted zip>/archify` | passed (linux) |
| Manual: served view on MyBatis 3 (`0437d36`) and Apache Dubbo (shallow clone of default branch), light and dark theme | no page errors; Atlas → Classic evidence round trip works |

New tests (test-value):

- `test/atlas.test.mjs` (py-tasks fixture): every resolved in-tree file dependency drawn exactly once between the right files; files contiguous per module; every measured function kept with its measurements and reported ones pointing at their finding and back; import cycle path/files, module cycle modules and boundary imports map to the files and modules they name; a hub selects its module; accepted findings marked; no Atlas without raw facts; coverage counts every record once; unique shortest module labels; injection order. Discrimination checked by fault injection (reverted): dropping intra-module dependencies and breaking the function-to-finding link each fail their test.
- `test/code-analysis-browser.test.mjs`: opens the Atlas from the served page, checks it drew every dependency and painted the canvas, focuses a module from the side panel, selects a complex function, opens its evidence in the Classic view (source excerpt present), and checks that turning Code Analysis off closes the Atlas. It also checks motion: the opening reveal runs and finishes, a selected import cycle keeps changing the canvas, and with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` there is no cross-fade and nothing moves. Run 8 times in a row after fixing a frame-timestamp race found by this test (a requestAnimationFrame timestamp earlier than the start time sent the cycle light to index -1); all passed.

Not run: root `test:full`, Windows/macOS, Firefox/Safari, perceptual review by a human, phone-width layout beyond the CSS breakpoint. CI on this head pending at the time of writing.

## Visual evidence

Agent-captured in headless Chrome (1440×900, dark theme) on head `f0be206`, from the served view of two real repositories analyzed with `--language java`: MyBatis 3 at `0437d36` and Apache Dubbo at `843b98b` (shallow clone of the default branch). The diagram IR is a one-component placeholder, so the page title is only a label. Images are hosted on the `claude/code-atlas-evidence` branch (no product files; delete it once this PR is closed).

### How to read the Atlas

| On the circle | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Outer coloured arc | One module of the module graph; a thicker arc is a reported hub | `module-graph.json`, `coupling/hub` |
| Tick just inside an arc | One analyzed file of that module (test and generated files left out) | raw facts `files`, module graph `fileModules` |
| Curve inside the circle | One resolved dependency between two analyzed files, coloured by the importing module and bundled through both modules; hugging the rim = inside one module | raw facts `imports` (resolved, file to file) |
| Spike outside a tick | One measured function; length = cyclomatic complexity (capped at 26) | raw facts `functions` |
| Dot on a spike | A reported complex function, in its severity colour (amber warning, blue info) | `complexity/function` |
| Thick glowing curve | The selected finding: an import cycle's path, a boundary's crossing imports | `coupling/import-cycle`, `architecture/boundary` |
| Side panel | Selection, totals, findings by rule, complexity histogram, modules by coupling, dependency-record coverage, legend | same run |

Unresolved dependency records draw no curve, so a missing curve is not proof that there is no dependency; the side panel states how many there are (MyBatis: 14,652 resolved, 4,361 external, 456 unresolved of 19,469 records).

### MyBatis 3: whole repository

![Atlas overview of MyBatis 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-overview.png)

394 files in 21 modules, 1,337 file dependencies, 2,585 functions, 41 findings. Long spikes with dots mark the 27 reported complex functions; thick arcs mark the 7 hubs (`session`, `builder`, `executor`, `mapping`, `reflection`, `binding`, `type`).

### Focusing a module: `executor`

![executor focused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-focus-executor.png)

`executor` (55 files, 340 functions, fan-in 8, fan-out 12): pink curves are dependencies inside it and its 217 dependencies on other modules; light curves are the 53 dependencies of other modules on it. Everything else fades.

### Selecting a complex function

![DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-function.png)

`DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters(PreparedStatement)` in `scripting` (complexity 25, nesting 10, 93 lines, warning): its spike is ringed and the curves are its file's dependencies.

### Selecting an import cycle

![Import cycle selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-cycle.png)

A 6-file `logging` cycle drawn over the rest (path `LogFactory → Log4j2Impl → Log4j2AbstractLoggerImpl → back`). In the live page a light travels along it in import direction.

### Hand-off to the Classic view

![Classic view with source evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-classic.png)

**Open evidence in Classic view** closes the Atlas and opens the same finding with its captured source excerpt and AI task; the Atlas itself shows no source.

### Apache Dubbo: scale

![Atlas overview of Apache Dubbo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/dubbo-overview.png)

2,427 files in 81 modules, 13,447 file dependencies, 19,439 functions, 258 findings. Curve opacity scales down with the number of curves so strands stay readable; long module names are cut on the circle and shown whole on hover and in the side panel.

![dubbo-common focused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/dubbo-focus-common.png)

`dubbo-common` (457 files, 5,077 functions, fan-in 73, fan-out 0): no dependencies leave it, and the light curves are the 4,705 dependencies of other modules on it — the base layer of the codebase, visible at a glance.

### Motion

![Atlas motion on MyBatis 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/atlas-motion.gif)

Recorded at about 11 frames per second from CDP screenshots, so slower and choppier than the live page: the reveal on opening, the cross-fade to a focused module, and the light running around a selected import cycle. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` all three are off (covered by the browser test).

- Automated or browser checks: the browser test in Tests run (canvas painted, focus and selection state, motion and reduced motion, hand-off).
- Perceptual visual review: not performed by a human; the screenshots above are agent-captured.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip`: rebuilt with `scripts/build-zip.sh` on Node 22.23.4 / zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`; package smoke passed on the extracted archive.

title: 修复 Workflow 受限分叉导致的路由交付失败
body:
## 问题与价值

ref #1058 #1059

benchmark 第四题的退货流程中，拒绝分支与退款分支发生连线交叉，导致校验失败、无法交付。相同输入存在满足约束的路由，但原有搜索没有找到。

## 改动

- 常规路由失败后，按节点 ID 稳定选择最多四处分叉，尝试调整源端口顺序，并补充短端点绕行候选；通过完整校验后才接受。
- 每次调用该兜底逻辑最多额外编译四次；外层布局反馈独立运行，因此这不是全局四次尝试或总耗时上限。
- 保留原始节点、关系、标签和指定端口方向，已成功编译的流程沿用原有结果。
- 增加两个回归测试，覆盖第四题的交付恢复、输入不变及节点／关系数组重排。
- 同步产品包 `archify.zip`。

## 验证与生成基准证据入口

以下按 [真实仓库生成基准报告模板](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/d5d979493bba650b3995836afd379cd249f2d0dd/benchmarks/real-repo-generation/report-template.md) 整理本 PR 的缩小范围验证。

### 1. 结论与范围决定

本次证明第四题固定输入的交付恢复，以及既有 Workflow 的兼容性；不主张端到端生成性能提升。

沿用维护者明确要求的“第四题故障复现＋37 份既有 Workflow 回放”范围，依据 [首次范围约定](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/1086#issuecomment-6386651130)、[范围复核](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/1086#pullrequestreview-5660634284) 和 [本次集成复核](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/1086#pullrequestreview-5668081180)。这些回复明确要求沿用已有证据、限制本轮范围。

等效覆盖依据：原故障直接经过本 PR 修改的受限分叉路由路径；回归测试检查完整校验、输入／节点／关系／标签／指定端口方向保留，以及超过四处分叉时的稳定选择；37 份回放检查已有完整编译结果不变。这覆盖本次路由修复与兼容性，未覆盖 Agent 阅读五个真实仓库、首稿生成或修复轮数收益，因此不把本报告标为完整真实仓库生成基准。

### 2. 冻结版本与复现条件

| 证据 | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 原始 37 份回放及第四题证据包 | `82c7e0f089a02a4d514714adf37dc2061682da5f` | `83a109027936927cc65d212280ee1b6d28cabb38` |
| 本次最终集成 | dev `d5d979493bba650b3995836afd379cd249f2d0dd` | `81fee74310ebdc2d772d16f0841795e0ea09e39a` |

原始两侧 `archify` Git tree 分别为 `b9699a8157161aba4431d449fe4e6d7cb9d04adb`、`ff7927a613d5461f2eff5820265258de92f920fa`；本次两侧为 `68512d2a02679150487706929391ffeabe133289`、`997151116cbe0010bca94f73324341812f860454`。本次 ZIP SHA-256：`c1cbe9e6754d0554ec140b051348f9c6aff4408dc79326a03952ea647d73361c`。

相同输入字节、`showcase`、Node.js 22.23.3；本次 macOS／真实 Chrome。第四题输入 SHA-256：`8607fc7914f9f66da02cdad22ba8ec83b087f48a555c170e5f94835eb8a3e765`。本次工作区干净，保留 #1137 并从合并源码重建 ZIP；编译器及回归测试相对已审阅的 `ff27b7fc` 无变化。

### 3. 结果与命令

| 输入／检查 | Base 结果 | Candidate 结果 | 证据 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 第四题，同一 JSON | 因 `accepted` 与 `ineligible` 交叉导致 validate 失败，无交付 HTML | validate、deliver、严格 check、browser-check 通过 | 包内 `case4.*.compile.json`、finalize 回执及 HTML；本次同输入再次通过 |
| 37 份既有 Workflow | 完整编译输出 | SVG、receipt、diagnostics 逐项深比较一致 | 包内 `comparison.json`、`fixtures/`、`outputs/`，保留原提交标记 |
| 本次受影响测试 | — | 161 项通过，0 失败／跳过 | 下述 focused 命令；远端 CI 另列 |
| 生成物与 ZIP | — | 生成物检查通过；两次 ZIP 构建字节一致 | `npm run test:generated`、`scripts/build-zip.sh` 和 `cmp` |

```sh
# 原始证据重放，脚本与完整说明见证据包 README.md
node reproduce.mjs <base-root> <candidate-root> <output-dir>
# 本次最终 head
```

title: feat: add standalone artifact update notice
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #1064.

Forwarded standalone Archify HTML can show its generator version but had no explicit, bounded way for a reader to discover a newer stable version. This PR adds a quiet update notice to Native Viewer and Explainer artifacts. Both remain offline-first: no polling, telemetry, persistence, credentials, or automatic installation is introduced.

## Approach

- Emit a local identity payload containing artifact type, generator version, content digest, and the project-owned stable manifest URL.
- Show a keyboard-accessible version dialog. Only an explicit **Check for update** action requests that fixed manifest.
- Strictly validate the manifest before presenting a newer stable version. Development artifacts return before any request; malformed manifests, including calendar-invalid timestamps, report the generic unavailable result.
- Keep the readers aligned: Native Viewer and Explainer use the same externally observable update contract.

## Scope and impact

- This remains an update-only artifact slice. It does not add feedback submission, diagnostic copying, custom destinations, Issue routing, a new CI system, a renderer/schema rewrite, or delivery-receipt changes.
- Reader chrome is local to standalone HTML; canonical exports remain unchanged.
- The initial-load probe covers only the four instrumented JavaScript APIs: fetch, XHR, WebSocket, and EventSource. It does not claim to observe every browser network channel.

## Validation

- npm run test:generated — Viewer/validator freshness, release identity, schema enforcement, and root/package golden outputs.
- npm run test:core — core smoke suite.
- node --test --test-name-pattern "explainer reader update follows" test/reader-disclosure-browser.test.mjs — real Chromium coverage for Explainer: zero instrumented API calls for a development artifact, malformed and calendar-invalid manifests fail closed, and a valid manifest makes exactly one controlled fetch after explicit activation.
- node --test test/explainer-renderer.test.mjs test/reader-disclosure.test.mjs — renderer and disclosure contracts.
- git diff --check — whitespace validation.

The older overflowing reader-update.workflow fixture was removed and is not described as regenerated or repaired here.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation drafting, and test design.
- I reviewed the final diff, ran the listed local validation, and remain accountable for this PR.
- [ ] I have personally reviewed every line of code in this PR for correctness, security, and maintainability.

title: feat: GitHub Enterprise source links for repository evidence
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #1034.

A repository-backed diagram on a GitHub Enterprise host (GHE.com or a
self-managed GHES) cannot publish source links today. Web links are only built
for github.com, gitee.com and gitlab.com, or for a self-managed GitLab host
declared with `provider: "gitlab"` (#662). For any other host,
`provider: "github"` fails with `repository-evidence/provider-invalid`, so the
only way through is `link_mode: "local-only"`: verification still runs, but the
sources render as plain text instead of revision-pinned links.

GitHub Enterprise Server and GHE.com serve exactly the github.com URL layout
(`/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<rev>/<path>#L<a>-L<b>`, `/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<rev>`),
so no new link builder is needed — the declaration only has to be accepted, the
same way the accepted GitLab precedent accepts a declared self-managed host.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/shared/repository-location.mjs`
  - `parseRepositoryRemote` now honours a `provider: "github"` hint on a host
    that is not github.com, mirroring the existing `provider: "gitlab"` hint.
    A public host still selects its provider automatically, and a declared
    provider that disagrees with a public host still fails
    `repository-evidence/provider-invalid`.
  - The returned location gained `publicHost` (whether the host is one of the
    known public forge hosts), so callers do not have to repeat the host table.
- `archify/renderers/shared/repository-evidence.mjs`
  - The evidence label keeps the host name for a declared GitHub Enterprise
    host (`ghe.example.com/Platform/evidence-repo`) instead of abbreviating to
    an owner/repository path that would read as a github.com repository. The
    label is rendered into every artifact, so github.com, gitee.com,
    gitlab.com, self-managed GitLab and `local-only` keep byte-identical
    labels.
  - The `provider-invalid` and `links-unsupported` diagnostics and their
    `supportedFixes` now name the GitHub Enterprise option, and state the two
    conditions that still reject such a host: a GitHub-family path is
    `owner/repository` on the standard HTTPS port (only GitLab names nested
    groups).
- `archify/references/authoring-contract.md` and
  `archify/references/repository-authoring.md` — the declaration, the
  `owner/repository` rule, the `#L<a>-L<b>` anchor and the `provider: "github"`
  entry in the local-only identity paragraph.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — an `### Added` entry under `## [Unreleased]`.
- `test/repository-evidence.test.mjs` — two new tests mirroring the
  self-managed GitLab tests: the accepted host (HTTPS, Git SSH, SSH URL and a
  case-variant path all match one repository, with the github.com link layout)
  and the guards that still apply (no declaration, a provider that disagrees
  with a public host, plain HTTP, a nested path, a non-standard port, and
  origins on another host or port). The existing github.com, gitee.com,
  gitlab.com and self-managed GitLab tests now pin the label bytes.
- `archify.zip` — rebuilt with the canonical Node 22 toolchain; two builds are
  byte-identical (sha256
  `76a6fe5048f8769a1fcae75826757c2fec8d8a1865908a6277eb2cad48001bb6`).

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/repository-evidence.test.mjs` — 34 pass,
  0 fail, 1 pre-existing platform skip.
- Red proof: with the provider hint reverted, exactly the two new tests fail
  (`repository-evidence/provider-invalid`); the 32 pre-existing tests still
  pass. Restored, the file is green again.
- `npm run test:generated` — all checks pass (viewer, brand marks, generated
  validators, release identity, goldens).
- Full `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` run on this branch: 3141 pass, 44 fail.
  The same suite on the same tree with these changes stashed gives 3140 pass,
  43 fail, and the two failure sets are identical except for one
  load-sensitive update-notifier lease test that passes when it is re-run in
  isolation. The shared failures are pre-existing Windows-environment ones
  (symlink/EPERM, path separators) and do not touch repository evidence.
- Two independent reviews of the diff; the findings about the invalid example
  path, the contradicting paragraph, the missing changelog entry, the message
  wording, the missing negative cases and the duplicated host table were
  applied.

## Scope and limits

- The declaration is trusted exactly as the accepted GitLab precedent trusts
  it: Archify never contacts the host to detect its forge. A wrong
  declaration can only produce broken links; verification still runs against
  the local checkout, and a web link is only built for a revision, path and
  line range that were verified there.
- A GitHub-family repository path is `owner/repository`; nested groups remain
  GitLab-only, and a host on a non-standard HTTPS port still has no web links.
- The explainer still derives `link_mode: "local-only"` for an unrecognised
  origin, because it does not pass a provider hint — unchanged behaviour, the
  same gap the self-managed GitLab case has today. An explainer document that
  declares `meta.repository.provider` explicitly does get links.

## Refresh onto the current `dev`

- Rebased onto `dev` @ `7b4ebba9`; the only conflict was the packaged archive `archify.zip`, rebuilt from the merged tree with the canonical Node 22 toolchain (two builds, byte-identical, sha256 `76a6fe5048f8769a1fcae75826757c2fec8d8a1865908a6277eb2cad48001bb6`).
- New head `ade96ef7`. The focused suite and `npm run test:generated` are green on the refreshed branch.

title: feat(compare): read Architecture snapshots from Git refs
body:
## Summary

`compare architecture` can now read one repository-relative Architecture JSON snapshot from two local Git refs and reuse the existing Delta pipeline:

```text
--base-ref v1.0.0 ─┐
                   ├─ resolve commit → git cat-file blob snapshot → existing Delta
--head-ref v2.0.0 ─┘
```

The sidecar receipt records the requested refs, resolved 40-character commits, and snapshot path. Legacy `compare architecture base.json head.json` remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** users manually resolve two refs, extract two JSON files, keep their paths and commit identities, then run `compare architecture`.
- **After:** one command resolves both refs and reads the same committed snapshot path:

  ```bash
  node archify/bin/archify.mjs compare architecture \
    --repo-root /path/to/repository \
    --base-ref v1.0.0 --head-ref v2.0.0 \
    --snapshot docs/architecture.json \
    architecture-delta.html --json
  ```

- **Real case:** vLLM `v0.31.0` (`db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6`) → `v0.32.0` (`5df63a7203cdb9328d824a27b682e77c7b9928be`). The tags do not contain Archify JSON snapshots, so the issue records this as a follow-up code-to-snapshot case rather than claiming direct support.
- **Maintainer fixes:** Git subprocesses now remove inherited repository-selection variables, snapshots are read with `git cat-file blob`, and Git-mode output/receipt checks protect the committed snapshot path. Windows drive-absolute paths and incomplete Git options return structured diagnostics.
- **Focused evidence:** Architecture Delta suite 45/45; core smoke 19/19; generated checks and release identity pass locally on base `dev@f90a1930fec2822443d5db5d0d7e05bfdbe61267` and candidate `7184b99`. Coverage includes lightweight tags and commit refs, legacy JSON/Git-ref Delta equivalence, inherited Git selector isolation, no-fetch behavior against a configured unreachable remote, tree/invalid path failures, incomplete options, no-artifact failure behavior, worktree preservation, and receipt-overwrite protection with the output beside the snapshot.
- **Package evidence:** With canonical Node 22.23.2 and zlib 1.3.1, `scripts/build-zip.sh /tmp/archify-fresh-7184b99.zip` produced 221 files and `cmp -s` matched the checked-in `archify.zip`.
- **Full-suite evidence:** `npm run test:full` reached the full 3,390-test matrix; local execution was blocked by the sandbox's `listen EPERM` restriction in server-based tests. This environment limitation is separate from the compare suites; remote CI is the authoritative full-suite check.
- **Current CI note:** final-head run [#2747](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/39754108489) passes the compare-relevant full regression, browser, Windows, package, website, and ZIP checks. Only the existing Story/WebM audio decode job fails with FFmpeg's `Error parsing Opus packet header`; the changed files do not touch the Story/WebM path, and failed-job reruns require repository admin rights.
- **Failure evidence:** missing refs, missing snapshots, unsafe paths, incomplete Git options, and output collisions return structured diagnostics without publishing compare artifacts.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The new mode is opt-in and reads committed Git objects without checking out or executing the target repository. Removing the feature restores the existing local-JSON-only interface.

**Blast Radius:** compare CLI

The feature changes `archify/bin/archify.mjs`, Architecture Delta tests, and user documentation. It does not change schemas, renderers, Viewer behavior, package dependencies, or generated Viewer artifacts.

## Scope and limits

This PR reads snapshots that already exist at the requested path. It does not infer Architecture JSON from source code, resolve component renames, or claim runtime impact. Code-only repositories require Agent-authored, version-pinned snapshots before this deterministic comparison step.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, review assistance, and writing.
- Tools/model: Codex; GPT 6 Astra xHigh.
- Accountable contributor: @RedHeartSecretMan
- Problem origin: proposed improvement, validated with synthetic Git-tag fixtures and the vLLM tag/snapshot inspection recorded in issue #1044.
- [x] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable: this revision changes CLI Git input handling, diagnostics, tests, and documentation without changing diagram rendering.

Closes #1044

title: fix(timeline): keep the year on multi-year labels and the header in frame
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #1019.

A timeline crossing a year boundary dropped the year everywhere it printed a
date. For the reported fixture (events at `2025-03-01T10:00Z` and
`2026-03-01T10:00Z`) both cards read `03-01 10:00`, both passport contexts read
`03-01 10:00:00 UTC+00:00`, and the header was just `Time: UTC`; the tick labels
ran `03-06, …, 12-25, 02-05`, so the axis appeared to go backwards at the year
boundary. The README promises each card shows its exact time.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/timeline/render-timeline.mjs`
  - `multiYear` is derived from the display zone (`wall()`), and multi-year
    spans print `YYYY-MM-DD` in card times, tick labels, and
    `data-node-context`.
  - `dateYear()` zero-pads every printed year to at least four digits and keeps
    the sign for BC years (`-0001`), including the single-day header (`0099`
    instead of `99`).
  - The tick dedup key includes the year only for multi-year spans, so
    same-year suppression is unchanged.
  - A dense multi-year axis can suppress an individual tick label, so the
    header states the range once: `Time: UTC · 2025–2026`.
  - The header caption is measured as part of the canvas. It is left-anchored
    and was unmeasured, so a long IANA zone at the minimum axis width (480)
    clipped it; the canvas grows only when the caption would be clipped or come
    within a 4 px inset that absorbs fallback-font variance.
  - Header growth stops at the declared-wide reader width (1920 px), because
    wider canvases are scaled down by the viewer below the declared minimum
    text. `meta.translations` permits 400-character messages, so beyond that
    bound the evidence chip and the localized axis label are ellipsized
    (grapheme-safe, with a 15% reserve for emoji fallback glyphs) while the
    renderer-owned zone/date suffix stays visible; the full strings remain in
    `<title>`/`aria-label`. Evidence and caption reserve independently, so an
    emoji in one does not truncate the other.
  - Legend entries and the legend title keep whatever width they require, so
    the cap cannot cause `legend/label-too-wide`.
- `archify/renderers/shared/legend.mjs` — `legendFootprint()`/`measureLegend()`
  accept an optional `textAdvance` (default `() => 1`, so every other renderer
  is byte-identical). Timeline passes the emoji-aware advance so legend
  packing, `data-legend-x`/`-width`, and the drawn label share one width.
- `test/timeline-rendering.test.mjs` — tests for the multi-year reproduction, a
  same-year control, a 480 px long-zone fit, a no-growth control, a near-edge
  inset case, display-zone BC years, extreme translated evidence/axis
  overrides, the evidence-slack allocation, legend width preservation, and
  emoji fallback/grapheme truncation.

## Stability impact

- Both checked-in timeline examples, both waterfall examples, and every other
  generated golden are byte-identical; a same-year 480 px canvas whose caption
  already clears the edge stays at its existing 536 px.
- Years 0000–0999 gain leading zeros (intended: every printed date is
  `YYYY-MM-DD`); display-zone years above 9999 print as-is.
- Non-multi-year labels are otherwise unchanged.
- Extreme legend content necessarily keeps its width (the alternative is a
  hard `legend/label-too-wide` failure); under the `showcase` profile such an
  artifact also trips `composition/desktop-readability`. That trade-off is
  deliberate and matches the pre-existing "legend content is authored" rule.

## Tests run

- `test/timeline-rendering.test.mjs`, `test/timeline-dst-ticks.test.mjs`,
  `test/render-output-checks.test.mjs`: 92/92 pass.
- Red proofs: the multi-year test fails on `dev`; the narrow-axis width
  assertion fails with the width reservation removed; the no-growth control
  fails under an unconditional width reservation (547 vs 536); the near-edge
  inset case fails without the 4 px inset; the BC test fails with the old
  `dateYear`; the header cap test fails at 5492 px without the bound; the
  legend test reproduces `legend/label-too-wide` without the legend floor; the
  emoji-legend and split-advance tests fail without their reservations.
- `npm run test:generated`: all checks passed (30 golden renders, 28
  schema-enforcement cases, 2 template-freshness checks, 8 version checks).
- Full suite on the refreshed head: 3396 tests, 3148 pass, 45 fail — all
  known Windows environment failures (symlink/8.3/path checks) plus two
  load-sensitive tests: the brand-href fetch test passes 5/5 in isolation, and
  a 20 s local preview/git test cancelled on the slow host. No timeline or
  legend test failed. The refresh rebase onto dev `f90a1930` only brought the
  preview-status and WebM story commits; their tests are unmodified dev code.
- `scripts/build-zip.sh` rebuilt twice and `cmp`-identical (sha256
  `36a2c1cf2ffefbf9eb439866dfba7d0a953966455148c4ba193f4c19434212db`).

## Generated artifacts

title: fix(waterfall): key the incomplete legend only to open bars
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #1022.

The waterfall legend listed "Incomplete (no recorded end)" whenever any span
carried `status: "incomplete"`, even when that span has a recorded end and is
painted as a solid bar:

```json
"spans": [
  { "id": "a", "name": "A", "start": 0, "end": 100 },
  { "id": "b", "name": "B", "start": 10, "end": 50, "status": "incomplete", "parent": "a" }
]
```

Span `b` has an end and renders as a solid bar labelled `40 ms`, but the key
still claimed an open bar. The documented paint rule
(`renderers/waterfall/README.md`) keys the dashed body and open edge to an
incomplete span **without** an end.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/waterfall/render-waterfall.mjs` — `presentStatuses` now
  applies the same predicate that decides a bar's paint:
  `status !== 'incomplete' || row.open`. `error` and `cancelled` still recolor
  a bar and keep their keys; `incomplete` gets a key only when the bar is
  actually drawn open. Validation already guarantees that an open span carries
  `status: "incomplete"`, so the filter matches every schema-valid combination.
- `test/waterfall-rendering.test.mjs` — new test pins both directions: a
  closed incomplete span claims no key, an open one keeps it.

## Stability impact

- The only behavior change is the legend: a trace whose only `incomplete`
  spans have recorded ends now renders without the open key (and without a
  legend at all when nothing else is keyed), so the canvas height drops by the
  legend band exactly as the legend footprint dictates. The artifact checker
  reports identical composition metrics and summary on the reproduction; both
  shipped examples render byte-identically, and no committed artifact contains
  the key.
- Viewer, checker and docs were checked for assumptions about the key; the
  viewer already handles a missing legend group, and no doc promises a key per
  present status.

## Tests run

- `test/waterfall-rendering.test.mjs`: 13/13. With
  `test/render-output-checks.test.mjs`: 75/75.
- Red proof: the pre-fix renderer emits the `Incomplete (no recorded end)`
  legend for both the closed and the open fixture; with the fix the closed
  fixture drops it and the open fixture keeps it (the new test fails on
  `dev` and passes here).

title: fix(timeline): state sub-second break durations in milliseconds
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #1023.

A quiet period shorter than one second still becomes a compressed axis break,
but both break formatters rounded any duration below 1 s down to `0 s`. For the
reported fixture (events at +0, +1, +2, +3, +400 ms) the renderer produced a
397 ms break whose visible chip said `≈ 0 s` and whose accessible label said
`0 s without events omitted`, while `data-break-ms="397"` and the caption
reported one compressed period. Timestamps keep millisecond precision
(`\.\d{1,3}` in the schema, preserved since #870), so the labels should state
the omitted duration.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/timeline/render-timeline.mjs` — `durationLabel()` (exact,
  used by the break's accessible label) and `approximateDuration()` (the chip)
  now report sub-second durations in milliseconds. Durations of one second or
  more keep their existing whole-unit labels unchanged: the exact formatter
  still prints up to two units (`1 d 11 h`), and the approximate formatter
  still rounds to the two most significant adjacent units (`15 h`). No other
  call sites exist.
- `test/timeline-rendering.test.mjs` — new test pins the issue fixture: the
  layout break length is 397 ms, `data-break-ms="397"`, the chip reads
  `≈ 397 ms`, and the accessible label contains `397 ms without events
  omitted`.

- Only sub-second break labels change. Longer break labels are byte-identical,

title: fix(waterfall): scale the timing tolerance to the value magnitude
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #1021.

A waterfall span may state `end` and `duration` "only if they agree" (`renderers/waterfall/README.md`), but the agreement check used a fixed absolute tolerance of `1e-9`. `start`, `end` and `duration` are parsed independently as binary64, so subtracting epoch-sized values loses precision: for `start: 1700000000.1`, `end: 1700000000.3`, `duration: 0.2` the residual is `4.768371582e-8`, and the renderer refuses a span whose decimal values agree exactly:

```
waterfall/invalid-timing: Span "job" states end 1700000000.3 and duration 0.2,
which disagree with start 1700000000.1.
```

The schema allows any `start >= 0`, so epoch-second traces (and any large common offset) are inside the documented contract.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/waterfall/render-waterfall.mjs` — the agreement check now compares the residual against `max(1e-9, 2 * Number.EPSILON * scale)` where `scale` is the largest of `|start|`, `|end|`, `|duration|`. Two epsilons is the bound for three independent parses plus the subtraction (rounding noise cannot exceed it), and the previous `1e-9` floor keeps ordinary strictness for small values. A genuine disagreement above the window still emits `waterfall/invalid-timing` with the same subject, evidence and fix.
- `archify/renderers/waterfall/README.md` — states the agreement rule ("two epsilons of the largest operand") so the tolerance is part of the contract instead of an implementation detail.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared behavior for the waterfall renderer. Inputs that pass today are unaffected (the new window is never smaller than the old one); inputs that fail today for a genuine disagreement still fail — verified for exactly-representable cases at large magnitudes (`start = end = 1e16` with `duration: 7`, `start: 0, end: 1e15` with `duration: 1e15 + 0.5`), which the fixed window rejects. The only behavior change is that decimal-equal epoch-sized spans now validate, which is the reported bug. Bar geometry and labels are unchanged: the renderer recomputes the rendered duration from the recorded end either way.

## Tests run

- `test/waterfall-rendering.test.mjs`: 13/13. The new test "epoch-sized starts keep end and duration agreement in floating point" pins the issue fixture and asserts that a duration of `0.25` at the same magnitude is still refused.
- Red proof: with only the renderer reverted to `dev`, that test fails (12/13); with the fix it passes.
- Affected batch (`waterfall-rendering`, `render-failure-diagnostics`, `renderer-diagnostic-boundary`): 39/39.
- `npm run test:generated`: all checks pass.
- Full suite (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs`): 3387 tests, 3140 pass, 44 fail — the same Windows environment failures as the `dev` baseline (symlink/archive/browser-gate delivery tests), no new names.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — validation behavior only; rendered output is unchanged for every input that renders today.

title: fix(viewer): mobile nav reachability, dock clearance and presentation scroll
body:
## Problem and value

- Related issue: #1026 (bug report with reproductions and base measurements).
- Problem on the original base: at 360×760 the nav was a single scrolling row; `100%` and `Zoom in` were pushed outside the viewport, the route probe shared the nav's z-index and sat under it, and the presentation stage centred an oversized scene so its start edge could not be reached.
- Intended outcome: every nav action is reachable and hit-testable, every dock-owned overlay clears the bar, and the presentation stage can scroll across the whole scene.
- Worth maintaining: one measured dock height and five consumers, plus browser regression tests; no schema, renderer, or public contract change.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, and writing assistance.
- Tools/model: Hermes Agent (Nous Research), `deepseek-flash`; the agent reproduced the defects with CDP, edited the viewer sources, wrote the browser tests, ran the suites, and drafted this text. An independent three-seat review (Standards/Spec/Structure) ran on two cycles; blocking findings were fixed and re-reviewed. An earlier Claude audit found one stale generated proof artifact; it was rebuilt before this exact-head pass.
- Accountable contributor: @jahfaliabdulrahman-dev
- Problem origin: reproducible defects found during mobile inspection of a local Viewer build, then re-measured on the current base.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared Viewer behaviour (`viewer/viewer.css`, `viewer/viewer-chrome-layout.js`, `viewer/focus.js`, generated template).
- Coordinated slice: nav reachability, the measured dock clearance, and presentation start-edge reachability are one change. The cosmetic grouping of the three camera controls is explicitly deferred: they remain separate flex items and may wrap onto separate lines; no wrapper is introduced because it changed the toolbar's directional-key contract.
- `viewer-chrome-layout.js` publishes the measured dock height as `--archify-dock-h` (0 when hidden) before the desktop-only `eligible()` gate. This is intentionally separate from `--archify-nav-reserve`: the latter is the desktop stage-rail lift, while the former is the raw mobile dock height needed below that gate. The Passport fit reads that same measured dock and refits after placement; on the short-viewport compact path it moves below the dock when the space above is insufficient, using `--archify-passport-reserve` (the viewport-to-dock gap) for the CSS floor; the below-dock top is clamped inside the viewport. The regression guard covers the explaining position, the collapsed Passport at a mid-viewport dock, and a deep scroll past the dock. A schema-sized explanation scrolls inside the chip instead of growing through the dock.
- The stage, route probe, semantic lens, overview map and radar feedback consume the published band. The presentation stage uses `justify-content: flex-start` plus `margin-inline: auto` on the scene: fitting scenes stay centred and an oversized scene keeps its leading edge scrollable.
- Print: the print rule resets both `--archify-nav-reserve` and `--archify-dock-h` to `0px !important`. With scripts disabled, the mobile fallback would otherwise retain `6.25rem` of reserve: 116px of padding, 100px of it dead.
- Preserved: desktop stacking and layout, route-probe `data-route-dock="top"`, guide/finder visibility states, the wide-diagram scroll transform, dev's contrast tokens, parent navigation, short-viewport Passport handling, export notices, and the newer decoder diagnostics.

## Tests run

Base: `dev` @ `10b4dd5c`; head: **`c393fc7f`** (merge commit `4dfebf7e`, the compact Passport scroll clamp, the stronger collapsed/deep-scroll 320×300 guard, the full generated rebuild, and the README motion-proof refresh).

- `npm run test:generated` — pass at the final head.
- `test/viewer-mobile-chrome-browser.test.mjs` + `test/viewer-print-clearance-browser.test.mjs` + `test/passport-explanation-browser.test.mjs` + `test/semantic-legend-gateway.test.mjs` — **10/10 pass**.
- Browser regression set including `viewer-camera-browser.test.mjs` and `viewer-chrome-layout.test.mjs` — **50/50 pass**.
- `test/readme-showcase.test.mjs` — **14/14 pass** (one skipped) after rebuilding the motion proof from the final gallery artifacts.
- New focused test: 320×300, parent `meta.parentHref`, a schema-sized (≤1200 character) authored node explanation, `mobile: true`. It asserts the dock actually wraps (nav height > 1.5 button heights), every visible dock action stays inside the container and is hit-testable, `--archify-dock-h` covers the dock, the Passport title, prose and Back stay readable and clear of the dock (above it, or below it when the dock scrolls into the fixed chip) and the prose scrolls rather than being clipped, parent Back is hit-testable before the fixed Passport covers the header, and closing the explanation restores a hit-testable Explain focus. It asserts the reached `scrollY` for both offsets, so a short fixture cannot turn the mid/deep checks into clamped no-ops. It covers both the dock-flush position and a mid-viewport dock offset, so it is the guard for the merged composition, not a relabelled pre-integration capture.
- Shared boundary sample: rebuilt local `dev + #1001 + #1027` tree at the fixed #1027 head plus #1001 — `viewer-camera-browser.test.mjs`, `viewer-chrome-layout.test.mjs`, `viewer-mobile-chrome-browser.test.mjs` and `viewer-print-clearance-browser.test.mjs` — **44/44 pass**; the existing 175/225/300% camera assertions, dock/chrome checks and the new 320×300 sample all pass together.
- Not covered: no physical-device/printer run; the new sample is automated geometry/hit-test evidence, not a perceptual capture. Required CI at `c393fc7f` passed: https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40236775509. The separate FFmpeg 8.0 WebM decoder issue was tracked in #1061 and fixed by #1062, which is in `dev`; `webm-decode` also passes here.

## Visual evidence

- Existing mobile captures remain at their recorded earlier head; they are not relabelled as new-head evidence. No repeated Lens Clear/Copy or no-JS print captures are claimed.
- The new 320×300 check records geometry and hit-test results only; it does not claim a visual review of the composed screen.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify/assets/template.html` regenerated from the merged sources.
- 15 example pairs re-rendered; the five bundled drilldown pairs, `examples/ai-agent-n8n.html`, `docs/cases/mco-runtime.architecture.html` and `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html` kept current; `docs/gallery.html` and its artifacts rebuilt; `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` and receipt regenerated; `archify.zip` rebuilt (235 files).
- Dev's current `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.*` and export notices were retained; the proof was not refreshed merely because generated files were rebuilt.

## Attribution

The no-JS print reset and initial print regression were identified and prototyped by @BlueboxC in the fork correction at `28fbc157c608f985d0e4a2c6621230dcad12311b`; this PR adapts the authored one-line source change and regression test, preserving attribution in the test header and commit message. The fork commit also contains unrelated work and is not cherry-picked wholesale.

## Exact-head status

- Local generated and targeted checks above pass at `c393fc7f`; the same composition guard also passed a 360×760 recurrence with the long fixture during verification (the compact fix does not change the non-compact path).
- CI run 40236775509 at `c393fc7f` is **green**: scope, full-regression (1/2), browser-regression (1/2), test (18/20/22/24), webm-decode, webm-artifact, package smoke (ubuntu/macos/windows), Windows test portability (Node 22/24), website, zip-freshness and published-update-manifest all pass. CodeRabbit completed (including the scroll-offset nitpick, fixed in this head). The PR remains `BLOCKED` by the required reviewer decision, not by a check; do not merge until the maintainer review completes.

title: fix(viewer): camera viewport follows the container, not the narrower SVG box
body:
Fixes #1000

## Problem and value

- Related issue: #1000 (bug report with a minimal fictive JSON reproduction and a validation receipt). The PR is a Draft until a maintainer agrees on the scope, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for interaction changes.
- Problem on the current base (`dev` @ 824db3ad): a height-limited, narrow stage (for example a deep, right-growing tree) is centred in a much wider `.diagram-container`. `clamp()` and `clipToViewport()` in `viewer/viewer-camera.js` treat the SVG's own box as the viewport. After zooming in, the content is clipped to that narrow column, and panning stops at the column edges, although the container has free space. It happens standalone and in iframes.
- Intended outcome: the camera viewport is the container's content box in SVG layout coordinates and is never smaller than the SVG box. Zoomed content may use the whole container. Below or at 100% nothing changes, because the SVG stays at its layout origin.
- Before/after evidence: the new focused browser test (see Tests run) fails on `dev` and passes on this head.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, and drafting this description.
- Tools and model: Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5. Assisted areas: `viewer/viewer-camera.js`, the regression test in `test/viewer-camera-browser.test.mjs`, regenerated outputs.
- Accountable contributor: @leonkoellerwirth-arch
