## 摘要 / Summary

从 **4.0.0** 起将 Archify 从 MIT 改为 **AGPL-3.0-only**；4.0.0 之前的所有版本（1.x–3.x）仍为 MIT。原因：已有站点把 Archify 包装成收费在线服务转卖。AGPL 仍是开源协议，只要求把修改版作为网络服务提供的人公开源码；安装 Skill、生成和使用图表不受影响。

Relicense Archify from MIT to **AGPL-3.0-only starting with 4.0.0**; all releases before 4.0.0 stay MIT. Motivation: copies are being resold as paid hosted services. Normal use (installing the Skill, generating/using diagrams) is unaffected.

## 改动 / Changes
- `LICENSE`, `archify/LICENSE`: AGPL-3.0 全文 + 开头 NOTICE，原样保留 Cocoon AI（Cocoon-AI/architecture-diagram-generator）的 MIT 版权与许可声明，并声明 4.0.0 之前版本仍为 MIT。/ Full AGPL-3.0 text plus a NOTICE preserving the Cocoon AI MIT notice verbatim (package smoke still checks it).
- `archify/package.json`, `integrations/deepseek-harness/package.json` (+ its contract test), `archify/SKILL.md` frontmatter → `AGPL-3.0-only`.
- README（EN/ZH/JA/KO + README.md）：徽章、官方渠道段落、License 段落 + “为什么改 AGPL”说明。/ Badges, official-channels line, License section with a short "Why AGPL?" note in every language.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (both copies).
- Website: footer/meta/ProductFacts/gallery/community (`website/src`), checked-in `docs/index.html`, `scripts/gallery-template.html` → regenerated `docs/gallery.html`; `website/test/seo-content.test.mjs` expects `AGPL-3.0`.
- Regenerated `archify.zip` (canonical Node 22 / zlib 1.3.1-e00f703).

## 测试 / Tests
- `npm run test:full`: 3043 pass, 0 fail.
- `website` tests (after `npm run build`): 54 pass, 0 fail.
- `scripts/package-smoke.mjs` on the unpacked zip: passed.

## ⚠️ 待决定 / Open items (blocking merge)
1. **贡献者同意 / Contributor consent.** 外部贡献者的代码是按 MIT 提交的。MIT 允许把这些代码再以 AGPL 发布（保留其 MIT 声明即可），因此法律上不严格需要同意；但为了社区关系和稳妥，建议至少征得主要外部贡献者同意或公告征求意见。按 `git blame` 估算 src（archify/viewer/scripts/website/src，不含 examples/生成文件）约 44% 行属于 tt-a1i，约 41% 属于 sunsunsun / sunsunsun-java（Friend A），其余约 15% 来自约 100 位其他贡献者（主要：mango、goatliamia、GuYueFangYuan、YunyueLi、To3akaRin、uygnoey 等）。/ External contributions arrived under MIT; MIT permits sublicensing under AGPL with the notice kept, so consent is not strictly required, but asking the main contributors (esp. sunsunsun ~41% of surviving src lines) is recommended. 2. 版本：本 PR 不改版本号；实际生效于 4.0.0 发布时。/ No version bump here; takes effect with 4.0.0.

title: feat(workflow): surface partialLayout on --layout-json when validation fails (#934)
body:
## What this PR does

Closes #934 by surfacing the partial layout the workflow compiler already computes when
validation fails. The success path is unchanged; the failure path also emits a
`partialLayout` object containing the column grid, the node frames the compiler placed,
the rejected router candidates for each exhausted relationship, and the cached route points
of any relationship that routed before a later check failed.

It also carries the **five-project authoring comparison** the maintainer asked for, and the
two real defects that comparison surfaced.

## The three review gaps are addressed

**1. Layout-feedback exhaustion.** The non-diagnostic catch calls `buildPartialLayoutPayload`
before `feedbackFailure` creates the solver-budget diagnostic, so a diagnostic-code filter
could return null and omit the partial layout entirely. The filter no longer gates the
payload: the measured column grid, node frames and routed edge geometry are reported
whenever the compiler has them.

**2. Parallel edges without ids.** Matching a diagnostic on `from`/`to` alone can select the
*first* edge between two nodes instead of the edge that actually failed, because an edge
without an authored id carries a null `subject.edge`. The failing relationship is now recorded
by **exact object identity** during compilation, and every failing relationship is reported
with its own candidate evidence instead of only the first match.

**3. Conflicts detected after routing.** An edge can already hold valid cached route points
when a later pin, label or boundary check fails. The failing-edge branch no longer skips that
cache entry, so the routed geometry survives alongside the candidate families.

The **diagnostic subject shape is unchanged** — no field was added, and the existing contract
tests that pin the exact subject continue to pass. Edge identity is tracked out of band
instead.

## Two defects the comparison surfaced, both fixed here

**The payload never reached the `finalize` receipt.** `finalize` is the command the Skill
tells authors to run, and its failure receipt was byte-for-byte the same on both CLIs. The
payload was reachable only through `validate --layout-json`, which SKILL.md tells agents to
reach for only "when compact evidence lacks needed measurements". The delivery path now
carries it: renderer → structured renderer failure payload → validate/deliver failure receipt
→ finalize receipt and compact summary.

**A relationship that had routed successfully still carried another relationship's rejected
candidates.** `registerRouted` now clears the capture, so a later failure on a different
relationship no longer reports another edge's attempts as its own.

## The authoring comparison

Five real repositories: **express, flask, kubernetes, vite, ansible**. Each slice ran its own
repair chain against the base CLI and the candidate CLI from the same task prompt and the same
pinned source checkout, recorded every command with exit status and elapsed time, kept the
unsuccessful runs, replayed the candidate side's final JSON against both CLIs, and captured
before/after screenshots at 1440×900 and 2048×1320 in light and dark with the project's own
`visual-check`.

- **base**: `main` @ `25cf3708`
- **candidate**: `dev` @ `b71d1b3e` + this branch

### Result: the change reduced rework by **zero** rounds

| Project | base repairs | base finalize | base delivered | base CLI s | candidate repairs | candidate finalize | candidate delivered | candidate CLI s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| express | 1 | 2 | yes | 2.716 | 1 | 2 | yes | 2.581 |
| flask | 2 | 3 | yes | 4.696 | 2 | 3 | yes | 4.370 |
| kubernetes | 3 | 4 | yes | 8.076 | 3 | 4 | yes | 8.158 |
| vite | 1 | 2 | yes | 4.226 | 1 | 2 | yes | 6.517 |
| ansible | 2 | 3 | yes | 6.366 | 2 | 3 | yes | 5.403 |
| **total (5)** | **9** | | **5/5** | **26.08** | **9** | | **5/5** | **27.03** |

Author-side wall clock totals: **1841 s (base) → 1169 s (candidate)**. That is a **learning and
ordering artifact**, not a tool effect — the candidate chains ran second in the same session,
after the source and the draft were already understood. CLI execution, the only timing that
isolates the tool, is a wash.

### The payload is real and readable — but largely redundant

Where it appeared it was rich. From the flask slice, the edge that failed:

```json
{ "id": "unhandled-exception", "from": "dispatch", "to": "user-exception",
  "attemptedCandidateFamilies": [
    { "family": "facing-straight",   "points": [[794.4, 217], [724.4, 615]] },
    { "family": "lane-gap-corridor", "points": [[794.4, 217], [794.4, 201], [794.4, 414], [708.4, 414], [708.4, 615], [724.4, 615]] },
    ... 15 more families ...
  ],
  "points": [[794.4, 217], [794.4, 201], [199, 201], [199, 657], [794.4, 657], [794.4, 641]] }
```

Read against the node frames, `view-call` occupies `x 732.4 … 856.4` directly under
`dispatch` (`x 724.4 … 864.4`), so every straight and column-gap candidate for
`dispatch → user-exception` crosses it, and the router's fallback was a **511 px leftward
detour along `y = 201`** — the same corridor `wsgi-call` runs in. That is precisely the merge
the diagnostic reported.

But the base's receipts already carried the conclusion. From the ansible slice, the base
diagnostic said, with the numbers spelled out:

```json
"evidence": { "requiredFontPx": 9.5, "maximumSlotFontPx": 8,
               "canvasWidthPx": 1458, "maximumCanvasWidthPx": 1240, ... }
```

"Compact column spacing or node widths until the implicit canvas is at most 1240px wide" was
an explicit instruction with the target width stated. The author did not need the payload's
column grid to find that number. Two further observations: the base's `validate --layout-json`
**already** returned the column grid, the node frames and the routed points — the payload's
marginal content is the rejected candidate point sets; and those sets are only present for
some failure classes (in the vite slice the failing relationship never entered the router's
reject path, so nothing attributable to it was available).

### Honesty notes

- **Not better.** No measurable repair-round reduction in any of the five projects. This is a
  better-diagnostics change, not a better-workflow change, on this evidence.
- **The wall-clock improvement is not real.** Both candidate chains ran second in one session.
- **Small sample.** Five projects, one diagram each, one authoring agent, and the failure
  classes each project happened to hit.
- **One slice was interrupted.** The ansible slice's first sub-agent run hit a token-plan
  limit; its remaining repair rounds were completed from the preserved traces, and the tooling
  errors that produced (runs without `--repo-root`) were removed from the log rather than left
  to look like authoring attempts. Every genuine authoring failure is kept.
- **The candidate tree changed mid-run.** The delivery-path fix landed while the flask and
  vite slices were in flight. Both detected it, preserved their pre-update receipts, and
  re-ran against the current build.

### Evidence folder

`evidence/README.md` is the index and the method. `evidence/projects/<slug>/` holds the task
prompt, the pinned revision, each side's draft and every repair with its receipts and
`commands.log`, the frozen replay receipt, the screenshots, `report.json` and
`comparison.md` (with each slice's own negative findings). `python3 evidence/aggregate.py`
rebuilds the table above. The pinned source checkouts under `projects/*/src-*` are inputs
rather than evidence and are excluded by `evidence/.gitignore`.

## Focused regressions

`archify/test/validate-layout-json-partial.test.mjs` carries 8 cases:

| # | Case | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | feasible pin | success path unchanged, no `partialLayout` |
| 2 | self-loop | route-feasibility failure carries attempted candidates with points |
| 3 | explicit-pin-conflict | pin failure carries `partialLayout` |
| 4 | `compileWorkflow` result | `partialLayout` is a top-level field, the receipt stays byte-identical |
| 5 | non-route failure code | a `layout/constraint` failure still carries the measured partial layout |
| 6 | three parallel edges | every relationship is attributed its own rejected candidate geometry, none dropped |
| 7 | routed then failed | the failing edge keeps its cached route points, and a routed relationship carries no rejected attempts |
| 8 | finalize receipt | the `finalize` failure receipt carries the partial layout |

Each of the new cases **fails against the previous revision of this branch** and passes here.

## Test results

```
$ node --test archify/test/workflow-compiler.test.mjs \
    archify/test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs \
    archify/test/workflow-*.test.mjs \
    archify/test/validate-layout-json-partial.test.mjs
# tests 300
# pass 299
# fail 0
# skipped 1
```

The single skip is the pre-existing browser-gated test.

## Base

This PR is retargeted to `dev` and synchronized with its latest revision (`b71d1b3e`).
`archify.zip` is regenerated against that base via `scripts/build-zip.sh` (Node 22.23.2,
bundled zlib 1.3.1-e00f703).

## Commits

| SHA | What |
|---|---|
| `10fabc87` | feat(workflow): surface partialLayout on --layout-json when validation fails (#934) |
| `c64d4294` | fix(workflow): make the partial layout dependable on every failure path — the three review gaps |
| `cf3e7b44` | feat(workflow): carry the partial layout into the finalize failure receipt — the delivery gap |
| `f4e6a77a` | fix(workflow): do not report another relationship's stale router attempts |
| `95cc8ec7` | docs(evidence): add the #934 Workflow authoring comparison |

Closes #934

title: fix(sequence): emit the whole ordered adjustment when a note reaches several messages
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #903.

On the reported draft (owner at `y: 300` with a note wrapping onto the blockers at `y: 330` and `y: 366`), the `sequence/note-overlap` receipt advertised `set /messages/1/y to 399` — a move that jumps the first blocker past the second one, reordering the timeline — and the follow-up run then reported the same failure for blocker `/messages/2/y` with `supportedFixes: []`. The diagnostic's repair model was single-blocker while the failure reaches several messages, so the documented repair loop stalled exactly where the issue measured it (26 of 26 targeted multi-blocker configurations, 3 of 354 random documents).

The receipt now carries **one ordered adjustment for every message the note reaches**: the first reached message takes the first clear slot at or below `requiredY`, each following one the first clear slot below the previous, every candidate verified through the same readability predicate a single move uses. Both repair paths now share one invariant — a repair never moves a message past one the note does not reach, because that would silently reorder the timeline — and an arrangement that cannot hold (no authored room, a crossing, a content-limit breach) advertises `[]` instead of a broken edit.

PR improvement check (`CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-improvement-check`): test-value (implementation mode) drove the suite toward user-visible outcomes — the advertised set applies to a clean document, a withhold keeps the document honest — instead of source-shape assertions; simplifying the single- and multi-blocker paths onto the shared `moveCeiling` predicate removed the duplicated crowding cap that caused the forced `+28` spacing, and the moved-message clone now drops its memoized note layout so a long scan does not accumulate dead entries.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/sequence/render-sequence.mjs` — the note-overlap repair is now an ordered joint adjustment:
  - `noteReachedMessages` lists every message the wrapped note reaches, y-ordered; the multi-blocker receipt carries them all in `evidence.reached` and the human message counts the rest (`and N more message(s) below`).
  - `noteOverlapAdjustment` places each reached message on the first clear slot at or below the previous one (never above `requiredY`), re-running `messageFitsAt` per candidate and restoring every temporary move in a `finally`. The advertised set is the verified arrangement; `[]` when none holds.
  - `messageFitsAt` hardening, all driven by review findings: candidate geometry is read at the moved position with the memoized note layout invalidated (`noteLayouts.delete`), so a reached message with its own note is judged where it would actually land; a moved message's own note must still end above the content limit on an authored canvas (an automatic one regrows); and a position within 4 px of a segment frame edge is rejected (`sequence/segment-message-border-run`; the shared `composition/container-border-run` check keeps the exact-collinearity case covered in every profile).
  - The single-blocker path (`noteSingleAdjustment`) keeps its one-slot preference — `requiredY` first — and gains the same bounded step-over for an edge or near miss, capped by the next message the note does not reach (the reported timeline order is preserved; the unedited payment draft in `test/sequence-segment-labels.test.mjs` still advertises `[]`).
  - No cap truncates wide failures: the scan bound scales with the reached count (a 23-message chain yields 23 fixes `996…1612`).
- `test/sequence-note-wrap.test.mjs` — 29 tests: the 20 maintained note-wrap cases plus nine new ones covering the issue's joint adjustment (red on the pristine renderer: 20 pass / 9 fail), the ordered withhold when the arrangement would cross a later message or lack authored room, the moved-position geometry of a reached message's own note, the authored-canvas content limit, a segment frame edge (multi and single paths), disjoint lanes keeping a closer row (no forced uniform `+28`), and the long chain.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: Shared behavior. `render-sequence.mjs` produces diagnostics for every sequence artifact through `validate`, `render`, `deliver`, and `compare`. Only the receipt contents of a failing `sequence/note-overlap` change (plus the repairs offered); passing documents and rendered SVG are byte-identical (`render sequence examples/cache-miss-request.sequence.json` is sha256 `89c56e9e…` on base and head).
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: human messages stay byte-identical except the new `and N more message(s) below` clause on multi-reached receipts; exit codes and the set of inputs that pass or fail are unchanged. Intended change: a multi-reached failure advertises the whole verified adjustment instead of one edit that reorders the timeline.

## Also repairs the tip's generated checks (#910 aftermath)

While verifying this branch on the tip, `npm run test:generated` fails there — reproduced on the pristine renderer before this branch's changes, and the same `test (22)` job is red on dev's own push run for `96234021` while its predecessor `d5806a6f` was green. #910 changed the shared HTML template and the three guide templates without re-deriving their downstream artifacts, so this PR carries the mechanical repair as its second commit:

- `check-release-identity` read the star icon's SVG path data (`l1.9 3.9 4.3.6-3.1`) as a hardcoded package version; the path numbers are now separated (`4.3 .6-3.1`), leaving the icon geometry identical while no longer matching the version pattern.
- All 15 bundled example renders under `examples/` and `archify/examples/`, plus the `examples/web-app.html` viewer example, are re-derived from their JSON IR (`npm --prefix archify run render:examples` plus the packaged render; `test/golden.mjs` re-checks all three template-owned artifacts); `npm run test:generated` now passes end to end.
- `archify.zip` is rebuilt from the re-derived tree; versus the previous build of this branch it differs only in its 15 packaged example members.
- The checked-in site pages and proofs are re-derived with the repository's own generators: `docs/guide.html` (`build-guide.mjs`), `docs/start.html` (`build-start.mjs`), `docs/gallery.html`, `docs/gallery/manifest.json` and the 12 gallery artifacts (`build-gallery.mjs docs`), `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` and its receipt (`archify compare architecture` with the checked fixtures), and the README live-proof GIF plus receipt (`scripts/build-readme-showcase.mjs`, headless Chrome capture + ffmpeg, 54 frames / 5.4 s / 815,100 bytes). The five reproducibility tests — `guide-page`, `start-page`, `gallery`, the checkout case in `architecture-delta`, and `readme-showcase` — pass on the result.
- `published-update-manifest` stays red for a reason outside this diff: dev's `docs/skill-updates/archify/stable.json` still describes v3.0.1 while release v3.1.0 was published at 17:23Z. `release.yml` documents that manifest as a post-Release follow-up commit ("publish … in a follow-up commit"), and the failing job message asks for exactly that; it is deliberately left to the release flow.

## Tests run

Base `origin/dev` `96234021` → candidate head `61ee87fd` (sequence fix `14b4c7c1`, tip repair `54ccf00d`, artifact re-derivation `2ae106d0`, live-proof rebuild `61ee87fd`).

- New suite on the head: 29/29 pass. Red proof: the same test file on the pristine renderer (head tree with only the renderer reverted) scores 20 pass / 9 fail — exactly the nine new cases.

title: fix(sequence): report canvas-level failures as typed diagnostics
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #890.

Canvas-level `sequence` failures only pushed prose into `problems`, so their diagnostics fell back to the untyped default (`code: layout/constraint`, `subject: {diagramType: 'sequence'}`, empty `evidence` and `supportedFixes`) even though the messages already carried the measured repair, e.g. `keep y between 160 and 397` or `set meta.viewBox[0] to at least 1132`. `references/authoring-contract.md` asks agents to consume `code` / `subject` / `evidence` / `supportedFixes`, so for these failures the documented repair loop had nothing to act on. The sibling checks in the same renderer (`participant-*-overflow`, `unknown-endpoint`, `segment-message-border-run`, `note-canvas-limit`, `note-overlap`, `segment-label-overlap`) already carry the fields.

PR improvement check (`CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-improvement-check`): test-value (implementation mode) drove the suite toward user-visible outcomes — a typed receipt and a repair that clears its own diagnostic (or is withheld with `[]`) — instead of source-shape assertions; the focused survey in `simplify-codebase` found the mid-function `report` closure duplicated the push-and-record pattern, so it now has a single definition at the top of `validateSequence`, and no other worthwhile simplification inside this diff's ownership.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/sequence/render-sequence.mjs` — five canvas-level sites now emit the renderer's native typed diagnostics:
  - `sequence/message-outside-timeline` — `subject` names the message and `/messages/i/y`; `evidence` carries `y`, `minimumY`, `maximumY`, `viewBoxHeight`, `lifelineTop`, `lifelineBottom`; the `set /messages/i/y to ` repair is offered only when `messageFitsAt` confirms the move stays readable (timeline bounds, 28 px crowding, label/route/note collisions, positions within 4 px of a segment border in showcase, and an exact border coincidence in every profile — the shared `composition/container-border-run` check). The check simulates the candidate y on the real message object (its memoized note geometry is invalidated and restored), so it also sees what the repairs reviewed on this PR traded for: a segment label that would newly cover the moved message, two segment titles landing on the same fallback slot (compared pairwise at the current and the candidate y — an overlap the validator reports in every profile), the moved message's own note on an authored canvas, and the legend room a downward move would take from an authored canvas (the speculative legend measurement runs inside `withIsolatedDiagnosticRecording`, and an automatic canvas regrows to hold its legend). A failure the document already had keeps its own diagnostic; only a newly created one withholds the repair.
  - `sequence/segment-outside-canvas` — `subject` names the segment (`/segments/i`); `evidence` carries `from`, `to`, and both bounds; start/end repairs are offered only while the clamped range stays valid (`from < to`) and the edited segment's label placement stays clear of the other segment labels (and, in showcase, of the messages it would cover). The check simulates the repaired bound on the segment itself and, when a sibling segment is eligible for the same repair, simulates both together so a repair loop cannot land two labels on the same fallback slot.
  - `sequence/segment-label-overflow` — `subject` names `/segments/i/label`; `evidence` carries the label bounds, its width, the frame's available width, and the required viewBox width; the repair raises `meta.viewBox[0]` on authored canvases and authors `meta.viewBox` at no less than the schema minimum (480) on automatic ones, and the suggested width re-tests the same predicate the diagnostic uses so a rounding artifact cannot publish a width equal to the current one.
  - `sequence/participants-exceed-canvas` — `subject` is `/meta/viewBox/0`; `evidence` carries the last participant, participant width, count, column fit, the required width, and `viewBoxAuthored`; the repair raises `meta.viewBox[0]` on authored canvases and authors `meta.viewBox` (schema-legal height, preserving a taller measured automatic height) on automatic ones. For spread canvases the suggestion re-evaluates the column geometry the layout uses at the candidate width and steps up until the row it would produce fits, so the offered edit clears the diagnostic in one application (a fractional column gap could otherwise make it a no-op, or take up to five successive one-pixel applications).
  - `sequence/legend-canvas-limit` — `subject` is `/meta/viewBox/1`; `evidence` carries `contentBottom`, the required legend height, and whether the canvas was authored; the repair raises `meta.viewBox[1]` when authored.
  - `sequence/timeline-height-insufficient` — typed for contract uniformity; the `viewBox` schema minimum (480) and the automatic-height floor (327) keep it unreachable from schema-valid input today.
- Messages, exit codes, and pass/fail behavior are unchanged: messages stay byte-identical, and only the structured fields (plus the standard `Fix: …` suffix where a repair exists) change in receipts.
- `test/sequence-canvas-diagnostics.test.mjs` — 30 tests: structured fields per kind, distinct subjects for repeated failures, "the offered repairs clear their own diagnostic" for every both-bound and repeated case, withheld repairs (`[]`) for crowded messages, off-canvas ranges, border-adjacent or exactly-coincident positions in showcase and standard, single and joint label collisions, and the automatic-canvas repairs authoring a schema-legal viewBox. The twelve review follow-ups cover the message clamp's trades (a segment label newly covering the moved message, plus note-bearing, blocker-move, and automatic-canvas variants; the two-title fallback-slot collision in showcase and standard with a clear-title control; the implicit-legend loss with a hidden-legend control) and the width repairs re-validating against the widened canvas (a floating-point-equal width and a 31-participant spacing chain that must clear in one application).

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: Shared behavior. `render-sequence.mjs` produces diagnostics for every sequence artifact through `validate`, `render`, `deliver`, and `compare`. Consumers reading `diagnostics[]` now receive typed fields for these five failures instead of the `layout/constraint` fallback.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: rendered SVG is byte-identical on the maintained example; human-readable messages are byte-identical; exit codes and the set of inputs that pass or fail are unchanged. Intended change: `subject`/`evidence`/`supportedFixes` are populated for these failures and the human receipt gains the shared `Fix: …` suffix exactly where a repair is offered.

## Tests run

Base `origin/dev` `65607f4f` → candidate head `02d9b494`.

- New suite on the head: 30/30 pass. Red proofs: the original 8-test revision against pristine `65607f4f` with only the test copied in scores 0/8 — the codes do not exist on the base; the five message-clamp follow-ups offered `set /messages/0/y to 397`, `.../1/y to 344`, and `.../1/y to 395` before the fix, each application swapping the failure; the two-title collision tests offered `.../0/y to 397` before the pairwise check; the implicit-legend test offered `.../1/y to 384` before the legend measure; the width-repair tests offered a width equal to the current canvas (2059 on a 2059-wide canvas) and a chain value (4099/4100) that did not clear the diagnostic in one application.
- Focused batch via the repository runner (`npm run test:focus --` with `sequence-canvas-diagnostics`, `sequence-column-fit`, `sequence-note-wrap`, `sequence-segment-labels`, `sequence-header-clearance`, `sequence-self-message`, `sequence-width-review`, `render-failure-diagnostics`, `renderer-diagnostic-boundary`): 132 tests, 130 pass, 0 fail, 2 browser-gated skips — identical under Node 22.23.1 and Node 24.
- Full suite `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` on the head: 2517 passing / 51 unique failing. 50 of the 51 are the pre-existing Windows environment failures (symlink privileges and runner path handling) that are identical across the pristine `65607f4f` comparison run (2488 passing / 58 unique failing, whose extra 8 were exactly the new suite's original red proof); the 51st is one of two `update-notifier`/`delivery-update` concurrency tests that flip between runs on this Windows host ("a killed checker holding the cache claim…" this run, "concurrent checks use one writer…" the run before) — both pass when their files are rerun on the same head. No other test changes state, and the head run executes all 30 new tests.
- Generated checks on the head: `npm run test:generated` — viewer freshness, brand marks, validators, release identity, and `test/golden.mjs` all passed.
- Rendered-output byte-identity: `render sequence examples/cache-miss-request.sequence.json` is sha256 `6743e6d3…` on both base and head.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — non-visual diagnostics change; rendered output is byte-identical.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip` rebuilt with the canonical Node 22.23.1 toolchain (bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`) on the base `65607f4f`. Calibration: a pristine-tree rebuild reproduces the committed archive byte-for-byte (`57060be5…`). The head archive rebuilds byte-identical twice (`b3fb133e…`), and its only changed member against the committed archive is `archify/renderers/sequence/render-sequence.mjs`. `scripts/package-smoke.mjs` passes on the extracted archive.

## Problem and value

This adds a listing for [archify-index](https://github.com/Thakay/archify-index), a small standalone tool I wrote after documenting an agent integration with four Archify diagrams and opening each one from a file picker. It writes a single `index.html` beside the delivered pages and shows them in one window, one tab per diagram, opening every diagram in the same theme through the existing `?theme=` parameter. Given JSON specs, it runs `archify deliver` on them first.

It follows the package model in #663: it lives in its own repository, reads delivered pages as text and never changes them, runs no code inside Archify, and has no telemetry, hosted service or runtime dependency. It is separate from the drilldown links in #281: the index lists a set, while #281 links a node to another diagram.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: metadata only. Adds `community/packages/archify-index.json`. No Archify runtime, schema, Viewer, website source or generated output changes; the catalog card is derived from the file at build time.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: nothing in Archify changes. Three fields deserve a note.
  - `type: "wrapper"` is the closest of the five types. The tool calls the Archify CLI when it is given specs, but its main use reads pages Archify already delivered, and it never authors JSON IR. I'm happy to change the type if you read it differently.
  - `schemaVersions: [1, 2]` are the `schema_version` values of the specs it was tested with through `archify deliver`: three v1 and two v2 examples from Archify 3.0.1. The tool does not read `schema_version` itself.
  - `archify: "3.0.1"` is the only release it has been tested against. On current `dev` it labels pages of the newer diagram types from their delivery receipt or their English or Chinese description; I'll widen the range only after testing the next release.
- The name follows the existing `archify-` entries. If you would rather keep that prefix for official packages, I'll rename it.

title: fix(checker): preserve endpoint identity around quadratic curves
body:
## Problem and value

Public `archify check` can reject readable-v2 SVG with a false arrowhead collision when relationships end in non-collinear quadratic curves. On current dev, `M20 20H100Q140 20 140 60` and `M20 25H100Q100 140 140 140` are treated as ending at earlier straight-piece endpoints although their actual endpoints are separated.

Preserve actual relationship endpoint identity when projecting straight pieces. This removes an erroneous repair demand without expanding curve-body analysis or changing rendered output. This narrow fix has a public reproduction.

## Stability impact

- Shared checker behavior: collectArrows records actual endpoints; routeParts assigns semantic source/target flags only to pieces that reach them. Renderer layout, schemas, defaults, parser behavior and quality thresholds remain unchanged.
- Preserve legacy composition metadata, moveto boundaries, real straight/collinear-Q collisions, and tiny terminal segments removed by normalization. The accepted scoped-review correction remains unchanged.
- Applied test-value: five public checker cases distinguish the false positive from trailing-line, genuine-collision, collinear-Q and normalization controls without freezing automatic layout. Endpoint identity cannot be recovered from projected straight pieces alone; the scoped simplification assessment found no worthwhile state removal.
- #822 remains at c50ed25adee38ae2cfecea61a95c2bfe2204d71a. A private combined run passed 82 tests on the previous base, 2026-10-10 19:54:04–19:54:08 UTC. Only five root README files changed in the new base; parser/checker inputs are unchanged. No #822 code is included.
- #873 (bc5e2c720697399d52698cb9192e2e0051c60047) adds malformed-SVG structural acceptance checks; its checker patch does not change endpoint projection or routeParts. No combined-run evidence is claimed.

title: fix(viewer): save exports through Artifact host
body:
## Problem
Viewer exports use an anchor download which Claude Artifacts suppress, so published diagrams cannot save generated files.

## Value
Artifacts use the host save confirmation when it is available, while standalone HTML retains the existing browser-download behavior.

## Approach
- add an optional `window.claude.use("downloads")` adapter
- wait for host save completion before receipts and success feedback
- preserve anchor fallback only when the capability is absent or unavailable
- treat user cancellation as neither a success nor a fallback download
- cover host success, unavailable capability, cancellation, and rejection in Chromium

## Validation
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=<Chrome> node --test test/export-browser.test.mjs`
- `npm --prefix archify run check:viewer`

## Impact
The optional host path only activates in compatible Artifact hosts. A hosted Artifact check remains an explicit maintainer acceptance item because this checkout cannot publish an Artifact.

body:
## Revision update — 2026-10-16

Responding to the maintainer's request:
https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/863#issuecomment-6212616138

- Rebased onto latest dev: `708e95efde033270af6e2e212d60bfea34859361`.
- Updated candidate: `1d8bf42` (full SHA in PR head).
- Resolved source/test conflicts while preserving #941's standalone AppCompat environment cleanup and other latest-dev behavior.
- Updated the delivery contract and zero-response diagnostic to disclose that the Windows switches suppress browser de-elevation: an elevated parent keeps the browser elevated. Native token/elevation observations remain required; no Windows acceptance is inferred from this change.
- Scoped test-value review retained the upstream environment, pipe, profile and cleanup coverage and adapted only the expectations intentionally changed by this PR. No additional fixture family or complexity layer was needed.

### Verification on the updated candidate

- Focused visual-check, pipe transport, finalize lifecycle and temp cleanup suites: **123 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**. Skips require native Windows filesystem/discovery behavior.
- `npm run test:generated`: passed.
- Real macOS Chrome `test/finalize-browser.test.mjs`: **1 passed, 0 skipped**, including repeated finalize and all four gates. This is macOS regression evidence, not Windows acceptance.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Rebuilt only archify.zip; repeat build byte-identical with official Node 22.23.2 / zlib 1.3.1-e00f703. SHA-256: `b80aae8a6eb4f9d7b715c6dd974a17b7dc2b868eb516601f3dd6d11d40337d61`.
- Updated-head CI completed successfully; see below. Historical results remain labeled separately.

### Native Windows validation completed — 2026-10-17

[Redacted evidence bundle](https://gist.github.com/xiajiahang/cfd0bd4836d662ac7fd08eb437cd31b4): exact commands, environment/browser versions, inherited compatibility values, sampled parent/browser token observations, stdout/stderr, delivery/browser/finalize receipts for 12 runs, runner source, input and identical HTML.

Baseline: `708e95efde033270af6e2e212d60bfea34859361`; candidate: `1d8bf425d1b24f6f5f525d2e12fb5d9a742d6917`. Windows 10 build 19045, Node 24.19.0, Chrome 155.0.8059.80, Edge 155.0.4283.45. Same input bytes and `finalize architecture ... --quality showcase --json`.

| Parent environment | Browser / inherited layer | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary | Chrome / unset | pass | pass |
| Ordinary | Edge / unset | pass | pass |
| Ordinary | Edge / controlled DetectorsAppHealth | pass | pass |
| Administrator | Chrome / unset | browser-check fails | all four gates pass |
| Administrator | Edge / unset | browser-check fails | all four gates pass |
| Administrator | Edge / controlled DetectorsAppHealth | browser-check fails | all four gates pass |

All three elevated baseline failures pass validate/deliver/check, then fail browser-check with pipe closure and zero response bytes. Matching candidates pass all four gates. Native OpenProcessToken/GetTokenInformation samples observe elevated initial candidate browsers (elevated=1/type=2), confirming retained elevation. Baseline samples include non-elevated browser descendants. Sampling can miss short-lived processes; sandbox subprocesses are not assumed to share elevation. The retained-elevation tradeoff remains for maintainer judgment.

All 144 original manifest entries were checked. All 12 input hashes match Git content at the stated commits; actual HTML hashes match stdout/browser/delivery records. All nine successful browser receipts report current provenance and match delivery receipt IDs. Public-file bytes were verified after upload. Private usernames/project/runtime paths were replaced consistently. Public JSON files are reserialized review copies, with separate checksums; embedded original receipt hashes remain historical values, not hashes of the redacted copies. Input/HTML bytes are unchanged.

Limitations: the original reporter Git Bash/AppCompat environment was not reproduced. The ordinary controlled AppCompat case passes on both revisions, so no fix claim for that specific reproduction is made. No perceptual visual review is claimed. Supplied native Windows records were inspected on macOS, not independently rerun there. No separate clean-worktree/source-digest attestation is archived; commit labels are runner-reported identities. Results apply to the recorded host/versions.

[Final-head CI](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/38887463181): 19 passing jobs, two deployment skips; CodeRabbit status successful. Maintainer review/merge decision remains outstanding.

---

## Historical submission evidence (original head 47d2166; not rerun on this head)

## Problem and value

Refs #790. When Chrome/Edge relaunch from an elevated Windows shell, the new process loses the inherited remote-debugging-pipe handles and browser-check fails before inspecting the artifact. Current dev does not pass either of the startup switches verified by the reporter.

Use Windows-only `--do-not-de-elevate` and `--edge-skip-compat-layer-relaunch` to keep the browser in the process holding those handles. This reuses the existing pipe transport rather than adding a second connection mechanism.

## Stability impact

- Shared process-launch behavior in `ChromeVisualBrowser`; direct callers include visual-check, browser-check and finalize across diagram types.
- macOS/Linux arguments, private profiles, gate order, provenance, failure receipts, pipe descriptors, cleanup and existing no-sandbox policy remain unchanged. No dependency, schema, version or rendering change.
- Deliberate Windows tradeoff: an elevated parent retains its existing privilege level in the launched browser rather than automatically de-elevating. This does not request elevation or add `--no-sandbox`. Maintainer review of that choice and elevated-host acceptance remain required.
- Project test-value review extends the existing browser fixture at the spawn boundary. It protects parameter forwarding as well as platform isolation, without introducing another fixture family. No concrete duplicate-state/layer concern justified a simplify-codebase change.

## Tests run

Comparison base: `744d8e10bda445ef1aebbf63d72ceca7445b069b`. Candidate: `47d2166a5c5a3a57540849cc04d12fc8c8eb72e6` (the user-reviewed source and tests are unchanged). Environment: macOS, official Node 22.23.2 with zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`.

- Red/green: new regression fails on unchanged runtime because `--do-not-de-elevate` is absent; candidate passes.

title: fix(text): ignore supplementary variation selector advance
body:
## Problem and value

Shared text measurement counts supplementary variation selectors U+E0100–U+E01EF as visible columns. An ideographic variation sequence therefore gains a spurious unit, causing unnecessary font shrinkage, wrapping or width rejection. Existing BMP selector handling already ignores their independent advance. Apply the same rule to the supplementary selector block.

Chrome canvas measurements with 16px Menlo/monospace: `漢` and `漢` + U+E0100 both measure 16.320007px, but base textUnits returns 2 vs 3. `a` and `a` + U+E01EF both measure 9.6328125px, but base returns 1 vs 2. The selector alone measures 0px but base counts 1. [Unicode selector block](https://www.unicode.org/charts/nameslist/n_E0100.html) defines the exact range.

An incomplete installation can put directories at required file paths such as `assets/template.html`, `bin/preview.mjs`, a schema, an example, or an authoring reference. `doctor` checks only path existence and incorrectly reports the installation ready, even though those files cannot be loaded.

Use one bounded regular-file check for doctor’s existing required-file inventory. This rejects directories and other non-file entries while preserving symlinks to regular files and the existing missing-file report.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, and description writing.
- Tools and model: Codex (model `gpt-6.1-sol`) investigated the source, wrote the change and its tests, ran the checks reported below, and drafted this description. Claude Code (Claude Opus) rebased the change onto current `dev` on 2026-10-24, re-ran the focused checks listed under Rebase onto current dev, and edited this description.
- Accountable contributor: @rudycelekli
- Problem origin: code inspection; a reproducible defect found by reading the current source, not an observed production or Agent failure.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- Local doctor behavior only: readiness requires an actual regular file at each existing inventory entry.
- Supported Node checks, corrupt-validator import checks, labels, nonzero incomplete-install exits, and ordinary complete installations remain intact. No inventory, version, or installation action is added.
- Applied test-value: one isolated installation exercises five representative required-file groups and restores each entry between probes. Existing complete, incomplete, and corrupt-validator tests supply compatibility coverage.
- Focused simplify survey centralizes the file-kind rule in one local helper; no unrelated doctor restructuring.

title: fix(workflow): offer a member-preserving group placement for blocked routes
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Revision history

- **`c52a8ce` / `e2267b80` — first head.** Diagnostic evidence plus a group-placement repair.
- **`d6beaabe` — second head.** Addressed the first review finding.
- **`04f774eb` — current head.** Addresses the second review finding.

### Review finding addressed: the repair could be empty, or eject a member

[Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r) found two concrete defects in the first head's candidate search, which stepped `toCol` down by one from the authored span. Both reproduce:

| shape | first head | current head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| group spanning **exactly** the blocking column (`fromCol: 1, toCol: 1`) | `supportedFixes: []` — the loop tested only `0..0` and the unchanged `1..1`, never the `0..1` span that compiles | advertises `fromCol 0, toCol 1`, which compiles |
| wider group owning a node in its **rightmost** column | advertised a compiling span that **ejected that node** from the group | advertises `0..3`, keeping the member at column 3 inside the span |

The second one is the more serious: `acceptsFix` only proves the document compiles, so a span that silently drops a member still verified. The search now derives the members' own column range and only considers spans that contain it, so ejection is impossible by construction rather than by luck. `readableGroupBounds` already excludes nodes outside `fromCol..toCol`, which is what made the ejection silent.

Two regression cases cover both shapes and assert that the advertised span compiles **and** keeps every member. Reverting to the first head's search makes them fail (`pass 0 / fail 1`).

### Second review finding: the repair could absorb a node that was never in the group

Both [Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239894375) and [CodeRabbit](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239894471) reported that the member filter matched **every** same-lane node with an integer `col`, never consulting the group's own span. An unrelated same-lane node outside `fromCol..toCol` therefore looked like a member and stretched the advertised span to reach it:

```text
fixture + unrelated "responders" node at col 5
  first head -> advertised 0..5, absorbing the col-5 node, although 0..1 compiles
  current    -> advertised 0..1, col-5 node stays outside
```

That overreached *and* silently changed the unrelated node's context while claiming to keep members. The filter is now bounded by the authored span, which enforces the reviewer's suggested check by construction rather than re-testing each candidate: `minimumFrom` cannot drop below the lowest genuine member, `maximumTo` cannot rise above the highest, and the enumeration stays inside `group.toCol`.

A third regression case covers this shape and asserts the real member stays inside the span while the unrelated node stays outside. Reverting the filter makes it fail. The earlier two cases still pass.

### Third review round: a test that could not fail, and a shape with no repair

Two further findings, both addressed or answered:

- **[CodeRabbit](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239908689): one added assertion compiled a hard-coded span.** The first test applied `0..2` literally instead of the advertised span, so it could pass while the diagnostic offered something else. It now parses the advertised `fromCol`/`toCol` and applies those, as the two sibling tests already did — all three validate the repair actually offered to the user.
- **[Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4239908622): adding an unrelated node at col 0 to the single-column fixture still absorbs it.** Verified, and deliberately left unfixed. Every span that keeps the col-1 member also contains col 0, so no member-preserving repair exists for that shape; the search correctly returns no suggestion. Absorption here is also deliberate group semantics, not a side effect of the repair: `nodeContext()` derives membership from the column range, and the validator only requires a group to contain *some* node. Advertising such a span would be exactly the silent context change the finding objects to, so the code reports nothing instead. No change to group membership semantics was made.

### Fourth review round: a false repair I had argued was acceptable

[BlueboxC](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/issues/821#issuecomment-6194631942) independently ported this change and added a **membership-equality** check that this branch was missing. Verified against head `18c8e0ba`, the missing check was a real false repair:

```text
unrelated node at col 0 (left of the authored span)
   advertised: 0..1
   membership preserved? false
```

My earlier reply on that thread argued this shape had no repairable span and that returning nothing was therefore honest. The conclusion was right; the implementation did not reach it correctly. The filter limited which nodes could *derive* the span, but nothing rejected a **candidate** whose span moved the membership of same-lane nodes outside the authored range — so the repair shipped with a message claiming it "keeps its members" while doing the opposite.

The invariant is now explicit, adopted from that port:

```js
const movesMembership = asArray(workflow.nodes).some((node) => node.lane === group.lane
  && (node.col >= fromCol && node.col <= toCol)
    !== (node.col >= group.fromCol && node.col <= group.toCol));
if (movesMembership) continue;
```

This is the compiler's own notion of membership — `nodeContext()` selects a group by column range — so "unchanged membership" is the correct requirement rather than a stricter one.

| input | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unrelated node at col 0 | advertised `0..1`, membership changed | **no repair**, `blockedBy` still reported |
| no extra nodes / col 3 / col 5 | `0..1` | `0..1` (unchanged) |

Four regression cases now cover the repair: single-column group, rightmost-column member, span-outside node, and the withheld case (which asserts that any advertised span leaves membership identical to the authored one). Reverting the guard fails it. Credit to BlueboxC in the commit message and the thread.

### Fifth review round: overlapping groups reorder the resolved context

[Codex](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/838#discussion_r4284487287) found a further gap after the membership guard: with two **overlapping** groups in one lane, moving the edited group's `fromCol` can reorder them.

```text
command 1..1 overlapping other 0..1, same lane
  advertised: 0..1
  BEFORE: col-1 node resolves to: Other
  AFTER : col-1 node resolves to: Incident command
  RESOLUTION CHANGED? true
```

`nodeContext()` takes the first group whose range contains the node, with groups ordered by lane, then `fromCol`, then `toCol`, then `id`. Lowering `command.fromCol` to 0 sorts it ahead of `other`, so it takes over the node — while the edited group's own node set is unchanged, which is why the membership check could not see it.

The guard now compares the **resolved group per node** on both sides of the edit rather than membership, which subsumes the earlier check. Three of the five regression cases assert that **no** repair is offered, which is the honest answer whenever no span preserves context:

| input | advertised |
| --- | --- |
| overlapping groups | **none** |
| node immediately left of the span | **none** |
| node outside the span on the right | `0..1` |
| no extra nodes / plain fixture | `0..1` |

## Problem and value

Fixes #821.

A `workflow/route-preset-conflict` raised because a **scene label** blocks the only column an authored endpoint side can use currently publishes an empty `supportedFixes`:

```json
{
  "code": "workflow/route-preset-conflict",
  "message": "Workflow edge \"alert->page\" cannot satisfy route preset \"drop\": candidate violates lane/phase/group label clearance.",
  "supportedFixes": []
}
```

That is not an oversight in the existing search — it exhausts honestly. Instrumenting the rejection shows the blocker is a specific group label:

```text
BLOCKED-BY-SEGMENT seg=2
  obstacle = {"kind":"group-label","id":"command","x":174,"y":202,"width":89.6,"height":14}
  route    = [[94,145],[94,166],[214,166],[214,217]]
```

Segment 2 is the final vertical approach into the target node's **top** edge, and the group label `"Incident command"` spans exactly that column. Three consequences follow, all measured on `dev` @ `0b8f9f34`:

| authored change | result |
| --- | --- |
| `route` set to each of the other five presets | **all fail** (`orthogonal non-zero segments`, `perpendicular endpoint-side direction`) |
| `route` removed | fails as `workflow/explicit-pin-conflict` |
| every `fromSide`/`toSide` pairing | **all fail** |
| `page.width` widened to 132 | fails, same invariant |
| all lane labels shortened | fails, same invariant |
| **group `fromCol`/`toCol` narrowed off the target column** | **compiles** |
| group removed | compiles |
| target node moved to another column | compiles |

So no route-side repair exists, and the only authored field that does repair the document is the group's own placement. Meanwhile the enumeration *does* find a scene-clear route (`[[94,145],[764,145],[764,217],[214,217]]`) but correctly refuses it because it is an `outside-right` shape, not the authored `drop` preset family.

Value: the reporter of #821 — and two of the repository's own bundled v1 examples plus one baseline fixture, which cannot complete `migrate --to-schema 2` — currently receives an unactionable dead end. This change makes the failure self-repairing without touching how routes or labels are placed.

## Stability impact

- **Impact class:** Local behavior — one diagnostic path in the readable-v2 compiler (`CONTRIBUTING.md#choose-evidence-by-impact`). No layout, routing, clearance or geometry change; the same documents that compiled before compile now, and the same ones fail.
- **Changed behavior, two parts:**
  1. `workflow/route-preset-conflict` for the `lane/phase/group label clearance` invariant now carries **evidence**: `segmentIndex` and `blockedBy: { kind, id }`. This mirrors the existing evidence the same diagnostic already publishes for other invariants (`obstacleNode`, `labelRect`, `segmentIndex`, `actualSegmentPx`/`requiredSegmentPx`).
  2. When the blocker is a `group-label`, the diagnostic advertises the group placement that **verifies**, using the existing `verifiedEdgeFix`/`acceptsFix` machinery — the same mechanism that already gates the route-preset and label-segment repairs, so an unverified suggestion still cannot be published.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** when no repair verifies, `supportedFixes` stays empty exactly as before. The two existing tests that assert an empty `supportedFixes` array are for the `workflow/solver-budget-exhausted` and `explicit label-label clearance` invariants, which this change does not touch — both still pass.
- **Scope boundary, deliberately:** only `group-label` blockers are repaired. A `lane-header` or `phase-header` blocker needs different authored fields and is left to the existing behaviour rather than guessed at.
- **Compatibility / failure behavior:** no schema, default, exit-code or receipt-shape change. The diagnostic keeps its stable `code`, and the failure still exits non-zero.
- **Generated artifacts:** `archify.zip` **is** affected. `archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs` is packaged, and `scripts/ci-scope.mjs` does not match that path to a renderer/shared rule, so it falls through to `requireFull = true` and the `package` gate runs (the first CI run confirmed this: `zip-freshness` failed). The archive is refreshed in a follow-up commit — see below.

## Tests run

Comparison base `upstream/dev` @ `8072d6a2`; candidate head `68cb7418` (rebased onto current `dev` @ `8072d6a2`).

```sh
# Focused
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-migration.test.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-vertical-label.test.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-placed-label-evidence.test.mjs

# Regression proof: source fix reverted, new test kept
git checkout -- archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs
node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs --test-name-pattern='group label blocking'

# Full suite
npm run test:full
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression proof (fix reverted, test kept) | ✖ **fail 1** — the new test's `evidence.blockedBy` assertion fails |
| With the fix | ✔ passes |
| `test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs` (final head) | ✔ tests 103 / pass 103 / fail 0 |
| Review regression proof: source reverted to the first head's search | ✖ **fail 1** — the member-preserving test catches it |
| Review regression proof: member filter reverted | ✖ **fail 1** — the absorption test catches it |
| Review regression proof: membership guard reverted | ✖ **fail 1** — the withheld-repair test catches it |
| Review regression proof: context guard reverted | ✖ **fail 1** — the overlapping-group test catches it |
| `npm run test:full` (Chromium provided, final head) | ℹ tests 3527 / pass 3500 / fail 0 / cancelled 0 / skipped 27 / todo 0 — **exit 0** |

A pristine `upstream/dev` @ `0b8f9f34` checkout was measured beforehand for comparison: `tests 3235 / pass 3217 / fail 0 / skipped 18`. The candidate adds exactly three passing tests and introduces no failure.

The new regression test asserts the whole contract, not just the string: the invariant and `blockedBy` evidence, that **no** route-preset or route-removal fix is advertised for this shape, that the advertised group placement is present, and that **applying it compiles** (`ok: true`). Verifying the published fix independently outside the test — setting `groups[0].fromCol = 0`, `toCol = 2` — yields `ok=true` and a 786,517-byte render.

**Coverage gap, stated honestly:** the browser gate is exercised locally with a Chromium-based browser (Microsoft Edge) rather than Google Chrome, because Chrome is not installed on this host. This change is compiler-only and touches no Viewer/browser behaviour, so browser identity is not material to it; the full-suite run is done with Chromium available so the browser-conditional cases execute instead of skipping.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — diagnostic payload and repair discovery only; no rendered geometry changes.

## Generated artifacts

`archify.zip` is affected and was rebuilt in a follow-up commit, from the committed source, with the canonical toolchain (official Node **22.23.2**, bundled zlib **1.3.1-e00f703**; confirmed via `node -p 'process.versions.zlib'`).

- The same toolchain reproduces the **pristine `dev` archive byte-identically**, which validates both the toolchain and the comparison base before regenerating.
- The rebuild is deterministic (two consecutive builds byte-identical).
- Comparing archives entry by entry, the **only** entry whose bytes differ is `archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs`; the embedded copy matches `git show HEAD:archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs` exactly.
- The `zip-freshness` gate was simulated locally (`scripts/build-zip.sh` + `cmp`) and passes.

No other generated output is affected.

## Release follow-up

None — no version, tag, manifest, or distribution identity change.

Fixes #821

title: test(geometry): retain exact grid-boundary contact candidates
body:
## Problem and value

The shared spatial grid is a broad-phase candidate index for label placement. Its queries must retain geometry that touches a box at a cell boundary, including negative coordinates; otherwise exact downstream collision checks never see that obstacle. Existing tests cover multibucket lookup and overflow, but no zero-area contact query at an exact boundary. Add a small four-corner matrix across positive and negative cell origins.

## AI assistance and accountability

title: fix: tolerate Win32 link-count inflation in post-publication checks
body:
Fixes #474.

## Current base trigger

On Windows, `linkSync` + `unlinkSync` leaves the surviving name reporting **two** links even though only one name exists. The stale value is written to the directory entry, so it survives process exit, a reopened handle, and a rename round-trip — a fresh `fstatSync` in a brand-new process still reads `2`.

Because the inflation is indistinguishable from a genuine hard link when inspected from the outside, the publisher misreads names it created itself:

| Call | Expected | Actual on `dev` |
|---|---|---|
| `quarantineRemoveRegularFileBinding` (successor swapped) | `preserved` | `different` |
| `backupPublicRegularFileBinding` (successor swapped) | `preserved` | `different` |
| `verifyRegularFileBinding` (freshly linked name) | `match` | `unsupported` (`-hardlinked`) |

## Intended outcome

A name this module linked or renamed itself verifies as present even when Win32 overstates its link count, while any entry the caller did not create keeps failing closed.

The overstatement is one-directional: the count can only claim **more** names than exist, never fewer. So "at least as many links as expected" still proves the expected name is present — but only where this module knows how many names it created.

## Approach

`phase` is already the discriminator between the two situations, so the fix reuses it instead of threading a new flag through callers:

- `phase === 'verification'` re-reads a name this module just linked or renamed → tolerate an overcount.
- `phase === 'inspection'` reads an entry the caller did not create → read strictly, fail closed.

The two arithmetic checks in `quarantineRemoveRegularFileBinding`'s restore path are always post-own-link, so they tolerate unconditionally on Windows.

**No call sites change.** All 109 `verifyRegularFileBinding` / `quarantineRemoveRegularFileBinding` invocations and their `expectedLinks` arguments are untouched, so there is no per-site judgment to audit.

`nlink === 0` stays strict and is not platform-gated. Identity is still proven by `dev`+`ino` plus the content digest; `dev` and `ino` remain stable and distinct on Windows.

## Regression

`test/win32-link-count-publication.test.mjs` builds the inflation with a real `linkSync` + `unlinkSync` pair rather than mocking `fstatSync`, so it exercises the platform behaviour the fix exists for. It pins both halves of the contract:

| Test | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| a verified name keeps matching after its link count is inflated | **fail** | pass |
| a backup keeps its identity when the bound file reports an inflated count | **fail** | pass |
| quarantine removal restores a displaced name despite an inflated count | **fail** | pass |
| inspection of a pre-existing entry still fails closed on an inflated count | pass | pass |

The last row is the security guard: it passes on both sides, showing the strict path is not weakened.

## Baseline vs candidate

Run on Windows 11, Node v22.22.2, same five test files before and after:

| State | pass | fail |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` @ `603bbb4` | 49 | 46 |
| this branch | **57** | **38** |

Eight net tests fixed, none regressed. The six existing guard tests still pass, including `a hardlinked existing output is rejected before staging`, which `test/release-package-gates.test.mjs` writes into the release gate:

```
ok  a no-follow atomic output policy rejects special and hardlinked requested entries
ok  an existing output with handle link count 0 fails closed before staging
ok  an existing output with handle link count 2 fails closed before staging
ok  a path link count of one cannot hide a hardlinked handle identity
ok  a staged candidate whose handle has multiple links is not published
ok  a hardlinked existing output is rejected before staging
```

## Maintenance cost

The change adds one predicate (`linkCountMatches`) and one platform constant. It removes no branches and adds no configuration. The tolerance lives in the two functions that already own the link arithmetic, so it cannot drift out of sync with its callers.

## Affected shared callers

`linkCountMatches` is reached only through `inspectRegularFileDescriptor`, which is called by `captureRegularFileBinding` (`phase: 'inspection'`) and `verifyRegularFileBinding` (`phase: 'verification'`). Only the latter changes behaviour, and only on Windows.

## Scope note

This addresses the shared module. `archify/bin/*.mjs` has roughly thirty `captureRegularFileBinding(..., expectedLinks: 1)` calls inspecting entries the CLI itself created, and those hit the same artifact — an end-to-end `deliver` on Windows still reports `owned-delivery-journal-hardlinked`. That is a separate change because those sites are ownership assertions across a lock boundary, and widening them should be a deliberate decision rather than a side effect of this one. Evidence is on #474.

## Reproduction

```bash
node --test test/win32-link-count-publication.test.mjs
```

The first three tests fail on `dev` and pass here; without Windows the sequence is a no-op and all four pass.

body:
feat(viewer): add GIF motion export alongside WebM

Trace animations could only be exported as WebM, which requires browser
MediaRecorder support and produces a file many chat apps and doc
platforms will not preview inline. This adds GIF as a second motion
export target.

The per-frame capture setup is lifted out of recordWebm() into a shared
prepareMotionSession() that builds the static SVG background and the
authored edge/node signal scene once and hands back a draw(elapsed)
callback, so WebM and GIF sample the exact same scene and cannot drift
visually. Capability gating is split into motionTraceAvailable() (needs
only a trace animation) and canRecordMotion() (additionally needs
MediaRecorder), so GIF stays available in browsers that cannot write
WebM; unsupported menu entries degrade to a disabled tooltip.

recordGif() is a dependency-free GIF89a encoder: a 256-entry global
color table generated from a 6-7-6 uniform quantizer, then LZW
compression ported from gifenc's MIT-licensed encoder. No ffmpeg, no
npm, no Puppeteer.

Regenerates the checked-in example renders in both examples/ and
archify/examples/ plus examples/web-app.html so the golden suite stays
in sync.

Fixes #731

title: fix(output): require explicit replacement for unrelated HTML
body:
## Problem and value

Proposed implementation for #680. Current `dev` lets `render` and `deliver` replace an unrelated existing HTML file selected by `meta.output`, returning success. This draft supplies a working, tested proposal for the replacement policy before finalizing the compatibility contract.

### Proposed recognition and consent rule

- A positional CLI output path is explicit replacement intent. No new flag or interactive prompt is needed.
- Implicit output can create a new file or regenerate an existing document with recognized Archify generator metadata, primary SVG accessibility markup, and the same diagram title. Node/relationship/style edits remain convenient.
- Otherwise fail with `output/replacement-required` and suggest a new path or an explicit output argument. Refusal preserves the existing HTML; initial delivery refusal creates no provenance/journal/lock side effects.
- Apply the shared guard to direct renderers, `render`, `deliver` and `preview`, including their existing pre-publication path rechecks. Preview reuses the title it last successfully published so edits within one session keep working, and refuses unrelated content placed at its output between generations.

**Decision requested before promoting this draft:** is generator + primary-SVG markup + same title an acceptable regeneration heuristic, and is the existing positional CLI output sufficient replacement consent? This does not prove source-file identity: distinct Archify inputs with the same title can match. Renaming a diagram between invocations, unrecognized legacy/custom templates, or files above a 64 MiB recognition budget require explicit output selection. If stronger source identity is wanted, that needs a separate agreed representation rather than silently adding machine-dependent paths or new sidecars to every artifact.

## Stability impact

- Impact: shared behavior and output-acceptance contract change. Existing schema-v1 validation is unchanged, including required `meta.output`; the shared resolver's default branch is guarded where supported, without making missing authored output valid.
- Existing explicit-output, extension, input-alias, hard-link, target-change, atomic publication and delivery ownership controls remain active. The policy does not sandbox explicit CLI directories.
- Recognition is conservative and ignores marker text in comments/scripts. It is a prevention mechanism for accidental replacement, not authentication or protection against deliberately imitated Archify markup.
- No renderer geometry, HTML template, schema, version or generated example changes. Output HTML bytes stay identical; no new ownership metadata or sidecar is emitted.

## Tests run

Base: `68b77b73eaf12297356d122968d9b7b8767be278` (`dev`). Candidate: `6803a71d5c3aaf26dcd69ee7f7fb36ce60a4dbd2`.

Revision from `220b187`: removed the locale-catalog import from the standalone path-safety runtime after CI exposed missing dependencies in minimal delivery/compare and archive-build fixtures. HTML escaping remains equivalent, with quoted titles now included in the behavioral fixture. Rebuilt the ZIP. The 21 behavioral tests pass again both in the checkout and extracted ZIP; the previously failing standalone archive/unmerged-index gate also passes locally. Wider compatibility/golden evidence below was collected on `220b187`; those tests have not been relabeled as new-head results. Final-head remote CI passed; links and coverage follow.

- Reproduced silent replacement by both public `render` and `deliver` against unchanged output-related code from the base, using synthetic HTML in a temporary directory. Added failing regressions before implementation.
- `node --test test/implicit-output-replacement.test.mjs`: **21 passed**, zero failures/skips, official Node 22.23.2. Covers all ten diagram types' byte-identical regeneration, refusal/explicit replacement, different titles, metadata preservation, escaped titles, disguised marker text, default resolver selection, preview startup, live title edits and an unrelated file placed between preview generations.
- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/implicit-output-replacement.test.mjs test/meta-output-contract.test.mjs test/renderer-atomic-write.test.mjs test/preview-contract.test.mjs test/native-output-path.test.mjs`: **68 passed, 12 platform skips, 2 failed** before adding the ten-mode cases. Both failures occur while setting up Windows symlinks (`EPERM`) and reproduce using the unchanged base package/test.
- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/output-path.test.mjs test/preview.test.mjs`: **47 passed, 10 platform skips, 14 failed**. The unchanged base package reproduces 12 symlink-setup `EPERM` failures (49 passed, 10 skips). The other two were null child-process statuses; both passed in a focused rerun without code changes. These local environment/transient limitations are not claimed as a green full suite.
- `node test/golden.mjs`: all maintained output/schema checks passed.
- Generated-validator, Viewer, brand-catalogue and release-identity freshness checks, plus `git diff --check`: passed.
- Extracted ZIP outside the checkout without installing dependencies: `node scripts/package-smoke.mjs <extracted>/archify` passed, and all 21 replacement/preview/diagram-mode behavior regressions passed on `6803a71`.

Full local `npm test` and manual browser/perceptual review were not run. Final-head [CI](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37340095719) passed on `6803a71d5c3aaf26dcd69ee7f7fb36ce60a4dbd2`: full Node 18/20/22/24 test lanes, Windows Node 22/24 path contracts, three-platform package smoke, ZIP freshness, update-manifest checks, real WebM decoding and shared browser regression gate. [DSH package and distribution acceptance](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37340095741) also passed on that head. Unrelated website/adapter-release jobs were skipped by workflow conditions. Local Windows limitations above remain explicit. CodeRabbit skips automatic draft review; its green status is not a completed code review.

- Rebuilt `archify.zip` using official Node 22.23.2 / bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`. SHA-256: `e355343fdd23b4c9cbae3e71629061a1ab19449806708c7afe07a8ecb27b0baa`.
- ZIP entry list is identical to the base. Only the four changed runtime modules and `references/delivery-contract.md` differ inside it. Tests remain outside the installable Skill.
