title: feat(levels): add C4 leveled architecture generation
body:
## Problem and value

Current-main trigger or rationale, intended outcome, why the approach is worth maintaining, and linked issue/agreed scope:

This adds C4 leveled architecture generation. Archify can already draw one architecture diagram. It cannot yet generate the C4 set: the same system at several depths, with a way to move from one drawing to the next.

C4 is not one diagram that grows. It is the same system drawn several times, each time at a closer zoom: Context (people and systems), Containers (deployable applications and data stores), Components (the insides of one container), and optionally Code. A box on one drawing is the title of the next drawing. You do not expand a node in place; you open the next diagram.

That is also the only shape that fits Archify. Expand-in-place nesting needs a layout solver, which `ROADMAP.md` declines, because the hand-placed coordinates are the product. A single architecture canvas is capped at about 14 components by the showcase readability floor (6px projected node text at a 1440×620 reading width), so a full C4 model does not fit on one canvas anyway.

What generation looks like after this change:

- Ask for a C4 model, or for a system that will not fit one canvas. `archify guide` routes that to a new `c4-levels` recipe.
- Each level is generated as an ordinary architecture diagram, with its own coordinates and cards, and is validated on its own. Context, Containers, and Components are separate files. Code, if you want it, is another architecture drawing, not a new renderer.
- A `diagram_type: "levels"` document binds those files into one artifact. It is a document, not a sixth diagram type, and it owns no geometry. Nothing reflows. A level's SVG inside the combined artifact is byte-identical to that level rendered standalone.
- The link is declared on the child: "Containers opens from the `platform` node on Context." The parent file is not edited, so an existing diagram can be reused as a level. The checked-in proof binds the existing web-app example as the container level.
- In the viewer, a node opens the next drawing. It does not grow into it. One click on the magnifier badge drills in; the zoom-out control, a crumb, or Escape goes back; `#level=<id>` opens on that level.

There is no agreed upstream issue for this. The non-goals are the scope proposal: no expand-in-place nesting, no cross-level automatic layout, no sixth row in the five-type tables, and no level source other than `diagram_type: "architecture"`. This branch is already merged with current `main`, including the reader shell that no longer ships guided views. Levels do not put that UI back. Per-level `meta.views`, when authored, travel in the levels manifest only.

Happy to move this to an issue first if you want the contract agreed before review.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: Contract change, plus shared viewer and artifact-check behavior. New schema (`schemas/levels.schema.json`), cross-file validation (`renderers/shared/levels-document.mjs`), `levels` on the render/validate/deliver/preview/doctor CLI paths, Skill and authoring instructions, and the shared viewer template. `check-render-output` inspects every SVG in a levels artifact. `Archify.stage` is the active canvas for export, finder, radar, focus, routes, and motion. Listeners bind to the stage container so a level swap does not drop them.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior:
  - Existing schema-v1 documents for the five diagram types stay valid. No migration. Each architecture level must set `meta.output`, which current `main` already requires.
  - A level that would fail on its own fails the document. Diagnostics are reported together, re-scoped onto the manifest entry when the failure is inside a level file. Codes are listed in `archify/schemas/README.md`.
  - Exactly one root. Every other level names the parent level and the component it drills out of, that component must exist, one child per node, no cycles, no unreachable levels. Sources stay inside the manifest directory, including through symlinks.
  - Single-diagram artifacts keep their historical check names. A levels document runs that per-SVG suite for every level, plus `levels_identified` and `levels_single_active`. `archify guide` gains the `c4-levels` recipe, so the recipe count on this head is 13, including the existing layout-repair recipe.
  - Author CSS outranks the user-agent `[hidden]` rule. Inactive level SVGs, cards, and the rail restate `display: none`. Inactive SVGs are written `hidden="hidden"` so the embedded SVG stays well-formed XML.
  - Export serializes the visible level, not the first SVG in the file. Drill markup (`data-drill-to`, the magnifier badge, level identity attributes) is stripped from the export.
  - Drill affordance: a magnifier badge in the node's top-right corner, placed from the authored rectangle. One click on the badge drills; a plain click on the node body is still focus. Double-click and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter still drill. A child level shows an inset frame and a zoom-out control that names the parent.

## Tests run

Comparison base and candidate head; applicable commands/results or evidence links. Identify reused evidence by its original revision and explain material coverage gaps. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md#choose-evidence-by-impact; required remote CI still applies.

- Comparison base: `upstream/main` at `d5a1333` (`docs: refresh WeChat group QR code`). Candidate head: `997ecb3` on `milan-lf/archify`.
- On that head:
  - `node --test archify/test/levels-document.test.mjs` → 17 pass
  - `node --test archify/test/levels-render.test.mjs` → 11 pass
  - `node --test archify/test/guide.test.mjs` → pass, including 13 recipes
- `npm test` was not run on `997ecb3`. `archify/test/levels-browser.test.mjs` was not re-run after the reader-shell merge. Required CI on the PR head should close that gap.
- An earlier full suite, from before this upstream merge, was 1465 pass and 1 fail. The failure was `compare rechecks every target immediately before committing the artifact pair` in `archify/test/output-path.test.mjs`, and it also failed on pristine `main` at that older base. That result is not evidence for `997ecb3`.

## Visual evidence

- Evidence provided: Render `archify/examples/web-platform.levels.json`. The root level is the Context drawing. The magnifier badge on the platform node opens the container level, which is the existing web-app diagram bound in unmodified. The zoom-out control, an ancestor crumb, and Escape return. `#level=<id>` opens on that level. Export downloads the level on screen. No screenshots are attached.
- Comparison conditions: desktop, default light theme, overview zoom. The intended difference from a standalone architecture HTML file is the rail, badge, inset frame, and zoom-out control. Level geometry is not intended to move; the byte-identical SVG claim is what `levels-render.test.mjs` locks.
- Automated or browser checks: the render and document tests above. The real-browser drill test was not re-run on this head.
- Perceptual visual review: skipped. Checked-in gallery HTML that conflicted with upstream was kept from upstream and has not been rebuilt on this head, so it is not the visual proof.

## Generated artifacts

`archify/assets/template.html` was regenerated from `viewer/template.source.html` after the levels rail, drill CSS, `Archify.stage`, and `<!-- ARCHIFY:LEVELS_DATA -->` placeholder were added to the current reader shell.

`archify/renderers/shared/generated-validators.mjs` was regenerated so `levels` is included.

These were not rebuilt on `997ecb3` and should be before review: the proof gallery, `docs/guide.html`, example HTML that embeds the viewer, `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.gif`, and `archify.zip`. Conflicted copies of those files were taken from upstream during the sync.

`CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased and `ROADMAP.md` describe the document. Both READMEs and both cookbooks point at leveled architecture generation without adding a sixth row to the type tables.

The Chinese copy in the scenario recipe, the gallery case, `README_ZH.md`, and `docs/authoring-cookbook.zh-CN.md` is a first draft and needs a native review. The weighted signal terms in the recipe decide how Chinese `archify guide` requests route, so that review is behavioral, not only prose.

title: fix(workflow): declare authored-height contract for explicit viewBox swimlanes (#616)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #616.

Per `references/delivery-contract.md`, document-level vertical scrolling is accepted by `visual-check` only with an explicit renderer contract. Previously, automatic canvases declared `data-reader-fit="intrinsic-height"`, and architecture diagrams with an explicit `meta.viewBox` declared `data-diagram-type="architecture" data-reader-fit="authored-height"`.

However, the workflow compiler emitted no `data-reader-fit` attribute when an explicit `meta.viewBox` was supplied. For tall multi-lane swimlane diagrams (e.g. 6 lanes × 5 phases with an authored height > 800px), `visual-check` reported `overflowDisposition: "unexpected-overflow"`, failing containment at standard viewports (1440×900, 1600×1000, 1920×1080) despite the layout being valid and readable with normal page scrolling.

## The change

1. **Workflow Compiler (`workflow-compiler.mjs`)**:
   - Emits `data-diagram-type="workflow" data-reader-fit="authored-height"` on `<svg>` when an explicit `meta.viewBox` is present on tall swimlanes (multi-lane or height > 800).
2. **Visual Check & Desktop Readability (`visual-check.mjs`, `desktop-readability.mjs`)**:
   - Extends the `authored-height` vertical-scroll acceptance to both `architecture` and `workflow` diagrams when `documentScrollUnclipped` holds.
   - Updates failure diagnostic messages to correctly name Workflow vs Architecture when clipped.
3. **Delivery Contract Documentation (`delivery-contract.md`)**:
   - Documents that both architecture and workflow diagrams with explicit viewBox declare `authored-height`.

## Verification

- `node --test test/delivery-contract.test.mjs test/layout-rules.test.mjs test/render-output-checks.test.mjs`: All 199 tests pass (0 failures).
- `desktop-reader-browser.test.mjs`: Added regression test verifying a rendered workflow with explicit `meta.viewBox: [1240, 838]` delivers with `authored-height` and passes `visual-check` containment with `verticalScrollAccepted: true`.

title: feat(workflow): add configurable typography with measured layout
body:
## Problem and value

Refs #631 and its [agreed scope](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/issues/631#issuecomment-5905457102). Current `dev` still lacks a generated text/layout proportion control beyond Viewer camera zoom. This adds optional Workflow v2 `meta.typography_scale` (1–2), measuring nodes, lane/group/phase headings, relationship labels and legends together. Omitted or explicit `1` preserves current-base output.

The maintainer supported this direction and requested source-aware automatic capacity and repair-probe fixes. Both fixes and their public-CLI regressions are retained in the current synchronized head.

## Stability impact

- **Contract/shared behavior:** Workflow v2 only; v1 rejects the option. Authored dimensions, viewBox and absolute routing remain authoritative. No new option for other diagram types.
- Merged current `dev` `0bd659b8` without rewriting PR history. Preserved its automatic-width/readability feedback, phase chips, default-edge contrast, measured failure receipts and routing/placement repairs. Source evidence and resolved brand metadata survive repair probes, including the new upstream probe paths.
- Shared legend measurement uses the rendered font once; default behavior matches dev. The typography browser suite is appended to the new shared browser inventory.
- PR improvement check: applied project **test-value** and scoped **simplify-codebase** survey. Reused upstream `workflowNodeTextProblems` and `measuredPlanReceipt` instead of retaining parallel implementations. The existing brand-context helper remains necessary because JSON probe clones discard Symbol metadata. No supported path was removed and no broader refactor is needed.
- Typography entries now sit under Unreleased, not the already-published 3.1.0 section. Installation, environment configuration and release identity are unchanged.

## Tests run

Base: `0bd659b89dc836144c92ddcfef747a0ee8490b8d`.
Runtime/tests/ZIP merge: `5876e8259e05ba1a0f30c69114616565184eb00b`.
Head: `baf73e81fdb25fd59d3f9c2c1c61215aee86e8a4` (adds evidence only).

[Revision-pinned evidence, measurements, comparison hashes and reproduction commands](https://github.com/To3akaRin/archify/blob/baf73e81fdb25fd59d3f9c2c1c61215aee86e8a4/docs/evidence/workflow-typography/dev-sync-20261015/README.md).

macOS, official Node 22.23.1 / zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`, Chrome 155.0.8059.79:

- `npm run test:full`: **3,100 passed, 0 failed, 115 skipped** (optional browser/platform conditions; skips are not passes). Generated checks and golden checks passed.
- Current `npm test` is core smoke only: **18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Typography/compiler/legend/routing/inventory focused group: **235 passed**; upstream layout/repair compatibility group: **35 passed**. The final combined typography/placement/width/crossing group after the last probe adjustment: **54 passed**, including the two new cases. These groups overlap; counts are not added.
- Real Chrome typography, maintained reader and edge-label contrast: **10 passed, no skips**. The later probe-only adjustment does not change the captured successful rendering paths; final full and focused runs cover that adjustment.
- **16/16 fixed inputs across ten diagram types:** public validate/render succeeds on base and candidate; complete HTML and SVG bytes are identical with omitted typography. Frozen SVG expectations were refreshed from the independently rendered current dev, not candidate output alone.
- Repeated canonical ZIPs are byte-identical; the extracted 155-file package passes macOS smoke outside the repository. Source/test/document whitespace checks pass.

Test-value rationale: retained public-CLI source/brand capacity and executable-fix replay rather than adding helper mocks. Reused the upstream fixed-v1 cache regression, which caught and prevented a merge regression. Two added combination cases protect scaled output/readable styling with same-object edits, and source/brand retention when replaying an upstream placement repair. They assert user-visible output and successful replay, not private call counts or fixed automatic coordinates.

Final-head [CI run 38666252006](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/38666252006) **passed** on `baf73e81`: all 19 executing jobs succeeded, including both full-regression and browser shards, Windows portability, three-platform package smoke, ZIP freshness and website checks. Cloudflare/Pages deployments were skipped by the workflow. Maintainer re-review remains pending. CodeRabbit could not recover its old incremental checkpoint; a fresh full review was explicitly triggered and is pending. Earlier CI and screenshots retain their original revision labels and are not reported as final-head results.

An independent narrow review of `baf73e81` found no blocker in typography/legend integration, source/brand repair probes, automatic-width caching or authored-geometry preservation. Its additional read-only ordinary-fixture checks at scales 1, 1.01, 1.5 and 2 confirmed unchanged input and receipt/SVG agreement; this is scoped supplementary evidence, not another full-suite run.

## Visual evidence

[Current screenshots and raw browser measurements](https://github.com/To3akaRin/archify/blob/baf73e81fdb25fd59d3f9c2c1c61215aee86e8a4/docs/evidence/workflow-typography/dev-sync-20261015/README.md#视觉观察).

Automated coverage includes 1440×900 and 1920×1080, light/dark, source/brand decorations, focus/source access and tag visibility. Perceptual review inspected five 1440×900 Classic/100%-zoom screenshots: ordinary and dense scale-1/1.5 pairs, plus source+brand scale 2 dark. No clipping or label/decoration overlap was observed in that subset.

Dense visible caption minimum increases from 9.72px to 15.98px at scale 1.5. Larger typography uses more vertical space; it is not a universal first-screen or minimum-screen-font guarantee. Other cases have automated evidence rather than exhaustive perceptual acceptance.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated all ten validators and rebuilt `archify.zip` from the combined source. SHA-256: `98cc2f8929746c33e638d367363b9d1c564f4adf9458acc56531f489aa0adb73`.

Existing Gallery inputs do not opt into scaling and default outputs match dev, so unrelated Gallery outputs were not regenerated. Historical evidence remains intact; new evidence stays outside the Skill ZIP.

title: feat(sequence): support self-messages
body:
## Problem and value

On `dev` at `500d4a65211ffe607fde6b3ce7505027b45bb59e`, schema-v1 accepts matching message endpoints but Sequence rejects them as `sequence/self-message-unsupported`. This PR draws an orthogonal loop for internal processing while preserving ownership, order, wording and relationship identity. Closes #570; follows the [maintainer's agreed scope](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/571#issuecomment-5908329119).

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: OpenAI Codex assisted investigation, implementation, conflict resolution, tests, artifact inspection and PR writing. Exact model identifier is unavailable.
- Accountable contributor: @Laurie-Lin.
- Problem origin: the self-message capability requested in #570; constructed examples exercise its agreed behavior and failure boundaries. These examples are synthetic, not reported production sessions.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

Human confirmation is left unchecked pending the contributor's personal confirmation. Automated results and agent inspection do not imply human acceptance.

## Stability impact

Local Sequence geometry and its authoring instructions; no schema, shared geometry-helper or Viewer source changes relative to the comparison base. Loops turn right by default and inward for the rightmost participant. Active-profile text width, the complete return leg and wrapped notes inform lane clearance and automatic sizing. Schema-v1 still requires at least two participants. Invalid layouts retain structured diagnostics and non-zero exits; suggested edits are withheld when they would put either horizontal leg on a phase border.

The new merge commit `48ec9db0ac11fe7826ea71f9e6de1d4f258fa0f8` integrates current dev without rewriting prior commits. Conflict resolution retains upstream Read-visible notes, phase-border backdrops, Han wrapping, participant drilldowns and current Viewer/motion contracts while preserving loop paths and inward note alignment. The changelog entry stays in Unreleased; the canonical archive was rebuilt.

Scoped test-value / simplicity review reused the existing note wrapper, backdrop and collision rules. The existing left/right self-note test now protects context visibility and the phase-border backdrop. No new routing subsystem or parallel note implementation was added. Tests cover meaningful text, direction, ownership, failure cleanup and valid repairs rather than freezing automatic canvas choices.

## Tests run

Comparison base: `500d4a65211ffe607fde6b3ce7505027b45bb59e` (`dev`). Candidate: `48ec9db0ac11fe7826ea71f9e6de1d4f258fa0f8`. Official Node 22.23.2 / bundled zlib 1.3.1-e00f703, macOS.

New local runs against the merged source:

- Focused Sequence self-message, note-wrap, column-fit and segment-label suites: 81 passed, 0 failed.
- Affected sequence/authoring and shared regressions: 898 passed, 0 failed, 7 optional browser skips; separate real-Chrome coverage is tracked below.
- Core smoke: 19 passed, 0 failed.
- Generated/golden checks, canonical ZIP independent byte reproduction and extracted-package macOS smoke: passed.
- Five delivered candidate examples, their four-viewport browser visual checks, relationship inspection and complete light/dark SVG/PNG exports: passed. The ordinary fixture's candidate/dev HTML is byte-identical.
- Complete local Chrome gate: 310 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40479511330) completed successfully on `48ec9db0`, including full regression, both real-browser shards, maintained Node versions, Windows portability, ZIP freshness and three-platform package smoke. Deployment jobs were appropriately skipped for this fork PR. These are new-head results, not reused prior-head checks.

## Visual evidence

Fresh comparison uses the same five inputs on current dev, candidate and released v3.0.1 (`2ab3cae7`): minimal loop, consecutive loops, mixed ordinary/self calls, long label/wrapped note and ordinary messages. The four loop inputs fail on both baselines with actual receipts. Ordinary messages succeed on all three; differences from v3.0.1 include upstream Viewer and note changes.

The ordinary sample's authored width changed from historical 1100px to 1080px for all three versions: current dev makes its 7px note Read-visible, so 1100px fails the current desktop text floor on both dev and candidate. Topology, y positions, text and notes are unchanged; no product threshold was relaxed.

Fresh automated checks: 1440×900, 1600×1000, 1920×1080 and 2048×1320; light/dark, Classic, Still, Read, initial 100%. Current notes are visible in Read; Map hides them without reflow. Complete exports retain every wrapped note line. Agent image inspection of the three representative light/dark export pairs found no clipping, incorrect loop direction or label/note collisions. Maintainer visual acceptance remains pending.

title: feat(validate): expose informational viewport projection
body:
Closes #358.

@tt-a1i @ljcjeans-dev This implements the bounded informational path discussed in #358 without turning projected viewport geometry into a new validation gate.

## Problem and value

A candidate can pass static `validate` checks while still reaching `visual-check` with a whole-page viewport problem.

The repository already had most of the underlying desktop Reader model in `desktop-readability.mjs`, including `predictedFixedWidthOverflow()`, but that evidence was not surfaced through the public validation receipt.

This change connects that existing contract to `validate --json`.

The intended boundary is deliberately conservative:

- `certain-overflow` is emitted only when the shared static Reader rules can prove that the page already exceeds the 1440x900 desktop reference viewport before card height is counted.
- `undetermined` means static analysis cannot establish either fit or overflow because adaptive Reader sizing, card wrapping, and browser layout still matter.
- Neither status changes validation success, candidate freezing, exit status, or the existing `finalize` handoff.
- Browser evidence remains authoritative through `finalize` and `visual-check`.

This follows the maintainer direction in #358 to make better use of existing measurements, keep any projection informational, and state its assumptions rather than creating another acceptance gate.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared CLI receipt behavior backed by the existing desktop-readability contract.
- Passing `validate --json` receipts may now include an additive `viewportProjection` field.
- Existing schema-v1 input remains unchanged.
- Existing validation acceptance is unchanged.
- `candidateFrozen` and `nextAction` behavior are unchanged.
- Human-mode validate output is unchanged.
- No renderer geometry, topology, Viewer interaction, export format, schema, default, or quality threshold changes.

The projection records:

- target reference viewport;
- authored/rendered viewBox dimensions;
- Reader fit declaration;
- whether guided-view chrome contributes to the lower bound;
- whether browser measurement or card wrapping was included;
- projected SVG height and fixed chrome when a certain overflow can be proven;
- a lower-bound overflow amount and actionable guidance.

While wiring this path, the existing `predictedFixedWidthOverflow()` result contract was also completed so that `describeFixedWidthOverflow()` receives the authored `viewBoxWidth` and `viewBoxHeight` it already expects. Regression coverage prevents the previous `undefinedxundefined` guidance path from becoming observable.

## Tests run

Comparison base:

`629155a47cd5b487cb5a6e322b2ca71998698aaf`

Candidate:

`e7f16aef1feff4e3917b895d70a0f03798bcc1b8`

Final fork validation:

https://github.com/julianvanceblackwood/archify/actions/runs/36128590434

Passed on the exact final candidate:

- Node 18 full suite
- Node 20 full suite
- Node 22 full suite
- Node 24 full suite
- shared browser regression / WebM gate
- ZIP freshness
- website checks
- package smoke on Ubuntu
- package smoke on macOS
- package smoke on Windows
- scope classification

Focused regression coverage also verifies:

- authored viewBox dimensions survive the shared overflow projection contract;
- actionable guidance contains concrete dimensions rather than undefined values;
- intrinsic-height Reader cases remain outside the certain-overflow path;
- a real Lifecycle candidate can emit `certain-overflow` while `validate` still succeeds and freezes the candidate;
- a case that static rules cannot prove emits `undetermined` rather than claiming a pass;
- the receipt explicitly records that browser measurement and card wrapping were not performed.

The fork-only `published-update-manifest` check cannot resolve the upstream published Release from `julianvanceblackwood/archify`, and the two Windows portability jobs intentionally reject the fork origin when fixtures expect `tt-a1i/archify`. Those are repository-context checks rather than failures introduced by this change. The upstream PR run is the authoritative execution context for those gates.

## Generated artifacts

`archify.zip` was regenerated from the final combined source with the repository's canonical Node 22 deterministic builder.

ZIP freshness passes on the exact final candidate.

No Gallery, Viewer, start-page, schema, or example source changed, so no unrelated generated artifact was rebuilt.

body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #564.

A valid sequence diagram can pass delivery gates while its first segment heading is drawn beneath a participant header. This is observable in the small public reproduction in #564 and in the first headings of the bundled cache-miss/async-job examples.

Keep the existing message-avoidance placement, then relocate only a heading that overlaps participant headers into a free upward slot. Reserve all other segment headings as well, so fixing one overlap cannot create a title-to-title overlap. Rendering and validation share the computed boxes.

## Stability impact

- Shared sequence renderer; only generated label placement changes. Authored segment bounds, message coordinates, participant geometry, wording, and font size remain unchanged.
- Already-clear headings stay put. A fully occupied top rail retains legacy placement/acceptance instead of moving text off-canvas or introducing a new schema-v1 rejection. This is a bounded fix, not a general packing algorithm.
- No new schema, hard gate, routing rule, or live installation change. Independent from workflow #565 / #567.

## Tests run

Comparison base: dev `629155a47cd5b487cb5a6e322b2ca71998698aaf`. Native Windows, Node 22.22.3, real Chrome 153.

- Valid-input baseline: **12/12 geometry cases fail** on the obscured heading. Candidate: **14 new regression cases pass**, including message displacement, reserved neighboring titles, exhausted top rail, standard/showcase and fixed/spread columns.
- New regression plus existing column-fit coverage: **22/22 pass**.
- Existing real-Chrome header-clearance suite extended with a segment heading: **pass, no skip**, across 12 viewport/theme/zoom combinations.
- Public CLI `finalize sequence` and all four `visual-check` captures: pass.

The same dev base has confirmed Windows filesystem/test-environment failures (recovery/staging path assumptions, unavailable symlink privileges, short-path and Git fixture differences). No unrelated product/test workaround is included. Complete required CI results remain authoritative and must finish before merge.

title: fix(workflow): reserve heading clearance for inferred straight ports
body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #565.

The current dev compiler rejects an ordinary same-column straight route across two lanes when its inferred top endpoint runs through a lane heading. Adding the redundant `toSide: "top"` (or `fromSide` for an upward edge) makes the same input work: the layout prepass reserved heading clearance only for explicitly authored top ports.

Reserve that same existing clearance for the forced facing ports of unpinned, same-column straight routes. This fixes layout planning at its owner instead of relaxing the collision gate or adding an authoring workaround.

## Stability impact

- Shared workflow-v2 compiler layout; deliberately limited to `route: "straight"`, distinct lanes, same column, compatible direction constraints, and diagrams without absolute coordinate pins.
- Explicit sides, absolute `via`/`channelX`/`channelY`/`labelAt` pins, collision checks, schema, and already-clear layouts are preserved. No generic routing-policy change.
- 17 existing workflow inputs in two quality profiles produce identical SVG/receipts/diagnostics versus dev (34 comparisons; 32 successful renders and two identical pre-existing `release-luna` rejections).
- Independent from the sequence heading issue #564; no dependency or merge order.

## Tests run

- `node archify/test/golden.mjs`: **29/29 pass**; `git diff --check`: pass.

title: fix(architecture): preserve semantics and reject perimeter detours
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

A fresh Agent using the dev Skill could draw a technically misleading architecture diagram while `finalize` passed: a JSON specification or Markdown task file appeared as a database; the deliver/check order could be reversed; and a Worker report route could frame the whole drawing to avoid one crossing. This PR makes Architecture artifacts a first-class component kind, strengthens the source-tracing guidance, and rejects a broad perimeter detour in showcase validation. A fresh Agent is directed to reflow a connected feedback cycle and to trace actor → transport → handler → executor, including the report path and Runtime-owned PTY delivery.

The file/artifact kind is confined to Architecture. Existing diagram modes and legacy inputs retain their contracts. Viewer, legend, overview map, Semantic Lens, and Node Finder all render the artifact consistently.

## Real-use evidence and limits

Two ordinary Chinese Skill tasks used frozen repositories and fresh GPT-6 Sol medium Agents, with full trajectories and artifact snapshots:

- Archify self-project: the main/dev baseline needed three `finalize` attempts and mislabeled specification/output files. The earlier candidate passed on its first candidate and first `finalize`, with a clean 1440×900 composition and no blocking source-audit finding. This is one matched observation, not a general speed result.
- Hive local-collaboration architecture: main took 164.4 s end to end and mislabeled `.hive/tasks.md` as a database while omitting part of the team return path. Candidate v1 took 282.1 s; despite passing gates, its report edge looped around the scene. After diagnosis, the narrow detour check and authoring guidance were tested through fresh Agents. Candidate v5 took 193.8 s, needed two repairs, passed all four `finalize` gates and the browser visual check, and has no ordinary route crossing or broad perimeter loop. Independent source review found no blocking factual mismatch in its local scope. Two small semantic caveats remain: “stopped means queued” is too absolute for newly spawned Workers, and direct edits to the shared task file are not drawn. This sample does **not** establish an end-to-end speedup over main.

Agent trajectories indicate that repository exploration and first-draft composition, rather than the few-second `finalize` calls, dominate this Hive task. The change targets correct first construction and earlier diagnosis of the visible detour; it does not claim a general performance win. Local experiment receipts and screenshots are under `/tmp/archify-real-use-20260924/hive-matched/`, summarized in `experiment-summary.md` there. The self-project evidence is under `/Users/tushaokun/tdoc/archify-quality-review-20260924/natural-use/native-23-sol-self/`.

## Validation

- Full local Node 22 suite after the route change: 2,341 tests, 2,258 passed, 0 failed, 83 skipped. A post-documentation targeted rerun: 60 tests, 58 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
- New regression reproduces the Hive v1 perimeter route: `composition/excessive-route-detour` now rejects it; the existing legitimate shorter outer-route fixture still passes.
- `archify.zip` rebuilt with the same official Node 22.23.2/zlib 1.3.1 toolchain as CI; SHA-256 `500fef3bdfea0650d512890cdbd071a4e03e9a3ef50a084cb96d46a3b7b5b56e`. The frozen v5 test ZIP was produced by Homebrew Node 22/zlib 1.2.12; all 93 extracted entries are byte-identical. `git diff --check` passed.

Final-head GitHub Actions CI passed for Node 18/20/22/24, Windows portability, package smoke on macOS/Ubuntu/Windows, WebM, website, and ZIP freshness. CodeRabbit skipped review because this PR is Draft.

This PR remains Draft against `dev` for local trial. It has **not** been merged into `dev` or `main`.

title: feat: support nested boundaries via wraps referencing boundary id
body: ## Problem and value Boundaries could only group components in a single flat level — `boundaries[].wraps` accepted component ids only, so there was no way to declare that one boundary lives inside another. Anyone modeling a layered system (a subsystem inside a larger service, a security-group inside a region) had no way to express that nesting explicitly; the only way to get a visually-nested result was to accidentally overlap two boundaries' component lists, which states nothing about the intended hierarchy. This closes the nesting half of #410 ("embedded functions/systems within systems"). The connection-endpoint half of that issue (#284) is being handled separately in #317 and is not touched here. Agreed scope (from discussion on #410): `wraps` may reference another boundary's own `id`, nesting is capped at 2 levels (outer -> inner -> components) for this first version, and a worked example belongs in the docs. All three are included. ## Stability impact - **Impact class:** additive schema/renderer change to the architecture diagram type only (`schemas/architecture.schema.json`, `renderers/architecture/render-architecture.mjs`, `renderers/shared/engineering-profiles.mjs`). No other diagram type (workflow/sequence/dataflow/lifecycle) is touched. - **Changed behavior:** `boundaries[].wraps` now also accepts a boundary's own `id` (previously component-ids only); `boundaries[].id` is a new optional field; `componentContext()` now reports the full ancestor chain for a component nested under more than one boundary. - **Existing behavior preserved:** a `wraps` list containing only component ids behaves exactly as before — same geometry, same validation. The existing implicit/accidental-overlap nesting pattern (two boundaries independently listing overlapping components) is untouched and still works. - **Intended compatibility changes:** none that affect existing valid documents — the new behavior only activates when a `wraps` entry matches another boundary's `id`, which no existing document can already be doing (the field didn't exist before). - **Failure behavior:** new, explicit validation errors for cases that were previously either impossible or silently wrong: nesting depth beyond 2 levels, a `wraps` cycle between boundaries, a boundary `id` colliding with a component id, and `wraps` nesting combined with `meta.engineering_profile: "deployment-ownership"` (that profile's ownership/scope rules assume flat membership and haven't been designed for nested boundaries, so the combination is rejected with a diagnostic rather than silently mis-scoping ownership). ## Tests run Base: `dev` at `9b3d3f0` (current at time of writing). Candidate: this branch, same commit as the PR head. - `node --test test/architecture-nested-boundaries.test.mjs` (new file, 9 cases covering: correct containment geometry for 2-level nesting, transitive `componentContext` scope chain, depth-3 rejection, cycle rejection, unknown-id rejection, boundary/component id-collision rejection, `deployment-ownership` incompatibility, long-label title convergence, and flat/non-nested boundaries unaffected) — 9/9 pass. - `node test/golden.mjs` — all checks pass; the 5 bundled architecture examples render byte-identical to their checked-in output. - Targeted suite (`path-boundary-contract`, `renderer-diagnostic-boundary`, `geometry`, `layout-rules`, `architecture-compare-recovery`, `architecture-delta*`, `engineering-profile`, plus the new file) — 280/280 pass. - Full repo suite (`node --test` over every `test/*.test.mjs`) — 2107 tests: 2030 pass, 76 skipped (platform-specific, pre-existing — e.g. POSIX-only symlink/FIFO fixtures skipped on Windows, already marked as such in the suite), 1 failure identified as the canonical `archify.zip` freshness gate, expected per CONTRIBUTING.md since this PR touches schema/renderer; `archify.zip` is regenerated (Node 22, per `scripts/build-zip.sh`'s requirement) and included in this PR, and re-running `test/release-package-gates.test.mjs` after regenerating it passes that check. - Ran the full suite twice, once in a Linux environment and once locally on Windows, to separate real regressions from platform-specific flake. Two pre-existing items were confirmed unrelated to this change by re-running them against unmodified `dev`: a handful of `architecture-compare-recovery` fault-injection tests are flaky on both platforms regardless of this diff, and one Windows-only symlink-permission test (`archive build excludes untracked files and external symlinks...`) fails with `EPERM` on `dev` as well, consistent with the suite's existing Windows-symlink skip annotations elsewhere in the same file. - Not yet run: the broader agent-driven generation timing/repair-round comparison requested for final review. Opening as a draft per the go-ahead on #410 while that's still in progress. ## Visual evidence - **Evidence provided:** rendered the worked example from the docs (Platform region containing a Checkout Subsystem security-group, plus a Shared Cache component outside the inner frame) locally and opened it in-browser. Screenshot attached below — the outer Platform frame visibly contains the inner Checkout Subsystem frame, Shared Cache sits inside Platform but outside Checkout Subsystem as intended, both boundary titles render without overlapping each other or any component, and both connections (`Cart Service -> Notifications`, `Inventory Service -> Shared Cache`) route cleanly. Also stress-tested with a deliberately very long inner-boundary label to confirm the existing title-readability convergence loop still resolves it without collision (no code changes were needed there — the existing sibling-boundary collision logic already generalizes to nested frames). - **Comparison conditions:** same input JSON, default `standard` quality profile, default viewBox (auto-computed), rendered and viewed locally on Windows in Chrome. - **Automated or browser checks:** geometry containment and title-non-overlap are asserted in `test/architecture-nested-boundaries.test.mjs` (see Tests run), and confirmed visually in-browser (screenshot below). - **Perceptual visual review:** passed. ## Generated artifacts - `archify.zip` is regenerated (via `scripts/build-zip.sh`, Node 22) to stay in sync with the schema/renderer changes in this PR, per CONTRIBUTING.md's ZIP-freshness requirement. No other generated output (validators, viewer bundle, brand marks) required regeneration — `npm run check:validators` and the equivalent generator scripts were re-run and produced no diff beyond the one line in `generated-validators.mjs` that reflects the schema change.

title: feat(architecture): allow right-aligned boundary titles
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

Closes #534 (scope proposed there; opened as Draft until the maintainers agree on the field name and values).

On current `main` (`527886d`), architecture boundary titles are always anchored to the frame's top-left corner, and boundaries accept no presentation field beyond `pad`. In a row of peer regions (one region per VM, for example), the main inbound relationship often enters each frame at its top-left component, so the arrow runs through or next to the title. The only workaround is to move components or reroute edges, which breaks an otherwise clean grid.

This PR adds an optional `labelAlign: "left" | "right"` field on architecture boundaries. `"right"` anchors the title mask `boundaryLabelFrameInset` px from the frame's right edge. The change is a few lines in `measureBoundaryTitle`, so the maintenance cost is small.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: **Contract change** (architecture schema + Skill authoring contract). Changed callers: `measureBoundaryTitle` in the architecture renderer (title `x` only), `BOUNDARY_FIELDS` in architecture delta (`labelAlign` classified as `geometry`, like `pad`), regenerated `generated-validators.mjs`, and one paragraph in `references/authoring-contract.md`.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: additive field, no `schema_version` change. Omitting the field, or setting `"left"`, keeps the current `x` formula, so existing sources render byte-identically. Title width, height, font size, vertical rail, collision handling and frame geometry are unchanged for `"right"`. Any other value fails schema validation at `/boundaries/N/labelAlign`.

## Tests run

Base `527886d`, candidate `3bcf747`.

- New tests:
  - `test/layout-rules.test.mjs`: `labelAlign: "right"` puts the mask's right edge at `frame.right - 4`; the default stays at `frame.x + 4`; the frame, the mask's y/width/height and the other boundary's mask are unchanged. This test fails on base renderer code and passes on the candidate.
  - `test/golden.mjs`: `labelAlign: "center"` is rejected with `/boundaries/0/labelAlign`.
  - `test/architecture-delta.test.mjs`: a `labelAlign` change is `geometry-changed` with `changedFields: ["/labelAlign"]`.
- `npm test` from `archify/` on Node 22.23.2 (Linux): 1399 tests, 1344 pass, 49 skipped, 6 fail. The same 6 fail on base `527886d` in the same environment (`cli: deliver --open ...`, `cli: opener failure ...`, and 4 `release-package-gates` archive-build tests where the spawned build returns a null status). They look environmental: running `scripts/build-zip.sh` directly on Node 22 succeeds. I am relying on remote CI for these.
- `npm run check:validators`: passes after `npm run generate:validators`.

## Visual evidence

- Evidence provided: reproducible steps. Take `examples/web-app.architecture.json`, add `"labelAlign": "right"` to `boundaries[0]`, then run `node bin/archify.mjs deliver architecture <src> <out> --quality showcase`. The `AWS Region: us-west-2` title moves to the frame's top-right corner, and nothing else changes.
- Comparison conditions: same input and CLI flags on base and candidate; only the edited boundary's title mask/text `x` differs.
- Automated or browser checks: layout-rules assertions above. `deliver` and `visual-check` pass on a real 5-region diagram using `labelAlign: "right"` on four peer regions.
- Perceptual visual review: passed (1440x900 and 2048x1320, light and dark themes).

## Generated artifacts

- Regenerated: `archify/renderers/shared/generated-validators.mjs` (schema input changed).
- `archify.zip` left unchanged: the tracked archive already differs from a Node 22 `scripts/build-zip.sh` build of base `527886d`, so it is not refreshed per feature PR. I can rebuild it here if you prefer.
- Gallery, guide, start and README showcase: unaffected (no bundled example or Viewer change).

Fixes #408

As discussed, this PR introduces the packaging Proof of Concept (PoC) for the CLI-first npm release.

### Changes

- Updated `archify/package.json` to use the scoped name `@tt-a1i/archify`; removed `"private": true` so the package is publishable.
- `bin` exposes the CLI via `./bin/archify.mjs`; `main`/`exports` are intentionally omitted to prevent unsafe library imports (renderers call `process.exit()`), pending #222.
- Configured the `files` array to include everything the shipped commands need at runtime: renderers + generated validators, schemas, `assets/template.html` + embedded JetBrains Mono font + OFL license, `bin/` runtimes, delta/recipes/references, examples (incl. compare proof fixtures), migrations, and the four runtime scripts. The `generate-*.mjs` generators are excluded.
- Added `publishConfig.access: public` and repository metadata.
- `scripts/stage-clean-skill.mjs` now also strips `overrides` from the shipped manifest (it predated that field); `scripts/package-smoke.mjs` and the staging test gate it.
- Added `scripts/npm-pack-poc.sh` — repeatable end-to-end packaging verification (pack → extract → metadata + asset assertions → isolated install → doctor → render/deliver → byte-identical comparison for all 5 types).
- No source paths were moved or renamed; existing skill/ZIP installation flows are unaffected (`package-smoke` passes).

### Packaging constraints honored

- **Scoped name:** `@tt-a1i/archify`
- **CLI-first:** `bin.archify → ./bin/archify.mjs`, no `main`/`exports` in the packed manifest
- **No side effects:** packed manifest contains **no lifecycle scripts** (`npm install` copies nothing outside `node_modules`); verified via `npm pack --json` metadata assertion

### Validation Steps Performed

```bash
# 1. Create the tarball (from inside archify/)
cd archify
npm pack                      # → tt-a1i-archify-2.17.0-dev.1.tgz

# 2. Isolated project outside the repo
cd ..
mkdir archify-pack-test && cd archify-pack-test
npm init -y
npm install ../archify/tt-a1i-archify-2.17.0-dev.1.tgz

# 3. Exercise the CLI via npx — all 5 diagram types
npx archify render architecture ../archify/examples/web-app.architecture.json
npx archify render workflow     ../archify/examples/agent-tool-call.workflow.json
npx archify render sequence     ../archify/examples/cache-miss-request.sequence.json
npx archify render dataflow     ../archify/examples/product-analytics.dataflow.json
npx archify render lifecycle    ../archify/examples/agent-run.lifecycle.json

# 4. Full automated verification
bash scripts/npm-pack-poc.sh
```

All 5 diagram types executed successfully; each installed-package render is **byte-identical** (`cmp`) to a render straight from the source tree, using the same input file for both runs.

### Test output

```text
==> 1/9 Staging the clean package tree (scripts/stage-clean-skill.mjs)
  [ok] staged 79 files
==> 2/9 npm pack from the staged tree
  [ok] packed tt-a1i-archify-2.17.0-dev.1.tgz
==> 4/9 Verifying packaged metadata (scoped name, bin-only, clean manifest)
  [ok] name, bin-only surface, and clean manifest confirmed
==> 5/9 Verifying bundled assets required by the shipped commands
  [ok] all 31 required assets bundled (renderers, validators, schemas, template,
       font + OFL license, examples/proof fixtures, bin runtimes, references)
==> 6/9 Installing the tarball in an isolated prefix (no lifecycle scripts)
  [ok] installed into .../node_modules/@tt-a1i/archify
==> 7/9 Running archify doctor from the installed package
[ok] Node.js v25.8.1 (requires >=18)
[ok] Core template
[ok] Example renderer
[ok] Live preview runtime
[ok] Visual-check runtime
[ok] Output path safety runtime
[ok] Scenario recipe guide
[ok] Progressive authoring references
[ok] Architecture compare runtime and proof fixtures
[ok] Standalone schema validators
[ok] architecture renderer, schema, and example
[ok] workflow renderer, schema, and example
[ok] sequence renderer, schema, and example
[ok] dataflow renderer, schema, and example
[ok] lifecycle renderer, schema, and example

Archify is ready.
==> 8/9 Rendering and validating with the installed CLI
  [ok] validate architecture
  [ok] deliver architecture (receipt verified, artifact written)
==> 9/9 Rendering ALL 5 diagram types via npx and comparing against the source tree
  [ok] architecture: npx output byte-identical to source
  [ok] workflow:     npx output byte-identical to source
  [ok] sequence:     npx output byte-identical to source
  [ok] dataflow:     npx output byte-identical to source
  [ok] lifecycle:    npx output byte-identical to source

Packaging PoC passed.
```

### Notes for reviewers

- `npm pack archify` (bare word) from the repo root resolves as a **registry spec** and silently downloads the squatted `archify@0.0.4` — always use `npm pack` inside `archify/` or an explicit `./archify` path. The PoC script asserts the tarball filename so this cannot slip through.
- `npm pack` does not strip `scripts`/`devDependencies`/`overrides` from the manifest, so the PoC packs from the existing `stage-clean-skill.mjs` staging tree (same contract as the ZIP release), which now strips all three.

@joesaby - The packed tarball structure is ready if you want to pull this branch, run `npm pack`, and test the subprocess integration in astro-archify.

@tt-a1i - Let me know if the `files` array needs any adjustments before we look at release automation!

## Summary

Reworks all four pages (index, gallery, guide, start) around a shared **polish layer** — `styles/polish.css` + `scripts/polish.js` + `components/TraceField.astro` — instead of per-page one-offs.

**Shared signature interactions**
- Blueprint crosshair cursor with coordinate + hovered-element readout, grid flashlight (`mix-blend-mode: difference` works on light and dark sections)
- Trace routes draw themselves on load, nodes pop in with mono micro-labels, then signal packets start traveling
- Scramble/decode for mono labels and nav links, magnetic primary buttons, scroll progress line, nav condensation on scroll
- Word-split headline reveal (word-level for Latin, per-character for CJK), `data-typed` typewriter lines that restart on language flips
- Cross-document view transitions between pages, drawn dividers, fixed sheet-margin marks with live scroll coordinate

**index** — hero gains a cycling typed prompt + scroll-out dissolve; the types section becomes a **pinned scroll-driven showcase** (chapter crossing the viewport center crossfades the framed preview and steps the 01/05 counter); new dark **Cinema** band embeds a live autoplaying artifact with annotation marks; ghost Archify wordmark closes the page.

**gallery** — cards cascade-replay on filter changes and autoplay their artifact preview on hover; proof-board metrics count up.

**guide** — typed situation line matching the "write a situation" positioning; staggered recipe entrances.

**start** — the generated prompt now **decodes character-by-character** on every state change.

All motion honors `prefers-reduced-motion` and skips hover-only effects on coarse pointers. Zero new dependencies.

**Baseline refresh:** `docs/*.html` migration baselines updated to the new design; the tailwind style normalization in `migration.test.mjs` is now symmetric (it was asymmetrically applied to dist only, which breaks once the baseline is generated output too).

title: feat(check): reject boundary frames that enclose non-members
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

Closes #395.

Scoped to @tt-a1i's direction in https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/issues/395#issuecomment-5758756059. @bluefateludi — coordinating here per that comment; happy to hand over or split review.

Per that comment the practical acceptance evidence is being added during review. What is here now is CLI timing, repair-attempt counts, and before/after visual comparison; what is still owed is listed under **Evidence still to come**.

## Problem and value

On current main (`72c750b`) a boundary frame is drawn as the bounding box of its members plus padding. Any component parked inside that box renders as enclosed whether or not the author wrapped it, and nothing reports it. The reader cannot recover the authored model from the picture, and the artifact still passes all nine checks.

Geometry alone cannot separate the two cases, so membership has to reach the checker. Per direction (1), the architecture renderer emits the authored `wraps` set as an additive `data-composition-frame-members` attribute on the structural frame, alongside the existing `-kind`, `-id` and `-label`.

New code `composition/boundary-membership`: full containment is a `showcase` error, partial overlap is a warning at every profile. The diagnostic names the component, the boundary, and both measured rectangles; `supportedFixes` offers both repairs (move the component out, or add it to `wraps` if it belongs).

## Stability impact

- **Impact class: shared behavior.** `renderers/shared/geometry.mjs` (new `collectBoundaryMembership`), `scripts/check-render-output.mjs` (new metrics and issues), `renderers/architecture/render-architecture.mjs` (one new attribute on the frame rect), `delta/architecture-delta.mjs` (version scoping on the overlay). Callers: every `render` / `validate` / `deliver` / `compare` / `check` path that produces or reads an architecture artifact.

- **Changed acceptance verdicts, stated plainly.** This is a new rule, so on *matched unrepaired input* it changes outcomes, by design:
  - `showcase`: an architecture diagram whose frame fully encloses a non-member **now fails where it previously passed**. This is the acceptance change the issue asked for. A straddle stays a warning and still passes.
  - `standard`: exit status is unchanged in every case. Containment and straddle both surface as **new warnings** that did not exist on main.
  - Every other diagram type and any artifact without the metadata: unchanged, nothing new reported.
  - The artifact check count stays at **9** — the rule reports through `composition.issues[]` and the composition summary, not a tenth check.
  - Across the repository's frame-bearing artifacts, `archify check` returns the **same verdict** as on main (0 verdict changes). Two of the three artifacts that gain findings are repaired here; the third gains one warning, which does not change its verdict.

- **Compatibility, and "not checked" vs "checked and passed".** A frame with no `data-composition-frame-members` is skipped rather than judged, so previously rendered HTML and frames from other diagram types (workflow lanes, sequence bands, dataflow stages) are unaffected. A zero issue count would otherwise read identically for a clean artifact and an unjudged one, so the composition metrics gain three fields, **all new in this PR**:

  ```
  boundaryMembershipIssues         // hits reported
  boundaryMembershipFramesChecked  // frames that declared membership and were judged
  boundaryMembershipFramesUnknown  // frames that declared none, and were skipped
  ```

  Visible in the gallery manifest, where the distinction is the one asked for:

  | artifact | checked | unknown | issues |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `deployment-ownership` (architecture) | 4 | 0 | 0 |
  | `web-app` (architecture) | 2 | 0 | 0 |
  | `agent-tool-call` (workflow) | 0 | 9 | 0 |
  | `cache-miss` (sequence) | 0 | 3 | 0 |
  | `event-stream` (dataflow) | 0 | 5 | 0 |

- **Failure behavior.** Non-zero CLI exit and machine-readable receipt preserved. Stable `code`, concrete `evidence` (`containment`, `node`, `frame`, `nodeRect`, `frameRect`, plus `scope` on compare output), executable `supportedFixes`.

## Compare scoping, direction (3)

A repeated frame id no longer disables the rule for the whole artifact. A compare artifact overlays two versions in one coordinate space, so `buildDeltaSvg` marks elements with `data-composition-scope="base"` or `"head"`, and the rule joins a frame to a component only within a version.

**Sharing is decided by what each version actually renders** — the frame's measured rect and membership attribute, and the node's measured rect — not by what the comparator classified as changed. That distinction matters and was a live bug in the first cut of this change:

- The comparator reports a boundary change for `wraps` and `pad`. It reports **no** boundary change when a boundary's *members move*, even though the rendered frame moves with them. Deriving scope from change records therefore left the head frame unscoped, and it judged base-only geometry. Reproduced: base members at x=100 with a non-member at x=600, head members at x=600 with the non-member at x=900 — enclosed in neither version, reported by the overlay. Regression: *a frame whose members moved does not judge the other version*.
- The same hazard exists for components: grid placement is authored as `row`/`col`, so a change of `layout.origin` moves every rendered node with no component change at all. Regression: *a moved grid origin does not judge the other version*.

An element both versions draw identically carries no scope and answers to either. `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` is the shipped case: base draws `cache` inside both head frames and head draws `fraud` inside the base region, three cross-version enclosures that would otherwise be reported. The rule now reads all four frames (`checked=4, unknown=0`) and reports nothing, where on main it read none.

**Known limit, disclosed.** The overlay only contains the geometry it draws. When a boundary changes in a way that produces no base phantom, a base-only enclosure is not visible in the delta artifact and `archify check <delta.html>` cannot report it. `archify compare` validates the base and head snapshots separately, so the defect is still caught at generation time; it is the later artifact check that is incomplete. Happy to follow up if you want the compare artifact to carry enough baseline geometry to close that.

## Example repairs, direction (2)

No sparseness or component-type exemption: a boundary that spreads its members still answers for everything its frame encloses (regression: *a sparse membership is judged like any other*). Two of the three affected examples are repaired by geometry only — **no `wraps`, component, or connection was added, removed, or re-pointed** in either. The third is reported back to you rather than repaired.

The counts below are **this PR's checker applied to main's geometry** versus the repaired geometry. Main's own checker reports zero for all of them, because the rule does not exist there.

| example | on main's geometry | repair | after repair |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `examples/archify-repo-grid` | 3 straddles: the frame's default 30px pad overruns a 24px grid gutter into `agents`, `skill`, `html` | `"pad": 14` on the boundary | clean |
| `examples/maka-architecture` | 7 full containments: the region enclosed `providers`, `bots`, `tools`; `trust boundary` (members at opposite corners) swept up `session`, `agentrun`, `bots`, `toolrt` | layout restructure, below | clean, and zero composition warnings of any kind |
| `archify/examples/production-deployment` | 1 straddle: `audit` cut by the `private application network` frame's bottom edge | **not repaired** — see below | unchanged, 1 warning at `showcase` (a straddle does not fail) |

### The production-deployment straddle is left in place, and here is why

I repaired it first, then backed it out. `audit` sits inside the security group's x-span no matter where it goes horizontally without pushing the diagram past the `composition/desktop-readability` width, so it has to leave the frame vertically. The band above is occupied by `observability`, and the band below is bounded by the disaster-recovery region:

```
private application network bottom = 487   (api_b / postgres at y=405, pad 14)
audit must clear it                 → audit.y >= 487
AWS us-east-1 bottom  = audit.y + 62 + 20
AWS eu-west-1 top     = replica.y - 42      (pad 30 plus label allowance)
frames must not partially overlap   → replica.y - 42 > audit.y + 82
```

That forces `replica` down by ~42px, which grows the viewBox from 728 to 770 — and `archify visual-check` then reports `viewer/viewport-overflow` at 1440x900 (scrollHeight 922) and at 1600x1000. Shrinking either pad closes at most ~20px of it.

The repair that does fit moves the DR region to the bottom-left so it is horizontally disjoint from `AWS us-east-1`. That passes `validate` with zero warnings and `visual-check` cleanly, at viewBox 1376x710 — shorter than main. But it fails `test/desktop-reader-browser.test.mjs`, which pins this example's rendered layout exactly:

```
assert.equal(observation.readerWidth, 960);          // becomes 972
assert.equal(observation.diagramWidth, 930);
assert.equal(observation.minimumProjectedNodeText, 'AWS eu-west-1 / disaster recovery');
assert.equal(observation.scrollHeight, 900);
```

Any geometry change to this example moves those numbers. Rather than edit a pinned reader-layout fixture to satisfy a new rule, I have left the example alone and brought the case back here as you asked. Three ways forward, your call:

1. Leave it. A straddle is a warning at every profile, so nothing fails; the example simply carries one.
2. Take the DR-region relocation and update the four pinned assertions in `desktop-reader-browser.test.mjs`. I have it ready and have checked it in the browser.
3. Something else for the audit archive's placement that I have not thought of.

**Maka** needed real work and is worth a look. `AgentRun` already spends all four sides (`session` left, `model` right, `permission` top, `toolrt` bottom), which is why `toolrt → permission` had to detour around the diagram; and `permission`/`storage` sat at opposite corners, which is what made `trust boundary` sprawl. Putting them side by side while keeping the old detour pushed the viewBox past the `composition/desktop-readability` width. The arrangement that works moves `model` below `AgentRun` and `toolrt` to its right, which frees `toolrt → permission` to be a short two-segment route and lets `storage` sit beside `permission` on the top row. Externals (`user`, `bots`, `providers`, `tools`) now sit outside the app region. The spec diff is only positions, sides, one `via`, one `labelDy`, and one `pad`.

If the new reading of Maka is not the one you want, say so — the constraint is only that the two `trust boundary` members end up adjacent and the four externals end up outside the region bbox, and other arrangements satisfy it.

**On overlapping sets:** two boundaries that share a component necessarily produce nested frames, because both frames must contain that component's rectangle, and the existing `layout/constraint` rule already requires frames to be disjoint or fully nested. So the nested-membership regression is the overlapping-sets case; there is no separate partially-overlapping-frames case to cover.

## Tests run

Comparison base `5289f68` (current `main`), candidate head on this branch. The branch is rebased onto current `main`, so the Astro website migration is included in the base.

```sh
cd archify && npm ci && npm test
# 1422 tests, 1369 pass, 0 fail, 53 skipped   (main: 1398 / 1345 / 0 / 53)

# the browser gate, which npm test skips without a Chrome path
ARCHIFY_CHROME=<chrome> node --test test/desktop-reader-browser.test.mjs test/reader-layout-browser.test.mjs
# 10 tests, 10 pass, 0 fail
```

Worth stating because it caught a regression I had shipped: `npm test` **skips** the real-browser tests unless `ARCHIFY_CHROME` is set, so a geometry repair that overflowed the 1440x900 reader passed locally and failed in CI. Those two files are now part of what I run before pushing.

24 regressions in `archify/test/boundary-membership.test.mjs` (the whole delta between the two counts above): the reporter's minimal JSON end to end through `validate --quality showcase`; the error/warning tier split; `standard` compatibility; nested and sparse membership; a frame that declares no membership; an explicitly empty membership; zero-area and edge-touching components; five SVG-parsing decoys (title text that looks like an attribute, single quotes, comments, a rect outside the element, malformed nesting); a moved node drawn twice; the checked-in delta artifact; and three that drive `archify compare` end to end so the scope attributes are exercised at generation, not just read back.

**Every architecture spec in the repository** (15 across five directories), under `validate`:

| spec | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `archify/examples/web-app` | pass | pass |
| `archify/examples/production-deployment` | pass | pass |
| `archify/examples/brand-aware-delivery` | pass | pass |
| `archify/examples/checkout-platform.base` / `.head` | pass | pass |
| `docs/gallery/sources/web-app` | pass | pass |
| `docs/gallery/sources/production-deployment` | pass | pass |
| `examples/archify-repo` | pass | pass |
| `examples/archify-repo-grid` | pass | pass |
| `examples/maka-architecture` | pass | pass |
| `examples/rag-pipeline` | pass | pass |
| `archify/test/fixtures/v1-baseline/web-app` | pass | pass |
| `archify/test/fixtures/v1-baseline/production-deployment` | fails `desktop-readability` | same (pre-existing) |
| `docs/cases/mco-runtime`, `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime` | needs an `mco-org/mco` checkout | same (pre-existing) |

All 12 that pass on main still pass here. Eleven carry **zero composition warnings**; `production-deployment` carries **one** `composition/boundary-membership` warning, which is the straddle described above that I did not repair. Its verdict is unchanged, because a straddle is a warning at every profile.

**Every frame-bearing artifact** (26), `archify check` verdict on main vs this PR: **0 verdict changes.** Two (`docs/cases/mco-runtime.architecture.html`, `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html`) could not be regenerated here — they declare repository evidence against `mco-org/mco`, which this checkout is not. They keep the old HTML and report `checked=0, unknown=2`: visibly not judged rather than silently clean. Regenerating them needs that checkout.

### Timing

CLI timings, median of 9 alternating runs per cell, same machine and inputs (Node v26.4.0, Apple silicon, `archify validate architecture <spec> --json` and `archify render architecture <spec> <out>` against both revisions). Process startup dominates at this size; nothing here is outside run-to-run noise:

| case | validate main | validate PR | Δ | render main | render PR | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| web-app (5 nodes, 2 frames) | 229 ms | 242 ms | +5.4% | 165 ms | 165 ms | −0.1% |
| production-deployment (12 nodes, 4 frames) | 227 ms | 223 ms | −1.5% | 153 ms | 156 ms | +1.7% |
| brand-aware-delivery | 227 ms | 225 ms | −0.9% | 179 ms | 167 ms | −7.0% |
| maka (12 nodes, 2 frames) | 231 ms | 232 ms | +0.7% | 156 ms | 160 ms | +2.5% |
| rag-pipeline | 228 ms | 225 ms | −1.2% | 159 ms | 156 ms | −1.9% |
| archify-repo-grid (grid mode) | 223 ms | 214 ms | −4.3% | 164 ms | 158 ms | −3.8% |
| **synthetic 160 components / 8 boundaries** | 249 ms | 256 ms | +2.5% | 172 ms | 170 ms | −1.2% |

The spread in both directions at the same magnitude (−7.0% to +5.4%) is the noise floor, not a signal.

Isolating the checker (`node archify/scripts/check-render-output.mjs <artifact>`, median of 25 runs) shows the rule's marginal cost, which is small but not zero. The rule is O(frames × components) plus one tokenizer pass to collect component boxes:

| artifact | check main | check PR | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| synthetic 160 components / 8 boundaries | 72.3 ms | 77.9 ms | +7.7% (+5.6 ms) |
| checkout delta (compare overlay) | 61.6 ms | 63.7 ms | +3.5% |
| production-deployment | 62.6 ms | 63.9 ms | +2.2% |
| maka | 59.0 ms | 59.2 ms | +0.5% |

The synthetic case is reproducible: 160 components on an 8×20 grid at `pos = [40 + 180·col, 100 + 140·row]`, `size [120, 60]`, a chain connection along each row, and one boundary per row wrapping columns 0–9 with `"pad": 20` (alternating `region` / `security-group`). I can commit the generator as a fixture if you would rather have it in-tree.

### Repair experience

Measured on the three real repairs in this PR, working only from the CLI diagnostics:

| example | defects | strategies tried | `validate` runs | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `archify-repo-grid` | 3 straddles | 1 | 3 | fixed first try |
| `maka-architecture` | 7 containments | 6 | ~14 | fixed, but this was a layout restructure, not a nudge |
| `production-deployment` | 1 straddle | 6 | ~25 | **not fixed** — every candidate either overflows the 1440x900 reader or moves numbers a browser test pins |

Worth flagging rather than burying:

- **The diagnostic identifies the defect but does not suggest a direction.** It gives the component, the boundary and both rectangles, which is enough to know *what* is wrong, but unlike `layout/constraint` (which offers `labelAt [x, y] or labelDy +24`) it does not propose a repair position. On `production-deployment` the first two repair attempts each traded this warning for a different one. A follow-up could compute the nearest clear offset; out of scope here.
- **Repair cost is not uniform, and is sometimes unpayable.** A straddle caused by padding is a one-line fix. A containment caused by two members sitting at opposite corners of a dense diagram is a redesign, because the frame is a derived rectangle and the only lever is where the members are. And on a diagram already at its reader budget, there may be no repair at all that does not trade this warning for a different failure — that is `production-deployment` above, and it is the most useful data point in this table.
- **No false positives in the source specs.** Every hit across all 15 specs was a real misleading enclosure, confirmed in the browser — including the one I could not repair. No case needed a sparseness or type exemption. The one false positive found during development was in compare scoping, is described above, and is fixed with a regression.

- Elapsed end-to-end generation and repair session times, with the model/tool setup stated for agent-driven runs, rather than the CLI-only timing and attempt counts above.
- `deliver` timing alongside `validate` and `render`.
- A larger and denser real diagram than the synthetic grid, and a repair session on one.

```

**Perceptual review** — reported separately, and narrower than the automated evidence above. I compared base and candidate side by side for the two repaired diagrams in Chrome at 1440x980, dark theme, shipped preset, 100% zoom, no guided view:

title: feat(workflow): add in-memory renderWorkflow() library entrypoint
body:
Closes #527.

## Problem

Every archify renderer script (`renderers/<type>/render-<type>.mjs`) is a one-shot CLI entry point, not an importable function: it reads input from `process.argv`/disk via `loadDiagram()`, runs its render as a top-level `await` the moment the module is imported, and — through the CLI-only diagnostics boundary `loadDiagram()` installs — calls `process.exit()` directly on both success and failure. That makes it unsafe to `import` for in-process rendering: a host process embedding archify would have its own process torn down by a bad diagram, not just the render call fail.

The real consumer that ran into this is my own [astro-archify](https://github.com/joesaby/astro-archify) — an Astro integration that turns fenced ```archify code blocks in markdown into rendered diagrams at build time. Because the renderer scripts can't be imported safely, it [vendors a full copy of `renderers/`](https://github.com/joesaby/astro-archify/tree/main/vendor/archify) and [spawns `node render-<type>.mjs input.json output.html` as a subprocess](https://github.com/joesaby/astro-archify/blob/main/astro-archify-integration.js#L169-L217) per diagram, reading the output file back afterward — a process-spawn + temp-file round trip for what's otherwise a pure `IR in -> HTML out` transform with no runtime dependencies beyond Node builtins.

## What this PR does

Workflow-first PoC for #222, per the direction tt-a1i confirmed [here](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/issues/222#issuecomment-5743474339). Adds `renderWorkflow()` in `archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-api.mjs`: an async, importable function that runs the same validation and resource preparation as the CLI's `loadDiagramWithBrandMarks()` — schema, guided views + relationship IDs (via `validateCrossCollectionContracts`, the shared entry point #462 introduced), engineering profile, repository evidence, and brand-mark capture — then calls `compileWorkflow()`, and returns `{ html, svg, cards, meta, sourceEvidence, receipt }` to the caller instead of writing a file.

- A classified, author-facing failure comes back as `{ ok: false, diagnostics }` instead of throwing. The CLI-only process-level diagnostics boundary (`installRendererDiagnosticBoundary`, #418) is never installed by this path, so a bad document cannot take down the host process.
- Each call `structuredClone`s its input, so the caller's document is never mutated and concurrent/repeated calls stay independent.
- Nothing here writes a file, logs to console, or sets `process.exitCode` — delivery stays owned by the caller. A render result never claims delivery completed.
- `writeDiagram()`'s template-fill step is extracted into a small shared `renderDiagramHtml()` in `shared/cli.mjs`, used by both the CLI and this new library path. `render-workflow.mjs` (the CLI script) is otherwise untouched.

**Two host-isolation fixes from review, credited to @NaCr05:** NaCr05 independently reviewed the first version of this PR and published a [handoff patch](https://github.com/NaCr05/archify/blob/993119b0dcf3389f7096666d2172f5d8a35fa348/contribution-handoff/482/README.md) identifying two real bugs. I re-implemented both myself (verified each fails without its fix, using their analysis as the starting point) rather than apply the patch directly:
1. `svgRootAttrs()` fell back to reading `process.env.ARCHIFY_QUALITY_PROFILE` whenever no quality profile was otherwise resolved — so a host process with that env var set for unrelated reasons could silently override an "advisory" `renderWorkflow()` call the caller never asked to be pinned. Fixed with a `profileIsAuthoritative` flag, opted into only at the workflow compiler's own call site; architecture/sequence/dataflow/lifecycle's existing direct `svgRootAttrs()` calls are untouched.
2. `withDiagnosticRecordingSuppressed()` used a plain module-level depth counter, unsafe once the suppressed callback is async (its `finally` fires when the callback's *synchronous* portion returns, not when the returned promise settles) — exactly the shape `renderWorkflow()` has, since it awaits `prepareDiagramBrandMarks()`. Under `ARCHIFY_DIAGNOSTIC_FORMAT=json`, a failed library call's diagnostics could leak into a later, unrelated CLI failure report in the same process. Fixed by switching to `AsyncLocalStorage`, scoped per call chain, and wrapping `renderWorkflow()` in it.

Both fixes are scoped narrowly and verified not to change any existing CLI behavior (golden output byte-identical, full existing suite passes).

## What this doesn't do yet

This covers `workflow` only, because `workflow-compiler.mjs` already exposes `compileWorkflow()` as a function separable from the CLI plumbing — the other four renderers (architecture, sequence, dataflow, lifecycle) don't have that split yet, so they still need the subprocess path. A consumer like astro-archify, which renders all five diagram types through one generic path, can't retire its vendor+subprocess pattern until the same shape extends to the rest — that's the natural next slice once the API shape here settles, and astro-archify itself isn't touched by this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `test/workflow-library-api-call-contract.test.mjs`: input validation, host isolation (no mutation, concurrent calls independent), never installs the process-level diagnostics boundary, guided-view/relationship-ID contracts, and returns compiler-level failures as data rather than throwing.
- [x] `test/workflow-library-api-quality.test.mjs`: `renderWorkflow()` stays advisory under an ambient `ARCHIFY_QUALITY_PROFILE` the caller never asked for, while an explicit `qualityProfile` argument still takes effect. Verified this test fails without the `svgRootAttrs` fix.
- [x] `test/workflow-library-api-diagnostics.test.mjs`: a failed `renderWorkflow()` call under `ARCHIFY_DIAGNOSTIC_FORMAT=json` does not leak into a later, unrelated CLI diagnostic report. Verified this test fails without the `AsyncLocalStorage` fix.
- [x] `node --test test/workflow-*.test.mjs` — all 166 workflow tests pass. `node --test test/render-failure-diagnostics.test.mjs test/renderer-diagnostic-boundary.test.mjs test/renderer-import-isolation.test.mjs` — all pass (confirms the `diagnostics.mjs` change doesn't regress the CLI boundary for any of the 5 renderers).
- [x] `node test/golden.mjs` — golden CLI output is byte-identical across all 5 diagram types.
- [x] Rebased onto `dev` after #462 merged; full `npm test` run shows only pre-existing, environment-specific failures (verified identical against a clean, unmodified `dev` checkout) plus two `parse5`-module-not-found failures traced to this sandbox's incomplete `node_modules` install — none touch any file this PR changes.
