title: feat: open the renderer without changing a single existing artifact
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

A document can draw relationships today, but it cannot say what a leg costs, where a spot links to, what a node kind means in its own domain, what the reader may write while reading, or which stretch of the clock an axis covers. Each of those needs currently ends in either a core change or a fork of the renderer.

This branch opens **positions, not vocabulary**: `facts`, `links`, `media`, `types`, `labels`, `rules`, `edgeStates`, `meta.reader`, `meta.bands`. The core keeps owning geometry, checks and the receipt; the document owns words, numbers and colours. Nothing is required, and a document that declares none of it renders byte for byte as before — the checked-in golden test is the proof, not our word.

Design reasoning: `docs/openness-design.md`. Field tables and every measurement: `docs/openness-pr-brief.md`. No domain content is included; the travel pack that motivated the work stays downstream on the fork.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: additive schema positions plus compiler paths that return before doing anything when nothing is declared. One viewer behavior changes on purpose: an effect listed in `meta.reader.suppress` is not built, and the delivery receipt records what was left out.
- Compatibility: three `required` lists were relaxed (`nodes[].col`, `phases[].fromCol/toCol`, `groups[].fromCol/toCol`), each paired with a compiler diagnostic naming the same defect (`workflow/node-col-missing`, `workflow/phase-extent-missing`, `workflow/group-extent-missing`). A document rejected before is still rejected, with a better message; no silent skip was introduced.
- Nothing before moves: every `*.workflow.json` in the repository (15) compiled with the base commit's compiler and with this branch's gives **15/15 byte-identical** SVG, runtime and diagnostic codes; every re-renderable checked-in artifact of the other four renderers (10) re-renders to an identical `<svg>` byte for byte; `node test/golden.mjs` passes all five modes, plain and packaged; the gallery test (11 artifacts) and the checkout delta pair pass. Two `mco-runtime` cases pin evidence to revisions a shallow clone cannot fetch, so they are not covered by that run.

## Tests run

`cd archify && npm test`, comparison base `72c750b`, head `89f2451`:

- Windows: 1363 pass, 31 fail — the same 31, one for one, on a pristine `72c750b` checkout with the same dependencies (symlink privileges, missing `bash`/`unzip`, `core.autocrlf` expectations, git replacement refs, network-lease timing). Zero added, zero removed.
- 63 new cases in 8 files: `workflow-reader` 11, `clock-arithmetic` 6, `derivation-conflicts` 9, `phase-bands` 19, `workflow-rules` 6, `workflow-links` 4, `workflow-types` 4, `suppression` 4; `workflow-compiler-hard-contract` edited so the closed side stays closed. Remote CI is expected to cover the platform skips this machine cannot run.

- Remote CI on this branch (run `35429291282`): **11/11 green** — `test` on Node 18, 20, 22 and 24, `package smoke` on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows, `webm-artifact`, `published-update-manifest`, `zip-freshness`. The suite is green on all four Node majors; only the canonical archive is pinned to 22, which is why `archify.zip` is rebuilt rather than generated on whichever Node happens to be installed.

## Visual evidence

- Evidence provided: a pixel comparison of the 24 regenerated artifacts, before (base commit) and after, at 1440x900, dark theme, default preset and page state, plus measured width/scale numbers for the two clock-axis forms.
- Automated checks: `archify visual-check` passes on both artifacts of the downstream demo; the composition gate passes 9/9 on its compact form.
- Differences: none beyond re-capture noise — the same page captured twice differed by as much as each cross-version delta, node and edge counts matched, and no console errors were recorded.
- Perceptual visual review: skipped here (automation only).

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated because the viewer template changed: `archify.zip` (the distributable skill archive — rebuilt with the repository's own `scripts/build-zip.sh` pipeline under Node 22; verified by rebuilding the base commit's archive and matching its bytes before rebuilding this one), `archify/examples/*.html` (5), `examples/*.html` (6, including the checkout delta pair and its receipt), `docs/gallery/*` (index, manifest, 11 artifacts), `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.gif` and its receipt. One upstream portability fix came out of that work: `scripts/build-readme-showcase.mjs` wrote a Windows path into its receipt via `path.relative`, so no non-Windows machine could rebuild it; it now writes POSIX separators.

body:
## Problem and value

Related to #477 and #175. 本 PR 的整体范围由 Workflow 试点扩展为 **五类图的内容自适应画布与共享大图浏览**：Workflow、Architecture、Dataflow、Sequence、Lifecycle。

> **代码同步状态**：已将四类图扩展提交 `517f8a3e` 与 Viewer 稳定性/体积优化提交 `6761a3bd` 推送到 #478，当前远端 head 为 `6761a3bd315d010c0fbd1b2f7e879638787df0f3`。本地分支为 `labs/adaptive-canvas`，为保留 PR #478，远端分支仍为 `labs/adaptive-workflow-canvas-pilot`，base 仍为 `dev`。本地 `artifacts/` 未上传。推送后只读检查显示 `CONFLICTING / DIRTY`，尚未观察到该 head 的 Actions 运行，CodeRabbit 为 pending；**不能视为可合并或 CI 已绿**。本次没有合并或 rebase。

依照[维护者对 #477 的说明](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/issues/477#issuecomment-5743793183)，dev 已有缩放、拖动、节点聚焦和 Workflow v2 省略 viewBox 时的内容定界；#255 也已有泳道测量/高度适配。本变更不把这些基础能力重新当作从零新增。重点是补齐完整绘制范围、改善大图首次可读入口与全部内容可达性，并将内容定界接入其余四类 renderer。

目标是减少纯画布容量导致的返工，保留内容、构图意图、普通图体验和完整导出。**不是无限白板编辑器，也不是五类图通用自动布局/自动美化引擎。** 没有证据证明自动重排一定更好，因此不以增加该能力作为本 PR 的目标；不承诺 #175 的 20–30% 端到端耗时收益。

## Stability impact

- **影响级别**：共享行为 + 合同扩展，涉及五类 renderer 的画布边界、共享 Viewer、校验/交付证据及生成产物。
- **两项独立能力**：编译器计算有限、完整的 canonical frame；Viewer 改变浏览视角，不改作者几何。
- **兼容性**：Workflow v1 和有效显式 viewBox 保留既有合同。其余四类通过可选 `meta.canvas_fit: "content"` 启用；旧输入不自动切换；作者显式 viewBox 保持权威。
- **非目标**：不解除行/阶段/列限制，不增加节点拖拽编辑、自动重排、第二套 Scene/schema、白板 SDK 或虚拟化；不以删内容、缩字体、遮挡 overflow 或放宽校验换取通过。

### 按代码状态区分的能力

| 类型/层次 | 实现范围 | 代码状态 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow v2 | 完整 paint 范围、确定性隐式 canonical frame、显式容量诊断；保留已有布局语义与接口 | 已在远端试点范围内 |
| Architecture | content 模式覆盖节点、边界标题、连线标签、描边、箭头与图例；补齐旧 auto 范围遗漏 | 提交 `517f8a3e`，现已进入远端 PR |
| Dataflow | 内容决定画布，再确定 stage 背景范围；保留 stage/row/yOffset | 同上；row 0–4、最多 5 stages 不变 |
| Sequence | 时间轴、segment/activation、消息与图例纳入范围；spread 有界求解列间距 | 同上；参与者顺序、作者时间、fixed 列距及既有约束不变 |
| Lifecycle | 状态、迁移通道、带标题、标签/备注与图例纳入范围 | 同上；main/event/terminal 槽位和三带模型不变 |
| 共享 Viewer | 大小图按实际可读性判断；大图可读入口、缩放/平移/重置、既有搜索/概览/引导导航、全部内容可达 | 基础行为与四类接入均已进入远端 PR |
| 后续稳定性与体积 | 初次取景减少画布外空白；图例在 SVG 实际尺寸稳定后重测；构建期保守 JS 压缩 | 提交 `6761a3bd`，现已进入远端 PR |

四类 content 模式用 `validate --layout-json` 输出范围和 contributors；尺寸不足、负坐标、非有限范围或有界求解失败分别给出诊断。扩画布不能修复重叠或错误引用。尺寸修复建议必须经完整布局复验，不能把“足够的尺寸”说成数学全局最小尺寸。

全图 SVG 导出独立于浏览相机；图片/WebM 在分配 Canvas 前执行预算检查，无法安全输出时明确失败并建议 SVG。引导视图、故事播放、来源和说明卡片复用已有能力，需要对应 authored 数据，并非自动编写。

## Tests run

**以下结果按代码版本分别记录；本次文案更新没有重新执行代码测试，也没有触发或证明最终远端 CI 通过。**

### 远端试点的历史证据

- 原始比较：upstream/dev `f3cc060f` → `fe37aa3e`；远端后来前进到 `47672973`。原文中的结果属于 `fe37aa3e`，不能重标为当前或最终 head 的完整结果。
- 当时完整测试：2206 项，2195 passed，0 failed，11 platform/environment skips。
- Workflow 大图：4 桌面尺寸 × light/dark，30/30 节点、50/50 关系、5 guided views 可达；六样本 hybrid corpus 覆盖 Workflow/Architecture 的 30/100/300 节点。
- 当时 machine-only validation/repair 与 handoff-ready 中位数差约 0.6%，不支持端到端加速宣称。
- 当时消融移除旧版证据回执兼容分支会导致证据清理回归，恢复后专项通过。

### 四类扩展提交 `517f8a3e`（已推送；以下为该版本的本地证据）

- 相对 `47672973`：14 组 legacy SVG 字节一致；12/12 已复现的纯容量失败解决，另保留 4 个补充控制。
- 4 类型 × 4 桌面尺寸 × 2 主题共 32 组浏览器检查；Architecture 24/24 节点、23/23 关系，Dataflow 25/25、20/20，Sequence 12/12、11/11，Lifecycle 11/11、10/10 可达。
- 完整测试 2082 passed / 0 failed / 74 conditional skips；浏览器门禁 239 passed / 0 skipped；WebM、实际栅格导出、ZIP 可复现与仓库外解包检查通过。
- legacy render/validate 串行基准 24/24 组达既定开销门槛；没有测量真实 Agent 全流程耗时收益。
- 已推送的证据：[四类实现与验收报告](https://github.com/sunsunsun-java/archify/blob/6761a3bd315d010c0fbd1b2f7e879638787df0f3/docs/four-diagram-content-canvas-implementation.md)、[证据目录](https://github.com/sunsunsun-java/archify/tree/6761a3bd315d010c0fbd1b2f7e879638787df0f3/docs/evidence/four-diagram-content-canvas)。报告里的“未推送”是当时实施状态，测试按原版本记录，不冒称在新 head 重跑。

### 后续稳定性与体积改动 `6761a3bd`（已推送）

- 保留既有构图、字体、配色、内容、默认浏览策略与交互；JS 仅格式压缩/局部变量缩名，关闭逻辑压缩、属性及顶层改名；CSS/字体未压缩。
- 6 个固定样本、78 个场景通过等价核对；60 组三路静态导出逐字节一致；四张重点图 HTML 减少约 27%。这是**文件体积**，不是生成耗时下降比例。
- 对应工作区全量测试 2088 passed / 0 failed / 76 skips；浏览器 247 passed / 0 skipped。随后独立审核复跑压缩/生成器 282 项和图例/大图浏览器 9 项，均通过。

title: feat(viewer): add a fifth Blossom visual preset
body:
## Problem and value

Archify ships four visual presets, and each one is named for the job it does: Classic as the stable default, Signal Flow for motion demos, Blueprint for engineering review, Editorial for release notes. None of them covers the case where the diagram is the artifact a reader came for — a portfolio piece, a personal project write-up, a product story. Put a Classic or Blueprint diagram at the top of a personal site and it reads like internal tooling that leaked.

Blossom fills that gap. It keeps the existing semantic palette and byte-identical SVG geometry, so no diagram changes shape or meaning. Only the presentation layer differs: rose-tinted neutrals, 1.75rem corner radii, a soft ambient glow, and circular badges instead of square ones.

No linked issue; this is a self-contained addition to an existing extension point (the preset registry), not a change to an existing preset.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: presentation-only, additive. `visual_preset` gains one accepted value (`blossom`) in `meta`; the four existing values and their rendering are untouched.
- Existing behavior preserved: the runtime preset list grows from four to five entries, `Archify.preset.cycle()` reaches the new value, and the default remains `classic`. The geometry test in `preset-tryon.test.mjs` now asserts five variants normalize to the same canonical SVG, so a geometry regression in any preset fails the suite.
- Intended compatibility change: `meta.visual_preset: "blossom"` is newly valid. Documents that do not use it render identically — the delivered template only grows by the new preset's CSS block and one menu entry.
- Failure behavior: unchanged. The schema still rejects unknown preset values with the same path-prefixed message.

## Tests run

Base: `72c750b` (current `main`). Head: the commit on this branch.

```
cd archify && npm ci && npm test
```

Both revisions were run on the same machine and produce the same result:

| revision | tests | pass | fail | skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `72c750b` (pristine) | 1262 | 1238 | 17 | 7 |
| this branch | 1262 | 1238 | 17 | 7 |

The 17 failures are identical in both runs and are Windows-only environment cases, not regressions from this change: `git init --template=` hitting the `\\.\nul` invalid-argument bug (11 cases), `git ls-files` returning nothing for a checkout without a `.git` directory (4 cases), a preview child process reporting `SIGTERM` instead of a clean exit (1 case), and `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` from passing a bare Windows path to the ESM loader (1 case). Three test files (`generate-validators`, `generate-viewer`, `release-package-gates`) abort with `0xC0000409` when the whole suite runs on Windows; they pass individually on both revisions. I did not run the browser-dependent jobs locally — remote CI is still required.

Focused test for this change: `node --test test/preset-tryon.test.mjs` → 6/6 pass.

## Visual evidence

- Evidence provided: `preset-compare-contact-sheet.png` below — the same diagram (`examples/web-app-rendered.html`, "Sample Web App Diagram"), same 1440×900 viewport, same default view, rendered in all five presets across both themes. The ten individual captures are in the same folder if a full-resolution look is needed.
- Comparison conditions: identical input artifact, viewport 1440×900, device scale factor 1, default guided view, presets switched through the shipped runtime (`Archify.preset.apply(...)`) so the picker label and the `data-preset` on both `<html>` and the canonical SVG stay in sync.
- Intended differences: background, panel treatment, corner radii, badge shape, and control marks. Classic reads cool blue; Blossom reads warm rose.
- Unexpected differences: none observed. Geometry, node positions, labels, and edge routing are identical across all five.
- Automated or browser checks: measured computed values in a real Chrome session — Blossom resolves `--bg` to `#1a1116` (dark) and `#fdf5f9` (light), `--panel-border` to `#573747` / `#e6c4d4`, `--arrow-emphasis` to `#f0a3c0` / `#c2417a`, the picker label to `Blossom`, and the diagram container radius to 28px (1.75rem). `data-preset="blossom"` reaches `<html>`, the `<svg>`, and the menu item.
- Perceptual visual review: passed (five presets reviewed side by side at 1440×900 in both themes).

![Blossom preset compared with the four existing presets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2285946393/archify/blossom-evidence/preset-compare-contact-sheet.png)

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated from the final combined source, all committed on this branch:

- `archify/assets/template.html` — via `npm run generate:viewer` (`--check` passes)
- `archify/renderers/shared/generated-validators.mjs` — via `npm run generate:validators` (`--check` passes)
- `examples/*.html` (5) and `archify/examples/*.html` (5) — via `scripts/render-examples.mjs`
- `examples/web-app.html` — the architecture example that must carry the current template; it is the same render as `web-app-rendered.html`
- `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` + `.receipt.json` — via `archify compare architecture ... --quality showcase --receipt`
- `docs/gallery.html`, `docs/gallery/manifest.json`, `docs/gallery/artifacts/*.html` (11) — via `scripts/build-gallery.mjs docs`
- `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.gif` + `.json` — via `scripts/build-readme-showcase.mjs`
- `archify.zip` — via `scripts/build-zip.sh` under Node 22

`docs/guide.html` and `docs/start.html` were rebuilt and are byte-identical to `main`, so they are not in the diff.

Two freshness notes:

- The motion-proof GIF was re-recorded because its recorded `artifactSha256` values track the gallery artifacts, which changed with the template. The new file is smaller (1,488,435 bytes vs 1,796,065) because it was captured on Windows with a local ffmpeg build; the frames, dimensions (960×540), frame count (54), and duration (5.4s) are unchanged, and the receipt is internally consistent. If you would rather have the canonical bytes, re-running `scripts/build-readme-showcase.mjs` on the CI image and amending is fine by me.
- `archify.zip` is deterministic and verified byte-stable here (rebuilt to a second path and compared), but it was built on Windows under Node 22.23.2. The `zip-freshness` job will confirm it against the CI image.

title: feat(import): add Mermaid stateDiagram importer for typed lifecycle IR
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #94 (maintainer-labelled `enhancement`, `ready-for-agent`).

Current `main` has no path from a Mermaid `stateDiagram` into Archify's typed IR. Authors retype the topology by hand, and that is the step where a state or transition that was never in the source gets invented.

This PR adds `archify import state <input.mmd> [output.json] [--json] [--title text] [--outcome state=success|failure]`. A self-contained parser in `archify/importers/state.mjs` emits lifecycle IR that passes `archify validate lifecycle`. It has no runtime dependency. Geometry and text measurement reuse `renderers/shared/geometry.mjs` and `text-fit.mjs`, so the importer cannot drift from the renderer.

| Mermaid | Lifecycle kind |
|---|---|
| `state id <<choice>>` | `decision` |
| target of `[*] -->` | `start` |
| source of `--> [*]`, with `--outcome id=success\|failure` | `success` / `failure` |
| source of `--> [*]`, no override | `neutral` |
| every other state | `active` |

The importer refuses to guess:

- `[*]` is a pseudo-state. It sets the kind of the state it touches and does not create an unnamed box.
- A terminal state defaults to `neutral`. `--> [*]` says that the lifecycle ended, not how it ended. The importer does not read "Failed", "Done", or guard text. `success` and `failure` come only from the explicit `--outcome` flag. An override that names an unknown state fails with `import/state-unknown-outcome-target`.
- `waiting` and `external` are never emitted, because Mermaid has no construct with that meaning.
- Composite states are rejected, not flattened. Flattening would have to invent transitions between the inner region and the composite's siblings.

Also rejected with a diagnostic: `--` concurrency, `<<fork>>`/`<<join>>`, styling directives, floating notes, self-transitions (the renderer needs at least 32px between endpoints), and ids outside `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$`.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: **Local behavior**. It adds one new CLI path and one new module. No schema, renderer, Viewer, or existing CLI path changes.
- A real limit, stated plainly: the lifecycle renderer uses fixed bands (5 phase, 3 event, 3 outcome), so **capacity is 11 states**. A larger diagram is rejected with a diagnostic instead of being shipped broken. The importer computes the renderer's exact geometry and scores candidate orthogonal routes. An unplaceable route or guard label becomes an import diagnostic. Imported IR declares `quality_profile: standard`, and `showcase` may need manual routing.
- Failure behavior: every failure exits non-zero with `diagnostics[]` (`code`, `severity`, `subject.line`, `evidence`, `supportedFixes`), and nothing is written. An unknown format or option exits 2.
- Untrusted input: quotes, `<script>`, `</text>`, entity codes, and a `-->` inside a quoted description are inert in the IR and escaped in the artifact. The artifact SVG is re-parsed with `saxes` to prove it. C0 controls, `U+007F`, `U+2028`, `U+2029`, and `U+FEFF` are rejected by name, not silently stripped.
- No unrelated changes. The only edits to `bin/archify.mjs` are the usage line, the `IMPORT_FORMATS` registry, `commandImport`, and one `case 'import'` arm.

## Tests run

- Comparison base: `origin/main` @ `8c3af8a`. Candidate head: `b10bcca`.
- `npm test` from `archify/` on the base: **1337 tests, 1286 pass, 0 fail, 51 skipped**.
- `npm test` on the candidate: **1364 tests, 1313 pass, 0 fail, 51 skipped**. The delta is exactly the 27 new tests in `test/state-import.test.mjs`. The 51 skips are the `ARCHIFY_CHROME` browser tests, identical on base and candidate: skipped, not passed.
- The CLI seam is exercised. Every emitted IR runs through `archify validate lifecycle`. Valid fixtures also assert `composition.summary.warnings === 0`, so a layout regression that only avoids hard errors still fails.
- 15 fixtures: 5 valid, 4 malformed, 6 unsupported or adversarial. There is also one runnable documented example, `archify/examples/release-train.state.mmd`.
- Remote CI has not run yet on this head.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable. This change adds an importer that emits typed JSON IR. It does not change any renderer, the Viewer, or generated artifact layout. Rendering of the emitted IR goes through the existing, unchanged lifecycle renderer, and each valid fixture's IR validates with zero warnings.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip`: rebuilt under Node 22 from the combined source, because `archify/importers/state.mjs` and `archify/importers/README.md` are new packaged files. It was verified by SHA-256 against the committed blob and contains the importer.
- No other generated output changed. The Viewer, templates, examples, gallery, and README showcase stay fresh because none of their inputs changed.

## Notes for review

- **Overlap with #140 (flowchart importer, open) and the Mermaid sequence importer PR (#387).** All three add `archify import`. This PR uses an `IMPORT_FORMATS` registry, so a later importer adds one row. The expected conflict is confined to three hunks in `bin/archify.mjs`. Whichever lands second should also merge the per-format reference docs into one canonical page, as CONTRIBUTING asks.
- `--outcome` goes beyond the minimum in the issue. Without it, the `success` and `failure` legend kinds are reachable only by guessing from state names.
- This adds a new CLI command surface, `archify import <format>`. Happy to adjust the shape if you prefer a different one.

title: perf(template): drop backdrop-blur and filter transitions so viewer stays smooth
body:
## Problem

Delivered HTML artifacts (~840 KB for a 17-node architecture diagram) stutter badly during pan/zoom and when opening modal panels (radar, guide, export menu). Four costs in the viewer repaint the huge SVG every frame:

1. **`backdrop-filter: blur(10–18px)` on 10 panels/modals** — the browser re-samples and re-blurs the entire SVG underneath on every frame; the main cause of freezes when opening modals.
2. **`filter` in 6 `transition` lists** (e.g. `transition: opacity 0.18s ease, filter 0.18s ease`) — animating `drop-shadow` is not composited and repaints the filter per frame on hover/focus/lens.
3. **The scene `svg` was not a compositing layer** — the pan/zoom `transform` triggered full repaints.
4. **A permanent `drop-shadow` on the radar viewport frame** — recomputed on every camera sync.

## Change

Applied in `viewer/template.source.html` (the source of truth since #381), regenerated into `archify/assets/template.html` via `npm run generate:viewer`:

- `backdrop-filter: blur(...)` → `none` in all 10 places; panel backgrounds are already semi-opaque over their own base color, so the visual delta is negligible.
- Remove `filter` from all `transition` lists; hover glow now applies instantly instead of animating a filter per frame.
- Promote the scene canvas to its own compositing layer: `will-change: transform; contain: layout style;` — pan/zoom moves a ready raster, no scene repaint.
- Drop the permanent `drop-shadow` on the radar viewport frame.

## Scope

- The global Viewer visual change is the intended product change of this PR: the stutter is inherent to the shared template, so it cannot be fixed per-diagram. There is no linked issue; scope decision is deferred to the maintainer at review.
- **Regenerated stale artifacts**: `examples/archify-repo.html`, `examples/archify-repo-grid.html`, `examples/maka-architecture.html`, `examples/rag-pipeline.html`, `docs/cases/mco-runtime.architecture.html`, `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html`, `generated/maka-regenerated.workflow.html` (+ its `visual-check` receipt and screenshots). These were stale against the current renderer (last built before #256/#381 and this PR), so rebuilding them from the final template picks up accumulated upstream template behavior (export cleanup, source-evidence links) in addition to the CSS delta. That is required, not unrelated: with a shared template, any stale tracked render contradicts the golden/freshness tests and the claim that no tracked artifact retains blur.
- `generated/maka-regenerated.workflow.visual-check.json` was regenerated with `visual-check` so the receipt sha256 matches the rebuilt artifact (ok=true, containment + readability pass).
- **Rollback/failure**: pure presentation-layer change in the shared template; reverting the single commit restores prior rendering byte-for-byte. No API, schema, or contract change. Not applicable beyond revert.

## Validation evidence (final head `e277148`)

Base is `8c3af8a` (upstream `main`). All local runs below executed on the exact final-head tree; the last amend only added the two regenerated artifacts whose rebuild was verified before the amend.

1. `cd archify && npm test` — **1337 tests: 1290 pass, 0 fail, 47 skipped** (Node-version gates; skipped classification visible in the TAP output). Covers `check:viewer` freshness, golden byte-identity, `check:release-identity`, validators, brand marks, and the checked-in Checkout delta reproducibility test.
2. `ARCHIFY_CHROME=<chrome> node --test test/desktop-reader-browser.test.mjs` (real Chrome 152) — **2 tests: 2 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped**.
3. `node bin/archify.mjs compare architecture ... --quality showcase --json` — 28/28 checks, completeness `complete`; receipt sha256 matches `examples/checkout-platform-delta.receipt.json`.
4. `scripts/build-zip.sh archify.zip` on Node 22 — reproduces committed archive bytes (release-package-gates inside `npm test`).
5. `node bin/archify.mjs visual-check generated/maka-regenerated.workflow.html --json` — ok=true, containment + readability pass on 1440x900/1600x1000/1920x1080/2048x1320, both themes; receipt and screenshots committed.
6. Real-world regression: 17-node architecture diagram re-delivered with the patched skill — `deliver` 9/9 checks; `visual-check` containment + readability pass at all four viewports in both themes.
7. **Upstream CI**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has a `pull_request` trigger, so the matrix (Node 18/20/22/24) and webm-artifact jobs run on this head — see the Checks tab of this PR for `e277148`.

Automated browser evidence: items 2, 5, 6 (receipts). **Perceptual review, reported separately**: the author visually compared panels in both themes at 1440x900/2048x1320 before and after — no readability regression observed; the maintainer's perceptual call is welcome.

## Trade-offs

- Panels lose their blur effect — they were mostly opaque already, so readability is unchanged; exports were never affected (static serialization strips viewer chrome state).
- Glow on hover is instant instead of eased. If the easing is desired, an `opacity`-only transition on a pre-rendered glow layer would be the compositable alternative; happy to iterate.

title: feat: stable identity map — ownership sidecar, archify locate, drilldown bundles
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and behavior

This draft lets an author attach repository-path ownership to diagram components, classify a Git change range against that map, and navigate from an overview into manifest-bound child diagrams. It reports unclaimed and ambiguous paths explicitly. It does not infer runtime impact, recommend review order, or decide whether a PR should merge.

The recovery candidate is `cc1b33a7a02351347842dad4ebe9c13278afc166`, based on main `6db72a9`. The original mixed checkout and index were preserved; all integration was performed in a separate worktree. This PR remains **draft and unmerged**.

## Implementation and compatibility

- Ownership classification keeps explicit exclusions, ambiguous matches and uncovered paths distinct. Empty-segment/brace subset counterexamples, Unicode paths, genuine Git symlink/gitlink entries and divergent endpoint trees have executable regressions.
- Locate validates its receipt and HTML, names missing/invalid map fields with repair suggestions, and preserves earlier outputs on failure. Newly added and renamed maps receive explicit comparison states; comparison failure remains supplemental to the Locate receipt. Import observations remain authored facts, not inferred topology.
- Bundle delivery reuses canonical validation and manifest-bound filenames, including custom sidecars. A moved output directory remains usable after the source is removed. Missing required bundle inputs fail closed; ordinary Locate can omit optional child details while preserving the parent classification.
- Viewer changes are maintained in modular source. Backspace follows the Escape dismissal/return ladder only in active or nested drilldown. Ordinary pages do not register bundle message listeners; a real nested child still handshakes without its own embedded manifest. Offline messaging keeps source-window, role, payload, ID and digest validation.
- Projection state and count badges are removed from export clones without changing live interaction state. The ordinary HTML wrapper changes, so HTML byte identity is not promised; all SVG bytes in the final regenerated examples/cases stayed unchanged.
- README/reference updates document lint ownership semantics, manifest failures and the distinction between requesting descent and a completed child handshake. The named source-string test was replaced with actual receipt assertions. The recovered decision record is historical; six named stale references now use verified fixed-revision symbols.

Broad exclusion presets, a receipt-only output redesign, extra uncovered widgets, an inference engine and automatic PR comments are **not included**. The reasons and original requirement mapping are in the [disposition record](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/cc1b33a7a02351347842dad4ebe9c13278afc166/docs/identity-map-legacy-disposition-2026-09-12.md).

## Validation

- Final handoff contract checks: 44 passed, zero failed/skipped. They include public CLI field failures preserving previous files, import endpoint attribution, optional child ownership and unsupported comparison types.
- Final real-browser message/navigation checks: 6 passed, zero skipped, using Chrome 153.0.8010.36. These cover a genuine cross-origin OOPIF, native Tab leaving the frame, ordinary keyboard behavior, child focus-clear/return, repeated navigation, malformed messages, changed child identity, unsafe URLs with no request, and deletion after parent load.
- Earlier real-browser acceptance also verifies moved-directory child projection after deleting the source and clean SVG export while preserving live state.
- Packaged/development examples, Gallery, Checkout comparison, pinned MCO artifacts and README animation were regenerated. The official Node 22.23.2 ZIP contains 93 entries; only the expected template/examples, Locate CLI and two reference documents changed from the previous archive. `generate-viewer --check`, `actionlint` and diff checks pass.
- Full local tests on product commit `0e38aa9`: 1,489 total, 1,437 passed, zero failed, 52 skipped; tracked source hashes stayed unchanged. The final delta changes only the Motion Governor browser test and repository acceptance prose. Its focused Chrome 153 / Node 22 run passed 9/9 without skips; all hosted CI gates passed on this head in [run 34685055776](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/34685055776), including the complete Viewer interaction and bundle/portable-output/export suites. After `d83f5ce` still failed a real file reload, controlled Linux runs reproduced storage loss from a pre-initialization diagnostic read even in equally large script-free HTML. Without that read, generated Viewers and padded controls retained all twenty reloads per condition. The test removes the interfering diagnostic probe; it retains actual storage-value and Governor-mode assertions on five real file reloads and five same-origin HTTP navigations, plus existing reduced-motion/suspension/storage-error coverage. The [acceptance record](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/cc1b33a7a02351347842dad4ebe9c13278afc166/docs/identity-map-followup-2026-09-12.md#linux-control-identifies-an-interfering-diagnostic-read) links both controlled runs and preserves earlier failures. No product storage workaround or specific Chromium internal mechanism is claimed.

## Recovered evidence and limits

The experiment directories are offline research assets, not shipped Skill code. Most added lines in the recovery packages are fixed JSON observations and inert historical scoring inputs:

- [Fixed boundary replay](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/506d87e/experiments/legacy-replay): 75 observations and six actual CLI runs, including known bad behavior. An independent run produced identical JSON. Six original external map/sidecar files are retained verbatim; the unadopted presets revision is available on an archive branch.
- [First-look recovery](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/506d87e/experiments/legacy-first-look): 30 original answers, 15 static ground truths and 180 independent metric checks. Main-sample P@3 is 0.767 without Locate and 0.700 with it; all-15 P@3 is 0.711 and 0.644. One model, one trial per condition and non-blind experimenter ground truth do not establish human review benefit. Complete prompts and noise labels are not all recoverable.
- [E3 recovery](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/506d87e/experiments/legacy-e3-replay): the 100-step replay matches old JSON byte for byte. Nine commits trigger ten scheduled manual edits; that is not measured maintenance time. The recovered script's 61-anchor selection differs from the report's 67-anchor selection; both are retained, and the recorded report coordinates independently reproduce its complete observations.

No new model or simulated human study was performed. The author's Discussions #368 and #369 were corrected to state these evidence and availability boundaries. Separately reproduced main defects are isolated in #396 (renderer diagnostics), #397 (explicit straight routes) and existing #373 (finite SVG attributes); they are not bundled into this feature. Related nested-reading work #280/#281 is not closed or approved by this PR.

title: feat(viewer): add pointer-anchored wheel zoom
body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

**Since the reviewed head `e03c341`:** the wheel listener no longer calls `preventDefault()` for a gesture the camera does not consume (the blocking finding); the change now lives in the canonical `viewer/` sources on current `dev` with the delivered template regenerated from them; the physical-wheel regression covers page scrolling at the 1x bound, the 3x bound, the excluded navigation overlay and horizontal input, and is registered in the shared browser gate; the delivered template, packaged and golden examples, Gallery, README showcase and canonical ZIP are rebuilt; the visual-evidence note now reports automated browser checks separately from perceptual review, marks perceptual review as skipped for this revision, and lists what was not tested. The zoom captures are re-produced from the current head, with an eight-combination matrix and a pixel-level pointer-anchor check (against a center-anchored control) recorded in the note, and the author's perceptual review of the new captures is recorded there as passed. The author also exercised the wheel path on real hardware, recorded as partial device acceptance.

## Problem and value

The Viewer camera zooms only through `+`/`-`, always from the SVG center, so inspecting a distant region of a large diagram is tedious: the area under the cursor leaves the viewport on every click. This adds pointer-anchored plain wheel zoom on the diagram stage, from 1x to 3x in the existing 0.25 steps, matching common diagram tools.

Intended outcome: inspect any region of a large diagram with one gesture while the content under the pointer stays fixed. The approach reuses the existing camera state machine instead of adding a second transform owner, so it stays proportional to the problem.

Scope:
- `viewer/viewer-camera.js`: `zoom()` accepts a pointer anchor (`clientX`/`clientY`, explicit `anchorX`/`anchorY`) and still defaults to center-anchored zoom for the existing button and caller paths; new `wheel` listener plus `Archify.view.zoomByWheel(event)`.
- `viewer/template.source.html`: `.diagram-container.is-wheel-zooming svg { transition: none; }` so rapid wheel input stays anchored instead of drifting through the 0.18s transform transition.
- `viewer/README.md`: the Camera contract lists `zoomByWheel` and states the ownership rule.
- Deliberately unchanged: button zoom, drag pan, reset, semantic/guided camera, radar, export, print and embed behavior; bounds stay 1x-3x and button zoom stays center-anchored.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: shared behavior. The changed input is the delivered Viewer template that every rendered artifact embeds; callers are the Viewer modules and pages that read `Archify.view`. A plain vertical wheel over the diagram stage now zooms toward the pointer instead of scrolling the page while the camera can still move in that direction.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes: the `Archify.view` interface keeps every existing method and default, and `zoom()` still center-anchors when no anchor is supplied, so button and existing caller behavior is unchanged. No JSON schema, renderer, validator, export, layout or authored-geometry change; no version, tag or distribution identity change.
- Intended interaction tradeoff (explicit): pointer-anchored wheel zoom changes an existing navigation gesture. While the pointer is over the stage and the camera can still move in the wheel's direction, that wheel no longer scrolls the page. The gesture is handed back to native scrolling as soon as the camera cannot respond.
- Failure behavior: `preventDefault()` is called only in the branch that actually zooms. Embed pages, `Ctrl`/`Cmd`, horizontal input, excluded overlay controls, scrollable ancestors and the 1x/3x bounds return without consuming the event, so ordinary page scrolling survives. The axis is classified once from the normalized deltas, and that single result drives both the scrollable-ancestor check and zoom eligibility. The 60-unit accumulator only smooths step size and never decides ownership.
- Rollback path: the listener is isolated inside `Archify.view`; removing `zoomByWheel` and its registration restores the previous behavior without touching renderers or schemas.

## Tests run

Comparison base `dev` `31bfbc8` (merged into the branch). The code evidence below was collected at `4e25478`, Node 22.23.2, real Chromium 131 via `ARCHIFY_CHROME`. The commits after `4e25478` (`b9410d4`, `78cb8a8`, `6de499d`) change documentation and the evidence captures only: `npm run check:viewer` still passes and a rebuilt `archify.zip` is byte-identical, so the code evidence is reused at `4e25478` rather than relabelled to the new head.

- `cd archify && npm test` at `4e25478`: 1653 tests, 1588 pass, 65 skipped (browser suites skip without `ARCHIFY_CHROME`), 0 fail.
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=<chromium> npm run test:browser` at `4e25478`: 226 tests, 226 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped over the shared browser gate suites.
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=<chromium> node --test test/wheel-zoom.test.mjs` at `4e25478`: 3/3 pass. It uses Chrome's trusted CDP mouse-wheel input and asserts: pointer-anchored zoom with the X and Y anchor invariant, the reset identity transform, `Ctrl+wheel` pass-through, page scrolling at the 1x lower bound and at the 3x upper bound, and that the excluded navigation overlay and horizontal input neither zoom nor call `preventDefault()`.
- Coverage gap: no physical trackpad hardware and no OS-level device session; the wheel input is Chrome's trusted CDP input, so trackpad acceleration and platform-specific gesture behavior are not claimed. Browser coverage of unrelated Viewer suites is CI's, and the gate run above is the local equivalent of the same command.

## Visual evidence

- Evidence provided: `docs/wheel-zoom-visual-evidence/` — `before-wheel.png` at 1x and `after-wheel-zoomed.png` at 1.5x after one `-120` wheel event at 34% width and 31% height of the diagram stage. Both captures are re-produced from the current head rather than reused from the earlier revision, and the note reports automated evidence, perceptual review and the untested remainder separately.
- Comparison conditions: workflow `agent-tool-call.workflow.json`, `showcase` quality, 1440x900, dark theme, `data-motion="still"`, page at scrollY 0.
- Automated or browser checks: eight preset x theme x viewport combinations each move 1x to 1.5x toward the pointer with the gesture consumed, and `?embed=1` stays at 1x. The pointer anchor is checked at pixel level — the browser re-renders the pre-zoom crop at 1.5x (`clip.scale`) and matches the post-zoom crop of the same screen region with a mean channel delta of 1.0-2.5 of 255 and at most 2.5% of pixels above 24, against 21.6-22.9 and 15.6-20.6% for a deliberately center-anchored reference. Plus the wheel suite, `npm test` and the shared browser gate at `4e25478`.
- Perceptual visual review: **passed** by the author at `b9410d4` — both captures were inspected and show the diagram correctly magnified about the pointer with no visible defect.
- Device acceptance: **partially exercised** by the author on Windows and Android, both Chrome 151. The laptop (Chrome 151.0.7922.138, trackpad) zoomed in and out, resumed page movement at the 100% bound, kept `Ctrl`+wheel as browser zoom, and still scrolled `Shift`+wheel and the classic wide diagram horizontally; its recorded notches report `deltaY 100` with `deltaMode 0` and no modifiers, and consecutive notches added 1, 2, 2, 1, 2 steps of 0.25 with 0 steps at the 1x bound. On the pre-fix build (`e03c341`) the same laptop left the page at scrollY 0 with the pointer over the diagram at 1x, reproducing the blocking defect on real hardware. The Android phone (Chrome 151.0.7922.173) kept two-finger pinch browser-controlled, so the touch path is unaffected.
- Not tested: trackpad momentum at a bound, Firefox/Safari and other engines, macOS, display scaling, touch-specific viewer behavior on narrow screens, and installed-package hosts; the notch counts above are one wheel's readings rather than a claim about other devices. Device and trial-use acceptance remain separate claims from these browser checks.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated from the final combined source with Node 22.23.2:

- `archify/assets/template.html` — `npm run generate:viewer` (freshness checked by `npm run check:viewer` and `npm test`).
- `archify/examples/*.html` and `examples/*.html` — `node scripts/render-examples.mjs` for the packaged root and `... ../examples` for the golden root, including `examples/web-app.html`.
- `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` and `examples/checkout-platform-delta.receipt.json` — `archify compare architecture ... --quality showcase`. The derivation was confirmed byte-identical to the committed artifact when re-run with the previous template, so the only difference is this revision's template.
- `docs/gallery.html`, `docs/gallery/artifacts/*.html`, `docs/gallery/manifest.json` — `node scripts/build-gallery.mjs docs`.
- `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.gif` and `.json` — `node scripts/build-readme-showcase.mjs`; the receipt pins each scene's source-artifact hash, so it must track the regenerated Gallery artifacts.
- `archify.zip` — `scripts/build-zip.sh`, independently rebuilt and compared byte-for-byte.

Affected outputs left unchanged: standalone showcase pages that embed a Viewer snapshot (`docs/cases/*.html`, `examples/archify-repo.html`, `examples/archify-repo-grid.html`, `examples/maka-architecture.html`, `examples/rag-pipeline.html`, `experiments/mco-showcase/*.html`) follow the existing practice of being refreshed by dedicated showcase commits rather than by every Viewer change; no check requires them and they already carry `dev`'s template without this interaction.

## Checklist

- [x] I used a minimal focused change and preserved existing typed JSON behavior.
- [x] I ran `npm test` in `archify/` at `4e25478`: 1653 tests, 1588 pass, 65 skipped, 0 fail.
- [x] I ran the browser regression gate at `4e25478`: 226 tests, 226 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped over the shared browser gate suites.
- [x] I added a regression test for behavioral changes (`archify/test/wheel-zoom.test.mjs`) and registered it in `scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs`.
- [x] I checked generated artifacts and package freshness when their sources changed.
- [x] I removed secrets, private repository content, and customer data from fixtures and screenshots.

title: Add archify export svg for a standalone, styled SVG
body: ## Revision since the reviewed head (`5d48329`) Refreshed against `dev` at `31bfbc8` (merge commit `18f4e80`; the branch was 279 commits behind). What changed, and which finding each part answers: 1. **Source protection when staging the output** (review item 1) — `a0aa379`. `export-svg.mjs` no longer opens `.tmp-`. It creates a staging directory with `fs.mkdtempSync` beside the target, opens the candidate inside it with `flag: 'wx'`, and renames it into place; cleanup removes only that directory, so a temporary that belongs to another process is left alone. The destination guard (`resolveOutputPath`, the same one `render` uses) and the artifact hash are checked again after the browser has run and immediately before the rename. Regression tests in `test/export-svg.test.mjs`: the reported reproduction (a `result.svg.tmp-` symbolic link to `input.html` planted before the export runs — the artifact's bytes and the planted link both survive, and a plain pre-existing temporary keeps its content), an output path that is a symbolic-link alias of the artifact, a destination that becomes such an alias while the page loads (exit 1, nothing written, the link left as found), and artifact mutation during export (exit 1, nothing written). Against `bin/export-svg.mjs` from `5d48329`, the first and third of these fail; they pass on this head. 2. **`svgDocument()` lives in `viewer/`** (review item 2) — `a0aa379`. `viewer/export.js` owns `Archify.exportMenu.svgDocument()`; `archify/assets/template.html` is generated from it with `npm run generate:viewer`, and `check:viewer` passes. `test/export-browser.test.mjs` asserts the eleven-method interface and `viewer/README.md` lists it. 3. **Non-ASCII text and offline fonts with the current serializer** (review request) — `a0aa379`. A real-browser test renders a fixture with `Ā Ѡ Ж 中文 ắ` in a node sublabel, exports it, and asserts the UTF-8 XML declaration, the literal text in the written file, well-formed XML, no external resource, and the embedded-font contract `test/helpers/offline-fonts.mjs` already applies to the menu export (`assertFontCss`: license text, the six WOFF2 faces by digest and unicode-range, no `local()`). 4. **Load waiter on navigation failure** (CodeRabbit, `visual-check.mjs`) — `a0aa379`. `ChromeVisualBrowser.load()` settles its `Page.loadEventFired` waiter when `Page.navigate` fails, so `close()` no longer turns that failure into an unhandled rejection. `test/visual-check.test.mjs` drives the DevTools pipe with a fake target that answers `Page.navigate` with `errorText` and asserts no `unhandledRejection` after `close()`; without the guard it fails with `Error: visual-check finished`. 5. **Real browser regression in CI** (CodeRabbit, `export-svg.test.mjs`) — `a0aa379`. `export-svg.test.mjs` is added to `scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs`, the Chrome-enabled `test:browser` gate that `ci.yml` and `release.yml` share, as CONTRIBUTING asks for new browser suites. 6. **CLI-level coverage** (CodeRabbit validation-evidence note) — `a0aa379`. `archify export svg` is exercised through `bin/archify.mjs`: the argument guards and the no-Chrome exit 2 (no browser needed), and with Chrome a `--theme dark --json` export (exit 0, receipt fields, output digest, unchanged input bytes, no `prefers-color-scheme` rule) plus the default output path in plain mode. 7. Generated artifacts and `archify.zip` rebuilt from the combined source — `42a329d`, `596a9bd`. CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased. 8. **HTTP(S) blocked while the artifact is open** (CodeRabbit on `596a9bd`, `export-svg.mjs`) — `d396a3b`. `ChromeVisualBrowser.load()` takes an opt-in `blockNetwork` flag that enables CDP `Network` and sets `Network.setBlockedURLs(['http://*', 'https://*'])` before `Page.navigate`; `export svg` passes it, `inspect()` is unchanged. The real-browser regression plants an `` pointing at a local `127.0.0.1` listener, first proves with an unguarded `load()` that the listener is reached (the control), then asserts the export leaves it silent. With the flag flipped off in `export-svg.mjs`, that test fails with the listener recording `/probe`, the fake-browser test that asserts the flag fails with it, and the other fifteen pass. 9. **Changelog theme wording** (CodeRabbit on `596a9bd`, `CHANGELOG.md`) — `d396a3b`. Both resolved themes are stated as the `--theme auto` (default) case; `dark` and `light` lock the SVG to one theme. 10. **Ancestor-replacement limitation documented** (CodeRabbit nitpick) — `d396a3b`. A comment beside the `renameSync` states that a concurrent process replacing an ancestor directory of the target is outside the staging guard: Node has no descriptor-relative rename and the CLI accepts unrestricted output paths, so that case can fail or land under the replacement rather than being prevented. 11. **`archify.zip` rebuilt for the round-two source change** — `2d21bbd`. `d396a3b` changed two packaged files without rebuilding the archive, and CI said so twice: `zip-freshness` and the Node 22 reproducibility test in `release-package-gates.test.mjs` (the one failure in `test (22)`; `test (18)` does not run it). Rebuilt on Node 22; two builds are identical and that test passes against the result, and fails against the stale archive. Scope: the review on `5d48329` recorded that "the existing-HTML export is useful and distinct from #272's JSON delivery path"; this revision adds no contract beyond that. `ChromeVisualBrowser`'s own `writeAtomic()` for receipts and contact sheets keeps the `.tmp-` shape; that is outside this PR and is noted here rather than changed. ## Problem and value `archify/renderers/shared/cli.mjs:161` already states the intent: ```js // Keep the accessible name inside the SVG so it survives standalone SVG // export and embedding. ``` and the viewer already builds that standalone document: `serializeSvg()` in `viewer/export.js` clones the diagram SVG, pulls the SVG-relevant rules out of `document.styleSheets`, resolves the theme variables for both color schemes, embeds the font CSS, and sets `xmlns`. The "Download SVG" menu item consumes it: ```js : format === 'svg' ? Promise.resolve(serializeSvg(1, { autoTheme: true })).then(function (d) { var blob = new Blob([d.svgString], { type: 'image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8' }); recordExportReceipt('svg', blob, d.canonicalStateClean); download(blob, base + '.svg'); }) ``` The only exit from that function is a browser download. title: feat(architecture): allow connections to named boundaries
body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #284. Architecture connections can address optional boundary IDs so relationships attach to visible region/security-group frames without proxy components. This retains the scope agreed in [the maintainer review](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/317#pullrequestreview-5227921604).

Comparison base: `a73a142bd18f6c452440441ff3f5721443347e8e` (`dev`). Candidate: `b512e69003d10527694cd2ea37aea2d243d3a0b7`.

## Changes since 426bc204

- Synced `426bc204` onto current dev, preserving the previous merge resolutions. Upstream did not change the feature's router, title geometry, or shared validation implementation; conflicting validators and ZIP were rebuilt from the combined source
- Addresses [CodeRabbit's diagnostic finding](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/317#discussion_r4293692461): contained-endpoint errors join the existing diagnostics/problems collections instead of throwing immediately. Validation continues for other connections and shared layout checks, then fails through the existing aggregate error path
- The new public-CLI regression demonstrates the loss on the old implementation and verifies that component bounds, contained-endpoint, and edge-through-node diagnostics appear together. Existing diagnostic codes, evidence, repair suggestions, and nonzero exit behavior are preserved
- Beyond the dev sync, the authored product-source change is five added/three removed lines in the architecture renderer, plus one 18-line regression. No new abstraction, shared API, routing algorithm, or release-version change

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, conflict resolution, investigation, tests, review, and description assistance

title: feat(geometry): suggest a verified via elbow for clean-flow routing diagnostics
body:
## Problem and value

`clean-flow/edge-through-node` (an edge crossing an unrelated node) and `clean-flow/endpoint-side-direction` (a route not leaving/entering perpendicular to its authored side) only ever offer generic prose as `supportedFixes` — e.g. *"adjust fromSide/toSide, set route/via or channel coordinates, or move the obstacle."* Solving a correct 2-point `via` elbow for a cross-lane or reverse-flow edge by hand is a well-known, mechanical recipe (leave/enter perpendicular to the authored sides, one shared coordinate strictly between the two lanes) — but it had to be hand-solved and hand-verified per edge, every time, with no help from the tool beyond the generic hint. No existing issue link — found this authoring dense `lifecycle` diagrams with cross-lane transitions.

Scoped narrower than a full fix on purpose: this does **not** address arrow-vs-arrow crossings (`composition/proper-crossing` / `composition/ambiguous-corridor`) — only an edge's relationship to *nodes*, not to other edges. It's also not auto-layout (see Roadmap's "Not planned" — auto-layout is explicitly declined): it only computes a repair for an already-diagnosed violation on an already-authored edge, the same category as the existing `labelAt` suggestion for `layout/constraint`, not a general positioning engine.

## Scope

- What changed: added `suggestClearingVia()` to `renderers/shared/geometry.mjs` — given the two endpoint rects, `fromSide`/`toSide`, and the obstacle set, it samples candidate midpoints for the standard 2-point elbow and returns the first one whose three segments are verified clear of every obstacle (reusing `segmentIntersectsRect`) and that honors both endpoint-side direction contracts (via `routeHonorsEndpointSides`). Wired into `cleanFlowProblems` (active for every renderer, since `obstacles` was already required there) and into `cleanEndpointSideProblems` via a new optional `obstacles` parameter, enabled for the `lifecycle` renderer's transitions.
- What deliberately did not change: the other 4 renderers' `cleanEndpointSideProblems` call sites still don't pass `obstacles` (same one-line change as lifecycle's — left out of this PR to keep it reviewable and scoped to where I could verify the real-world benefit; happy to extend here or in a follow-up, maintainer's call). No change to `composition/proper-crossing`/`ambiguous-corridor`. No auto-layout, no general routing engine.
- No unrelated changes: confirmed — diff is limited to `renderers/shared/geometry.mjs`, `renderers/lifecycle/render-lifecycle.mjs`, and `test/geometry.test.mjs`.

## Stability impact

- Compatibility and migration risk: `cleanFlowProblems`'s signature is unchanged; behavior only changes (message/evidence content) when a verified via is actually found, otherwise falls back to the exact previous generic hint. `cleanEndpointSideProblems` gains one new optional parameter (`obstacles`, default `[]`); omitting it keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte, confirmed by a dedicated backward-compatibility test.
- Renderer, validator, package, or generated-artifact risk: touches a function shared by all 5 renderers' validators (`cleanFlowProblems`), so I specifically re-ran the `architecture` and `workflow` renderers' own test suites (see below) rather than only the new tests.
- Failure behavior and rollback path: `suggestClearingVia` returns `null` (not a guess) whenever it can't verify a candidate — including a real degenerate case I found and fixed during testing (below) — so a failure mode here is "no suggestion," never a wrong one.

## Tests run

From `archify/`:
- `node --test test/geometry.test.mjs` — 60/60 pass (7 new tests: `suggestClearingVia` directly against a real obstacle — verified via `segmentIntersectsRect`/`routeHonorsEndpointSides` on the returned points, not a hardcoded expected coordinate; an unsolvable case correctly returning `null`; a declined mixed-side-combination case; both diagnostics' new message/evidence output; the backward-compatible no-`obstacles` fallback).
- `node --test test/repair-receipt.test.mjs test/workflow-compiler.test.mjs` — 97/97 pass. One existing assertion in `repair-receipt.test.mjs` needed a one-line update: this change legitimately improved that test's own real fixture's diagnostic (a verified via is now suggested instead of the old generic text), so the assertion now accepts either form.
- `node --test test/architecture-delta.test.mjs test/sequence-column-fit.test.mjs` — 24/24 pass.
- `npm test` (full suite): **could not complete** — hangs indefinitely in my sandboxed environment (near-zero CPU for 1.5+ hours; confirmed via process inspection, not legitimate progress). Reproduces identically on unpatched `main`, so this predates and is unrelated to this change. Every targeted file above runs and completes normally and cleanly.

**A real bug caught during testing**: an early version of `suggestClearingVia` could return a degenerate via (two identical points) when source and target anchors shared the same row (horizontal elbow) or column (vertical elbow) — found by running the patch against `repair-receipt.test.mjs`'s own real fixture, not by inspection. Fixed with an explicit guard (`Math.abs(start[crossIndex] - end[crossIndex]) < 1) return null`), commented in place with the derivation.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — diagnostic message/evidence content only; no renderer output, SVG, or viewer change.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip`: **left unchanged.** `scripts/build-zip.sh` requires Node 22 exactly for canonical byte-identical output; my environment runs Node 24.19.0, so rebuilding here would produce non-canonical bytes. Happy to rebuild if useful, or a maintainer can on merge.
- No Gallery/README/guide regeneration needed.

## Checklist

- [x] I used a minimal focused change and preserved existing typed JSON behavior unless the issue requires a contract change.
- [ ] I ran the relevant targeted tests and `npm test` in `archify/`. — targeted tests (geometry, repair-receipt, workflow-compiler, architecture-delta, sequence-column-fit) all pass; `npm test`'s full suite hangs in my environment (pre-existing, see above).
- [x] I added or updated a regression test for behavioral changes.
- [ ] I checked generated artifacts and package freshness when their sources changed. — checked; `archify.zip` needs a Node-22 rebuild I can't produce correctly here.
- [x] I removed secrets, private repository content, and customer data from fixtures and screenshots.

title: feat(viewer): make story and journey autoplay dwell authorable
body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #57.

Both autoplay dwell constants in the delivered viewer were hardcoded at `1100`, and neither was authorable. `storyBeatDwell()` takes the max of that floor and `viewInterval / beatCount`, so for a story of three or more beats the floor always won and every beat got exactly 1.1s regardless of how much content it carries. The only workaround was patching the installed `assets/template.html` and re-delivering every diagram, which does not survive a skill upgrade.

Diagrams can now author playback pacing directly. `meta.motion.dwell` carries optional `storyFollowMinMs`, `journeyStepMs`, and `viewIntervalMs` values (integers, 1100-60000ms) that reach the delivered page as a JSON data block and drive the story and journey schedulers. Authoring nothing keeps today's exact 1100/3200 defaults and byte-identical rendering.

## Scope

- What changed:
  - `meta.motion` added to the shared schema `$defs` and referenced from all five diagram types; standalone validators regenerated.
  - `writeDiagram`/`applyTemplate` emit an optional `archify-motion-data` JSON block; authored-less renders emit no block.
  - The viewer resolves the block once at boot into `Archify.motionConfig`; the guided-story and route-journey schedulers read their timing from it, keeping the readability floor as the fallback.
  - New `autoplay-dwell.test.mjs` regression covering all five renderers (authored, absent, partial, out-of-bounds); three pinned literal assertions rebased onto the authored-default shape.
- What deliberately did not change: the 1100ms/3200ms defaults, the `max(floor, interval/count)` story-dwell formula, camera-settle design, route animation durations, and the schema-v1 typed JSON contract (the addition is optional and additive).
- No unrelated changes: confirmed. Every file in the diff serves the dwell contract or is a regenerated artifact of the template change.

## Stability impact

- Compatibility and migration risk: low. Existing schema-v1 documents validate identically (verified against all five checked-in examples with and without `meta.motion`). Artifacts without `meta.motion` render byte-identically modulo the timing-code region of the embedded template.
- Renderer, validator, package, or generated-artifact risk: standalone validators are regenerated from the schemas (`check:validators` green). A corrupt or hand-edited motion block degrades to the floor defaults instead of killing the viewer boot script (guarded; browser-verified with a literal `null` block).
- Failure behavior and rollback path: out-of-bounds dwell values fail schema validation with a machine-readable diagnostic before delivery. Rollback is a plain revert; no data or format migration is involved.

## Tests run

```
cd archify && npm test
# tests 1030 | pass 1003 | fail 0 | skipped 27 (browser-gated, no ARCHIFY_CHROME in runner)

node --test test/autoplay-dwell.test.mjs
# tests 4 | pass 4 | fail 0

node --test test/story-follow-camera.test.mjs test/route-journey.test.mjs \
  test/guided-views.test.mjs test/story-trail.test.mjs test/story-beat-navigator.test.mjs
# tests 30 | pass 30 | fail 0

node bin/archify.mjs validate architecture <motion-fixture>.json --json   # exit 0
node bin/archify.mjs validate architecture <storyFollowMinMs:10>.json --json
# exit 1 — schema/minimum: /meta/motion/dwell/storyFollowMinMs must be >= 1100
```

`npm test` includes `check:validators`, `test/golden.mjs`, gallery freshness, and the version-sync gates. Browser verification (Chrome, real playback): authored dwell held beat 1/5 past the 1.2s mark and advanced to 2/5 at ~2.2s, matching the authored 2000ms floor; a hand-tampered `null` motion block degraded to the 1100/3200 defaults with the viewer fully alive.

## Visual evidence

Static rendering is unchanged by design (geometry/layout verified byte-identical in the regenerated goldens; zero geometry-touching diff lines). Visual review of the delivered page: passed — diagram, guided-views panel, and playback all render and animate correctly in Chrome with authored, corrupt, and absent motion blocks. No layout or visual regression observed.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated because the viewer template changed (authoritative inputs listed per `CONTRIBUTING.md`):

- `archify/examples/*.html` (5) and `examples/*.html` mirrors (5) + `examples/web-app.html`
- `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` + `.receipt.json`
- `docs/gallery/*` (11 artifacts) + `docs/gallery/manifest.json` + `docs/gallery.html`
- `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.gif` + `.json` (54 frames / 5.4s — visual proof content unchanged, only embedded template bytes)
- `archify.zip` (rebuilt with Node 22, byte-reproducibility gate green)

## Unapplied review findings

Residuals from the pre-ship review (run 20260903-214252-3c7dcf46) that need a maintainer decision; finding #1 (corrupt-block guard) was applied in this PR.

- [ ] P3 — `archify/SKILL.md` — `meta.motion` has no author-facing documentation or changelog entry; add a SKILL.md bullet, schemas/README paragraph, authoring-contract section, and CHANGELOG entry (suggested fix in review).
- [ ] P3 — `archify/test/autoplay-dwell.test.mjs` — runtime wiring is proven only by source-shape regexes; a DOM-shimmed execution probe of the resolver would close the gap a DEFAULTS-mapping typo could slip through.
- Residual (informational): authored `storyFollowMinMs` above the default `viewIntervalMs` lets the floor dominate short chapters — the documented `max()` semantics; a cross-field validation rule is the alternative if that surprise is unwanted.
- Residual (informational): authoring any `meta.motion` lowers the attainable `viewIntervalMs` minimum from 3200 to the shared 1100 floor; worth a line in the contract docs either way.

## Checklist

- [x] I used a minimal focused change and preserved existing typed JSON behavior unless the issue requires a contract change.
- [x] I ran the relevant targeted tests and `npm test` in `archify/`.
- [x] I added or updated a regression test for behavioral changes.
- [x] I checked generated artifacts and package freshness when their sources changed.
- [x] I removed secrets, private repository content, and customer data from fixtures and screenshots.

title: feat(workflow): preserve critical approval details
body:
## Problem and value

Closes #84.

Business approval workflows need initiator, approver, required-deliverable, and rework facts, but representing those facts as cards made otherwise readable artifacts 2158–2254 px tall. This change keeps those facts in one typed source and reveals them progressively from the existing Semantic Passport without changing the overview geometry or first-screen primary path.

## Scope

- What changed:
  - Added an optional nodes[].approval contract with required initiator, approvers, deliverables, and reworkPath fields.
  - Added fail-closed compiler diagnostics for repeated facts and unknown, duplicate, or discontinuous rework edge references.
  - Added a collapsed Approval details section to the focused node's Semantic Passport, Finder indexing for the same facts, localized ARIA/native SVG fallbacks, and output escaping.
  - Marked visual exports as overview-only in the Export menu and layout receipt while retaining complete details in the self-contained HTML artifact.
  - Updated authoring guidance, schema documentation, changelog, regression coverage, generated examples, Gallery proof, README proof, and the canonical ZIP.
- What deliberately did not change:
  - No second permanent panel, duplicated detail cards, inferred approval facts, or detailed static-export format.
  - Ordinary workflows emit no approval metadata or export notice and retain identical diagram geometry.
- No unrelated changes: confirmed. Template-derived artifacts were regenerated because the shared viewer changed.

## Stability impact

- Compatibility and migration risk: additive and opt-in. Existing workflow v1/v2 documents remain valid and preserve their prior geometry and UI density.
- Renderer, validator, package, or generated-artifact risk: the workflow schema and generated validator changed; the shared viewer template required deterministic regeneration of all tracked HTML artifacts and release evidence.
- Failure behavior and rollback path: incomplete or ambiguous approval contracts fail before layout with typed source paths and supported repairs. Authors can remove the optional approval object to recover ordinary behavior; the implementation can be reverted as one commit.

## Tests run

- node archify/scripts/generate-brand-marks.mjs --check — passed.
- node archify/scripts/generate-validators.mjs --check — passed under canonical Node 22.
- node scripts/check-release-identity.mjs — passed.
- node archify/test/golden.mjs — all golden renders, schema enforcement, template freshness, and version checks passed.
- node --test archify/test/workflow-approval-details.test.mjs with real Chrome — 7/7 passed, including geometry equality, validation failures, escaping, Finder, collapsed/expanded Passport behavior, export scope, and first-screen containment.
- Affected cross-suite regression (compiler contracts, v1 compatibility, Semantic Passport, Finder, i18n, XML, Gallery, README evidence, delivery, and render checks) — 234 passed, 1 skipped. Five Windows/toolchain cases did not pass: one Node 22 Windows test-runner process crash and four canonical-package tests that depend on POSIX path conversion or symlink permission. The validator test passed 2/2 under Node 20 and its direct Node 22 freshness check passed.
- Full npm test was run in archify/ to discover stale generated outputs and coupled assertions; every failure related to this change was repaired and rerun in the targeted suites above. The Windows-only harness failures are disclosed rather than reported as green.
- Node 22 canonical ZIP rebuild — 77 files, 1,334,256 bytes, byte-identical SHA-256 to archify.zip.
- node scripts/package-smoke.mjs on the package extracted from that exact rebuilt ZIP — passed on win32.

## Visual evidence

Visual review passed using a temporary approval-workflow artifact in real Chrome.

| --- | --- |

| 1600×1000 | No horizontal or vertical document overflow. |

The Approval details group was also expanded at 1440×900: initiator, both approvers, both required deliverables, and the complete readable rework path remained visible inside the same artifact while document height stayed within the viewport. Light and dark endpoints were inspected. Temporary screenshots were not added to the release package.

## Generated artifacts

Regenerated:

- docs/gallery.html, all 11 Gallery artifacts, and docs/gallery/manifest.json (99 checks).
- examples/checkout-platform-delta.html and its receipt.
- docs/assets/archify-live-proof.gif and its receipt.

title: feat: add standalone SVG delivery
body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #241.

Archify already exports standalone SVG from the Viewer. This adds the same output to the existing verified delivery command, so documentation and CI jobs can generate it directly from typed JSON without running a browser:

```sh
archify deliver architecture spec.json diagram.svg --format svg --theme auto
```

Refreshed against `dev` at `53bc4e19b0d82993609110b865d47178fccd5004`. Candidate: `6dfdc0e6e05473148d6dc3c1a8b1ba19f0a23796`.

Since the [review of `147adb7`](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/272#pullrequestreview-5225081016):

- Delivery and renderer path guards now explicitly require `.svg`, including resolved symlink targets. HTML remains the default; input aliases are still rejected before writing and checked again before commit.
- The Viewer changes now live in `viewer/export.js` and `viewer/template.source.html`. The generated template and dependent artefacts have been rebuilt.
- Both export paths reuse the current embedded WOFF2 bytes and font attribution, and retain the UTF-8 XML declaration. The standalone checker accepts the declaration and embedded font resources.
- Integrated the subsequent sequence-layout, all-type repository-evidence and Spanish-locale changes from `dev`. SVG evidence receipts are covered across all five types; Spanish is included in the pixel matrix.

The follow-up in `6dfdc0e` addresses the remaining validator and handoff findings: external `href`/`src` resources are rejected with either quote style, including whitespace around `=`, and the handoff template now distinguishes HTML browser evidence from SVG receipt fields. Regression tests cover both. The inherited top-level SVG sizing behaviour is tracked separately in #451; this follow-up does not change Viewer layout or export styling.

## Stability impact

Shared behaviour: CLI delivery and Viewer export use one SVG finaliser. No new format framework, runtime dependency or schema change is introduced by this PR.

HTML remains the default, explicit `--format html` matches it, and its receipt shape is unchanged. Rendered HTML script bytes change to embed the shared finaliser; this is not a claim that HTML files remain byte-identical to the base.

SVG retains frozen-input validation, the nine HTML checks, repository-evidence verification and atomic replacement, then adds seven standalone checks. Invalid options, input/output aliases and failed SVG checks preserve the previous output. Raster, card and WebM exports stay in the Viewer; `visual-check` remains HTML-only.

## Tests run

Local checks use Node 22.23.2 and Chromium 153.0.8010.36 on Linux unless noted. Node downloads were checked against the published SHA-256 sums.

- Final head, `npm test`: 1,547 passed, 0 failed, 65 skipped.
- Final head, SVG delivery, artefact-checker, receipt-flush and delivery-contract suites with Chromium: 64/64 passed, no skips. Includes independent SVG comparison against untouched `53bc4e1`, path rejection and packaged failure preservation.
- Final head, Node 18.20.8: all five selected resource-check and handoff-contract tests passed; ten unrelated tests were excluded by the name filter.
- The single-quoted external-resource regression failed before the validator change and passed afterwards. The handoff regression likewise failed on the missing SVG example before the documentation change. Local fragments and permitted embedded images still pass with either quote style.
- Final extracted `archify.zip`, without `node_modules`: Linux package smoke passed. Its public CLI accepted the clean SVG and rejected external `href`/`src` resources with both quote styles. The packaged checker and handoff contract byte-match the source. All 85 archive entries passed `unzip -t`; a second Node 22 build matched the ZIP exactly. `git diff --check` passed.

Viewer/export code is unchanged since `033565e`. The Spanish merge was tested at `3abe10b`: SVG and localisation suites passed 18/18 with Chromium, the Node 18 SVG suite passed 7/7, and the extracted package passed all five modes in all three SVG themes. Those localisation and wider package results are reused, not presented as new-head runs.

The following wider evidence is reused from `033565e`:

- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=/usr/bin/chromium npm run test:browser`: 230 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped. The failure is the atlas test described below; this local run was not a green gate.
- `ARCHIFY_CHROME=/usr/bin/chromium npm run test:webm`: real WebM decoding and SVG/raster/share-card export smoke passed; site-language integration passed 7/7. The additional legacy Passport browser suite passed 7/7.
- Node 18 output paths/types, failure diagnostics, delivery, repository-evidence and SVG suites passed 106/106.

The atlas failure is `atlas navigation must not cover child reading content` at `archify/test/atlas-browser.test.mjs:163`. It reproduced in isolated runs on both untouched `8bc4228` and `033565e` with the same browser. The atlas source and test are unchanged by this PR, the Spanish merge or this follow-up. The paired logs and browser version are preserved as requested by the maintainer. Reproduce from either recorded checkout with:

```sh
cd archify
ARCHIFY_CHROME=/usr/bin/chromium node --test test/atlas-browser.test.mjs
```

Browser coverage is recorded separately above. The unrelated pinned MCO checkout and native Windows-only archive-path check were not available locally.

[Final-head CI on `6dfdc0e`](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/35151698158) passed: the complete Node 18/20/22/24 matrix, browser/WebM gate, Linux/macOS/Windows package smoke, Windows portability, ZIP freshness and published-manifest checks. Pages deployment was correctly skipped for a PR. The local atlas failure did not reproduce in CI; its paired local evidence remains preserved for the maintainer's follow-up.

## Visual evidence

The committed parity test covers eleven fixtures: all five modes, all four presets, brand marks, non-ASCII labels and Spanish. Each compares `auto`, `light` and `dark` output under both system colour schemes, with HTTP(S), cache and local font sources disabled.

Final-head CLI output matches the untouched `dev` Viewer structurally and with zero differing decoded RGBA channels across all 66 comparisons. The candidate-Viewer comparison also passed all 66 at `3abe10b`; that evidence is reused because Viewer/export code is unchanged. Pinned font bytes, coverage and attribution are checked independently. CJK/emoji retain the existing system fallback; pixel equivalence is established in Chromium, not every SVG consumer.

To repeat the independent base comparison, set `ARCHIFY_SVG_BASELINE_ROOT` to an untouched checkout of the base above and run:

```sh
cd archify
ARCHIFY_CHROME=/usr/bin/chromium node --test test/svg-delivery.test.mjs
```

Perceptual review: the contributor accepted the original before/after artefacts; no new human visual sign-off is claimed for this refresh.

## Generated artifacts

title: fix: detect coincident routes in anti-parallel connections with labelAt

## Problem and value

Fixes #248.

Architecture connections can emit identical visible routes, especially for a bidirectional pair. Coincident geometry is not inherently invalid: a shared line can be intentional when labels clearly identify each direction. The problem is possible reader ambiguity, so showcase should warn and preserve author intent rather than reject every shared line.

## Scope

- Detect measured coincident architecture routes at showcase quality, including reversed and same-direction pairs.
- Normalize duplicate and forward-collinear route points before comparison.
- Resolve the effective CLI quality profile and skip connections with unknown endpoints.
- Report stable `composition/coincident-routes` evidence as a warning in the final artifact composition receipt.
- Keep standard quality unchanged and keep hard composition errors blocking delivery.
- Document warning-first authoring guidance; explicit `via`, `channelX`/`channelY`, or endpoint sides remain available when a warning identifies real ambiguity.
- Preserve the validated explicit-via repair and the `labelAt` removal regressions.

## Compatibility and impact

- Showcase delivery succeeds when coincident-route findings are the only composition findings; the receipt reports the warning for author review.
- Actual label clearance, crossing, containment, route rhythm, and other hard composition failures remain blocking.
